If $q=2$, the problem is exactly the family $X_{2p^s}$ resolved above. If $p=2$, giving the ``mirror'' family $X_{2^sq}$ for an odd prime $q$, the problem is genuinely different. Beyond $s=1$, we give a complete resolution for $s=2$, recovering, with an explicit proof and solution sets, the qualitative dichotomy of \cite[Thm.~2.3.1]{SSHS2025}, but the problem remains open for $s\ge3$.

papers.title: Numerical Approximation of Maxwell Transmission Eigenvalue Problem in Dispersive Media via Holomorphic Operator Function
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze a numerical method for the Maxwell's transmission eigenvalue problem in dispersive media. The problem is formulated as the eigenvalue problem of a holomorphic Fredholm operator function of index zero. For discretization, we employ the Nedelec elements. Convergence of the scheme is established via the abstract approximation theory of Karma. To compute the resulting nonlinear matrix eigenvalue problems, we employ a parallel multi-step contour integral method. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the viability and accuracy of the proposed approach.

papers.title: An event is a set, not a number: building the algebra of events before the probability measure in a school progression
papers.abstract: Asked what an event is, pupils often answer with a fraction. This paper argues that school probability should separate two learnings and order them: the algebra of events (random experiment, outcomes, sample space, events as sets of outcomes, the operations not, or, and) and the probability measure, which attaches a number to each event. Before learning to compute the probability of an event, pupils should learn to build, identify and handle the event. The thesis rests on the structure of finite probability, in which the rules are facts about events carried over by an additive function, and on the history of the subject, in which errors such as d'Alembert's two tosses concerned the weighting of outcomes and were resolved by refining events into equally likely outcomes. Five design principles are stated: two objects with two names; the event before its probability; modal judgements (certain, possible, impossible) on sets before numbers; the algebra of events taught as such, with the rules derived from it; the sample space as a modelling choice, with frequencies last, as statistical estimates, and the separation repeated for conditional probability and random variables. They are confronted with the probability chapters, from age 9 to 18, of the French-curriculum courses published at https://commeunjeu.org, with research and other curricula. In primary school events precede probabilities without set notation, which comes at age 12; the lessons apply the principles and prove the rules from events in lower secondary school. But, in the version analysed, events account for 18 to 44 percent of the exercises, proofs are hidden in upper secondary school, and automatically corrected calculations record only the number. It proposes number-free tasks on events for ages 6 to 8 and changes to the International Baccalaureate curriculum. No empirical evaluation is reported; hypotheses are stated.

papers.title: Stability of Multidimensional Linear Discrete Systems
papers.abstract: We study linear multidimensional discrete systems of the form \[ x_α=\sum_{k=1}^m A_kx_{α-e_k}, \qquad α\in\mathbb N^m, \] with uniformly bounded boundary data prescribed on the codimension-one coordinate faces and attractivity understood in the sense of Pringsheim convergence. We first derive an explicit solution representation in terms of sums of ordered matrix products and introduce a shell decomposition whose associated sums satisfy a one-dimensional affine recursion. Our main result is a generalized Fornasini--Marchesini theorem in arbitrary dimension: asymptotic stability is equivalent to the condition \[ ρ\!\left(z_1A_1 + \cdots + z_m A_m \right)<1 \qquad \text{for every } |z_1| = \cdots = |z_m|=1. \] We then study the critical spectral boundary, where the maximal toral spectral radius equals one. We prove that a nonsemisimple unimodular eigenvalue of a toral pencil forces instability, yielding necessary spectral conditions for Lyapunov stability. In the simultaneously diagonalizable case, we obtain a complete classification of asymptotically stable, neutrally stable, and unstable systems in terms of the common eigenvalues. Finally, we show that bounds involving only the individual spectral radii can fail outside this setting: even when all coefficient matrices are nilpotent and their spectral radii sum to zero, a critical system may still be unstable.

papers.title: Endpoint well-posedness for the Boussinesq equation
papers.abstract: We prove small-data global well-posedness for the quadratic good Boussinesq equation on the real line and the circle at the endpoint $H^{-1/2}\times H^{-3/2}$. On each domain, a small invariant spectral set supports a continuous global group, with uniqueness in a fixed local integral class. In the periodic case, both components have zero mean and the flow is Lipschitz on bounded time intervals. The a priori bounds follow from a balanced perturbation determinant for the third-order Lax operator. Averaging two real spectral branches yields coercivity and frequency-tail control. On the line, we construct the endpoint flow by commuting Hamiltonians and Green-field estimates. On the circle, discrete spectral bounds and Kishimoto's endpoint local theory give global well-posedness.

papers.title: Designed short-time observations for rotational damping recovery in Timoshenko beams
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of spatial rotational damping in a clamped Timoshenko beam. The coefficient belongs to a prescribed bounded finite-dimensional family. One fixed spatial average of rotation is recorded in separately labelled experiments with known initial rotational velocities. We construct these velocities so that the leading coefficient-to-data map is an invertible Gram matrix. Testing the equations against the smooth observation kernel gives a uniform parameter-Lipschitz remainder without differentiating the damping coefficient. A weighted temporal moment then yields global injectivity, Lipschitz stability and a globally convergent projected fixed-point reconstruction for sufficiently short observation times. Upper and deterministic two-point lower bounds give the same noise-amplification order $T^{-5/2}$ for $L^2$ time-history errors. A second sensitivity estimate supplies a separate sufficient condition for strong convexity and global projected-gradient convergence. We derive continuous and exact discrete adjoints, prove finite-time convergence of a conforming finite-element midpoint scheme, and propagate forward error into coefficient error. Reproducible synthetic experiments examine symmetry, gradient accuracy, noise and discretization bias.

papers.title: Liouville theorems for the stationary Navier-Stokes equations under partial component conditions
papers.abstract: We prove Liouville theorems for smooth stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes flows in $R^3$ with finite Dirichlet integral and velocity vanishing uniformly at infinity. If the partial components of velocity $(u_1,u_2)$ belong to $L^{4,\infty}$, then we show that $u$ must vanish. The second result only requires that one component $u_1$ belongs to $L^{3/2,\infty}$. The proofs are based on the head-pressure sign and a localized energy identity, combined with different pressure estimates for the two cases.

papers.title: Measure Convergence under Weak Domination for Unitarily Invariant Norms on Finite von Neumann Algebras
papers.abstract: The classical Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem (DCT) is a cornerstone in commutative measure theory, while its extension to the noncommutative setting has remained a longstanding challenge due to the barriers posed by the noncommutative structure. Let \(α\) be a unitarily invariant norm defined on a diffuse tracial von Neumann algebra \((\mathcal{M}, τ)\), let $L^α(\mathcal M, τ)$ be the completion of $\mathcal M$ with respect to the norm $α$(which includes all $L^p(\mathcal M, τ)$ as special cases). In this paper, by replacing ``almost everywhere convergence" with Nelson's convergence in measure, we establish a noncommutative analog of the dominated convergence theorem for $L^α(\mathcal M, τ)$ under a { significantly weaker dominating condition} than those previously considered. For instance, in a \(II_1\) factor \(\mathcal{M}\), if \(P\) is a projection with \(τ(P)=\frac{1}{n}\), then \(n^2 P\) ``dominates" every operator of norm \(\leq n\). As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of center-preserving $*$-automorphism of finite von Neumann algebras, which unifies and extends the earlier works of Kadison and Haagerup on the structure of automorphisms.

papers.title: Combinatorial Insights into Asymptotic Normality
papers.abstract: In this paper we examine various sequences $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of real random variables arising naturally in connection with certain combinatorial structures. The goal is to investigate sufficient conditions for convergence to the standard normal distribution upon centering and normalization. By studying signed binomial sums, Stirling numbers of both kinds, and factorial moments, we obtain certain cancellations in the computation of centred moments $\mathbb{E}[(X_n - \mathbb{E}[X_n])^k]$. This allows us to conclude that $\frac{X_n - \mathbb{E}[X_n]}{\sqrt{Var \ X_n}} \xrightarrow{d} N(0,1)$ when the factorial moments $\mathbb{E}[(X_n)_k]$ are rational functions satisfying some simple conditions on the coefficients. A particular class of such random variables are those whose factorial moments are products and quotients of falling factorials in $n$; we apply our result in this situation and we discuss specific examples arising from block statistics of $k$-divisible non-crossing partitions and from outdegree statistics of rooted plane trees with $k$-divisible outdegrees.

papers.title: The $e$-expansion of integral form Macdonald polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the expansion of the integral form Macdonald polynomials $J_μ(x;q,t)$ in the elementary symmetric function basis. Motivated by the connection between chromatic symmetric functions and LLT polynomials, we conjecture the $e$-positivity of a normalization of $J_μ(x;q,t)$. We verify the conjecture when $μ$ is either a hook or a two-column partition. In the hook case, we express the $e$-coefficients as weighted sums over compositions. In the two-column case, we derive explicit formulas for the $e$-coefficients.

papers.title: Active Flux and Polygons: why a stabilisation and how to implement boundary conditions
papers.abstract: In a recent paper, the authors developed an Active Flux-type algorithm for polygonal meshes (see \cite{BP_Pampa_VEM}). The main difference between Active Flux methods on polygonal meshes and those on Cartesian or simplex meshes is that the basis functions are not explicitly known. These functions describe the solution using point-value approximations on the polygon boundaries and the average value within the polygons. In \cite{BP_Pampa_VEM}, it was shown that directly transposing the algorithm from simplexes to polygons leads to a mild instability, and a remedy was proposed without a rigorous explanation. In the present paper, we clarify this issue and demonstrate that the solution presented in \cite{BP_Pampa_VEM} is indeed correct. Furthermore, another challenge-the implementation of boundary conditions-was previously solved heuristically. Building on \cite{pampa_dg}, we show how to properly implement these boundary conditions. Finally, the method is illustrated through several examples with hybrid meshes.

papers.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
papers.abstract: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $Δ(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $Δ(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.

papers.title: Exceptional times of compact support for $α$-stable superprocesses
papers.abstract: We consider symmetric $α$-stable Dawson--Watanabe superprocesses on $\mathbb R^d$ for every $d\geq1$ and $0<α<2$, started from an arbitrary nonzero finite measure. We prove that, almost surely, the times at which the spatial support is compact and nonempty have Hausdorff dimension one in every nontrivial interval before extinction. We also prove that, almost surely, the times at which the support is contained in any prescribed neighborhood of the extinction point have Hausdorff dimension one in every nontrivial interval ending at extinction. These results extend the corresponding conclusions for $0<α<2/3$ to the full stable range. The key new ingredient is a uniform zero-set theorem of independent interest for Feller branching diffusions started from zero with deterministic continuous cumulative immigration. It shows that sufficiently small total immigration ensures that the zero set on a prescribed open interval has Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to one, with arbitrarily high probability. The estimate is uniform over the immigration profile and allows singular continuous immigration measures.

papers.title: A High-Order Geometric-Compatible DGSEM with Subcell Limiting for the GPR System
papers.abstract: We construct an equation-of-state-independent geometric-compatible finite-volume (GC-FV) method and a high-order nodal discontinuous Galerkin spectral-element extension (GC-DG) for a reduced Godunov-Peshkov-Romenski system on fixed Eulerian meshes. Density is recovered from $ρ=ρ_0\det(\mathbf{A})$, so mass conservation is a hidden companion law of the distortion equation. Starting from a straight-path Dal Maso-LeFloch-Murat fluctuation pair, minimum-change cofactor projections produce a single-valued density flux and exact induced local Lax-Friedrichs dissipation without jump quotients. The summation-by-parts property lifts the geometric two-state identity to high order and yields an equivalent subcell representation of GC-DG. We then blend GC-DG with the compatible GC-FV operator on the same Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto subcells. Because both operators induce the same boundary density flux, the global subcell blend retains the exact semidiscrete mass balance while suppressing shock-generated oscillations. A complementary modal/face-jump indicator supplies the elementwise blending coefficient. Numerical experiments verify high-order convergence, the expected temporal scaling of the fully discrete mass drift, and robust shock capturing for fluid, nonlinear-elastic, thermal-wave, and elastoplastic problems, including genuinely multidimensional configurations.

papers.title: Propagation dynamics of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model in a time-periodic shifting environment
papers.abstract: The current paper is devoted to the study of the propagation dynamics of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model in a shifting environment. We investigate the scenario in which the favorable and unfavorable habitats are spatially separated, with the favorable habitat shifting at a time-periodic speed. We first establish the vanishing, persistence, and spreading properties of solutions with compactly supported and front-like initial data. In particular, we show that if the self-limitation rate of the species is large relative to the chemotactic sensitivity and the species is initially confined to a bounded region, then the species eventually becomes extinct when the habitat shifts rightward with a large average speed. In contrast, when the average shifting speed of the habitat is moderate, the species can persist and spread along the shifting habitat into an increasingly large spatial region. Finally, we establish the existence and nonexistence of time-periodic forced wave solutions whose wave speed coincides with the average shifting speed of the habitat.

papers.title: Linear Hashing Is Poissonesque
papers.abstract: The Poisson approximation theorem states that when $m$ balls are tossed uniformly and randomly into $n$ bins, the distribution of the bin loads can sometimes be approximated by $n$ independent Poisson random variables of mean $m/n$. We show that when the balls are tossed via a random $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear map, the load distribution is still governed by this Poisson distribution, albeit in a (necessarily) weaker manner. This allows us to show that a random linear map behaves like a fully random map in the following ways: 1. $\textbf{Expected loads.}$ We show that the expected value of the $r$th largest bin is governed by the $r$th largest value among $n$ independent Poisson random variables of mean $m/n$. Specializing to the canonical setting of $m=n$ and $r=1$, our bounds show that the expected maximum load when $n$ balls are hashed into $n$ bins by a random $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear map is no more than the corresponding expectation for a fully random map $\textit{plus}$ $\frac{3}2 + o(1)$. Specializing to $m\gg n\log n$, we show that the expected max load is $(1+o(1))m/n$ in this regime. 2. $\textbf{Concentration.}$ When $m\gg n\log (1/ρ)$ balls are tossed into $n$ bins randomly, we expect with $0.99$ probability that $\textit{every}$ density-$ρ$ subset of bins will contain a $(1\pm o(1) )ρ$-fraction of the balls. We show that this remains the case if the $m$ balls are tossed using a random linear map, and our bound matches the $o(1)$-factor produced by the fully random case. This gives a stronger version of the Leftover Hash Lemma for linear maps. An implication of this is that all bins have load $m/n \pm O(\sqrt{(m/n)\log n})$ with probability $0.99$. We obtain these results by showing that the average of a log-potential on the bin loads is upper bounded by the cumulant generating function of a Poisson random variable of mean $m/n$.

papers.title: Floer lasagna modules for some 2-handlebodies
papers.abstract: Morrison, Walker and Wedrich used Khovanov homology to define the skein lasagna module for a 4-manifold with a link in its boundary. The skein lasagna module was shown to be a deep and powerful invariant; in particular, Ren and Willis proved that it detects exotic smooth structures. Still, computing the skein lasagna module outside some carefully chosen grading range remains an important open problem. Motivated by this construction, Chen defined the Floer lasagna module using Heegaard Floer link homology. In this paper, we give a complete, but partially conjectural description of Floer lasagna modules for a class of 4-manifolds obtained by adding 2-handles along plumbed L-space knots (with certain framing constraints). In particular, we prove that for $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ it is infinite-dimensional, and conjecture that for $\mathbb{CP}^2$ it is infinite-dimensional as well. We compute this module for $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ (and conjecturally for $\mathbb{CP}^2$) in all Alexander and Maslov gradings. This strengthens and extends the recent results of McCulloch.

papers.title: Positivity of simplicial volume and uniqueness for the twelve-vertex flag three-spheres
papers.abstract: We study the twelve-vertex flag triangulation $T_{12}$ of $S^3$ and the Davis $4$-manifold $M(T_{12})$ associated with it. We prove that $T_{12}$ is, up to isomorphism, the unique flag triangulation of $S^3$ with twelve vertices in which every edge is contained in a square; this proves Milizia's Conjecture~6.31. We also prove a general criterion for the tangent Euler class of a Davis $4$-manifold to be bounded, and we verify it for $T_{12}$ by means of an explicit symmetric form. Since the Euler class takes the value $256$ on the fundamental class of $M(T_{12})$, the duality between bounded cohomology and simplicial volume gives $\|M(T_{12})\|>0$. This answers Milizia's Question~1.7.

papers.title: Unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in $H^{1/2}(\Bbb T^3)$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) in the scaling-critical class $H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$. Unlike approaches based on the GP-hierarchy or normal form reductions, which typically involve higher-order expansions, our proof works directly with the original cubic NLS, where we also make use of several new a priori Euclidean-like Strichartz estimates. More precisely, we show that every distributional solution in $C_tH_x^{1/2}$ belongs a priori to the class $L^2_{t,\mathrm{loc}}L_x^6$. The key ingredients are a suitable high-low modulation decomposition and the compactness of solution trajectories on bounded time intervals. We also exploit the preservation of the canonical symplectic form under the truncated NLS flow, in order to obtain necessary stability estimates in the rough Sobolev space $H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$.

papers.title: An isometric embedding of the space of non-increasing sequences with non-negative terms into the Gromov-Hausdorff space
papers.abstract: The Gromov-Hausdorff space is a certain metric space induced by the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence, and we study an isometric embedding into this space. While the subspace of non-negative real numbers in the Euclidean space admits an isometric embedding, we prove that the subspace of $\ell^\infty$ consisting of non-increasing sequences with non-negative terms can be isometrically embedded into the Gromov-Hausdorff space.

papers.title: The_Quadratic_Conjecture_and_p-groups_of_maximal_class
papers.abstract: The Quadratic Conjecture for finite p-groups, which is equivalent to the Strong Oliver Conjecture, asserts that if a finite p-group G acts faithfully on an F-module V, then the center Z(G) contains a quadratic element. In this paper, we investigate the structure of maximal class p-groups and establish that they satisfy the Quadratic Conjecture.

papers.title: Resolution quivers and the QF-1 property of higher Auslander Nakayama algebras
papers.abstract: We give a resolution-quiver-theoretic proof of the QF-1 conjecture of Cruz and Marczinzik for higher Auslander Nakayama algebras of positive even global dimension. The proof combines syzygy calculations in Kupisch coordinates, which show that the projective dimensions of quotients of a fixed projective module with cyclic top strictly decrease as their lengths increase, with a torsion-pair argument and Morita's criterion.

papers.title: Rank-one Factored Gradient Descent without Restricted Isometry: Application to Quantum Pure State Tomography on Multi-Qubits
papers.abstract: Factored gradient descent (FGD) is a scalable nonconvex method for low-rank positive semidefinite matrix recovery, in which the rank and positivity constraints are satisfied automatically by the factorization. Most of the existing theory that certifies benignity of its loss landscape, however, relies on a restricted isometry property (RIP) of the measurement map. In quantum state tomography, one of its applications, the measurements that can be acquired with stable statistics are limited by detection efficiency and drift to Pauli observables of low weight; we first show that under such partial-weight Pauli measurements RIP fails in the worst possible way. We then bundle the mutually commuting observables setting by setting, pushing the state forward to the probability distribution of each setting, and introduce a max-sliced total-variation loss. On the stratum where the setting attaining the maximum is unique there is no spurious local minimum, and provided only that the measurement map is injective on generic pure states, the global minimum is the truth up to a phase. Finally we verify these claims numerically on four qubits and compare against FGD with the ordinary loss.

papers.title: Local Reflexivity and Exactness for Reduced $C^*$-Algebras of Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every countable non-exact discrete group $H$ and every nontrivial countable discrete group $K$, the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is not locally reflexive. These provide the first known examples of non-locally reflexive reduced group $C^*$-algebras, settling a longstanding existence question. Moreover, for every nontrivial countable exact discrete group $K$, we establish that local reflexivity of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is equivalent to exactness of $H$, and hence to exactness of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$. This gives a partial affirmative answer to Kirchberg's question of whether local reflexivity implies exactness for $C^*$-algebras. As applications, we construct finitely generated groups with the Haagerup property, as well as finitely generated residually finite groups, whose reduced group $C^*$-algebras are not locally reflexive. In particular, neither the Haagerup property nor coarse embeddability into Hilbert space guarantees local reflexivity of the associated reduced group $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: An efficient coupled block preconditioner for the Marker-and-Cell discretization of the Stokes-Darcy equations
papers.abstract: We consider the iterative solution of the large, sparse and nonsymmetric double saddle-point systems arising from the stationary Stokes-Darcy equations in two dimensions, discretized by the Marker-and- Cell (MAC) finite difference method. Existing block triangular preconditioners rest on approximations of two Schur complements, the second of which is hard to approximate uniformly in the physical parameters. We propose instead a coupled preconditioner that keeps the interface coupling and regularizes the constraint block by a small multiple of the identity, so that the second Schur complement never has to be approximated. We analyze the spectrum of the preconditioned matrix, both in the ideal case and for the inexact version used in computations, and derive from it a rule for scaling the regularization parameter with the physical parameters. Numerical results show mesh-independent convergence of preconditioned GMRES and robustness with respect to the viscosity and the permeability.

papers.title: Sharp $L^p$--$L^q$ bounds for the strong circular maximal operator
papers.abstract: We study $L^p$--$L^q$ boundedness of the strong circular maximal operator $\M$, the maximal function over axis-parallel ellipses centered at the origin whose two semiaxes range independently over $[1,2]$. We prove that $\M$ is bounded from $L^p$ to $L^q$ whenever $(1/p,1/q)$ lies in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(2/7,1/7)$, and $(1/3,1/3)$, the two-parameter analogue of the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(2/5,1/5)$, and $(1/2,1/2)$ obtained by Schlag and Schlag--Sogge for the circular maximal function. The range is sharp up to the boundary; in particular, weak type $(p,q)$ bounds fail for every $p\le3$. The proof is based on a bilinear estimate for frequencies in separated angular sectors, uniform as the sectors approach the coordinate axes. We also prove the analogous sharp result for axis dilations of a translated circle $c+\mathbb S^1$ with fixed $c\ne0$, where the vertex $(2/7,1/7)$ is replaced by $(1/4,1/8)$.

papers.title: Isometric Theory for Greedy-Type Properties with Enlarged Greedy Sums
papers.abstract: For a semi-normalized Markushevich basis, we study isometric almost-greedy inequalities in which a greedy sum of $φ(m)$ terms is compared with coordinate projections onto at most $m$ terms. Here $φ$ is any strictly increasing map of the nonnegative integers into themselves with $φ(0)=0$. We sandwich $φ$-almost greediness with constant $1$ ($φ$-AG$_1$) between two levels of symmetry for largest coefficients (SLC): $$φ\mbox{-SLC}_1\ \Longrightarrow\ φ\mbox{-AG}_1\ \Longrightarrow\ \mbox{weak }φ\mbox{-SLC}_1.$$ Both implications are equivalences if and only if $φ(1)\le2$. We then characterize $φ$-AG$_1$ by the weighted weak $φ$-SLC or a single homogeneous norm inequality, called Property $(F_φ)$.

papers.title: Beyond Deduplication: Sharp Retrieval Limits for Attention with Correlated Distractors
papers.abstract: Redundant context affects attention through two distinct mechanisms: repeated items add normalization mass, while score variation within correlated groups can produce extreme individual scores. We separate these effects in a planted retrieval model with exponentially many Gaussian distractors arranged in known, exponentially large clusters. The model is a two-level generalized random energy model, whose classical free energy yields exact retrieval thresholds. Gaussian interpolation further shows that increasing positive correlation at fixed token count lowers the distractor free energy, unlike adding duplicates. Our main result identifies a sharp limitation of subtracting log cluster size from pre-softmax scores: this correction removes multiplicity but retains within-cluster extremes. Even a temperature chosen after observing all scores cannot lower the required signal below $\sqrt{2α_1}$, where $α_1$ is the exponential rate of the number of clusters. Averaging scores before exponentiation instead suppresses these fluctuations and achieves $\sqrt{2ρα_1}$, where $ρ$ is the within-cluster correlation. The gap persists after adding exponentially many singleton distractors, so group size alone does not identify the target, and extends to fixed finite hierarchies of light-tailed independent-increment scores. Finite-sample, stability, and participation results complement the asymptotic analysis. A controlled retrieval experiment with frozen sentence embeddings supports this distinction while delineating its scope: averaging helps when the relevant item is a singleton, but can discard useful evidence when a relevant group contains multiple matching items.

papers.title: Abelian quotients and orbit sizes for subgroups of linear groups
papers.abstract: Keller and Yang formulated two conjectures relating abelian quotients of subgroups of finite linear groups to largest orbit sizes. After counterexamples were found to the original conjectures, two revised versions were proposed. We prove both revised conjectures for every finite group $G$ satisfying $F(G)=F^*(G)$. We also extend a regular-orbit theorem for nilpotent subgroups to completely reducible modules of mixed characteristic under the same hypothesis.

papers.title: Sheaves on nodal singularities I
papers.abstract: We study two families of moduli spaces of sheaves attached to the node, namely the punctual Hilbert schemes of the non-reduced plane curve $x^uy^v=0$, and the punctual Quot schemes of the module $k[[x]]^u\oplus k[[y]]^v$ over the reduced node $xy=0$. We compute their motivic generating functions for all $u,v$ and over every field. Both are specializations of a single rational function whose numerator counts matrices by rank, and they are related by the substitution $\mathbb{L}\mapsto Q\mathbb{L}$. This proves the Hilb--Quot correspondence for the node with independent ranks on the two branches. The main geometric ingredient is an elementary modification of an ideal along a branch of the curve, whose fibres are affine spaces of dimension equal to a contact length. We also construct stratifications of the Hilbert schemes into products of affine spaces and tori, and we formulate a branchwise Hilb--Quot--HOMFLY conjecture, which we test on the colored Hopf link.

papers.title: A Deterministic Game-Theoretic Approach to Convexity-Preserving Property and Finite-Time Extinction of Level Sets for Geometric Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the convexity-preserving property and finite-time extinction of level sets for quasilinear geometric equations using a game-theoretic approach introduced by Kohn and Serfaty. To construct the game whose value function approximates the viscosity solution, we use the approach introduced by Sato.

papers.title: A Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Biharmonic Dirichlet Control Problems With Patch Reconstruction
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present and analyze an interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for Dirichlet boundary control problems governed by the biharmonic equation, with the control imposed through the normal derivative. The method is based on a reconstructed discontinuous approximation that admits an arbitrarily high-order approximation space with only one unknown per element. We construct a discretization that approximates the state and adjoint state in this space and derive a priori error estimates in the energy and $L^2$ norms. The analysis is carried out under the limited regularity available on polygonal domains by means of a medius argument. Numerical experiments are provided to support the predicted convergence rates.

papers.title: Chern holonomy under the first and second Chern--Ricci flows
papers.abstract: We compare the Chern holonomy of the first and second Chern-Ricci flows on compact complex manifolds. For the first flow, we construct an explicit immortal pluriclosed solution on a complex two-torus with full and restricted holonomy $U(2)$, except at one finite time when both groups are $U(1)^2$; its smooth limit has holonomy $SU(2)$. The solution is uniformly nondegenerate and has bounds of every fixed differential order for all time. In contrast, the second Chern-Ricci flow preserves full and restricted Chern holonomy under the natural unitary identification, including the initial time and nonclosed groups. The proof combines preservation of a connection reduction, positive-time analyticity, and a path-transport comparison. As an application, the optimal minimum mean curvature on a holomorphic bundle is unchanged when metrics are restricted to any realizable full and restricted holonomy class. An explicit projected-curvature source explains the failure of the corresponding Ricci-flow holonomy argument.

papers.title: A Two-Grid Finite Element Method for the Nonlinear Poisson-Boltzmann Equation Based on a Solution Decomposition
papers.abstract: The nonlinear Poisson--Boltzmann equation (PBE) is a widely used implicit-solvent model for the electrostatics of biomolecules in ionic solvent. Its numerical solution is complicated by the point charges, the dielectric jump across the molecular surface, and the exponential nonlinearity. We study a two-grid finite element method for the PBE built on the solution decomposition $u=G+Ψ+\Phit$ of Xie [J.~Comput.~Phys.~275 (2014) 294--309], in which $G$ carries the singularities analytically, $Ψ$ solves a linear interface problem, and $\Phit$ solves a semilinear interface problem for an arbitrary number of ionic species. The nonlinear problem for $\Phit$ is solved on a coarse mesh only, followed by a single Newton correction on the fine mesh, so that only symmetric positive definite linear systems are solved on the fine mesh. The analysis uses a $C^2$ truncation of the exponential that grows quadratically beyond a level $τ$; for $τ$ above an explicit bound the truncated problem has the same solution as the original one, and no discrete maximum principle or mesh-angle condition is needed. Under standard piecewise regularity assumptions we prove quasi-optimal energy and $L^2$ estimates and an $L^4$ estimate for the finite element approximation of $\Phit$, and for the two-grid solution we prove $\enorm{u-\utg}\le C\big(h^{s-1}+H^{2(s-1)+t/2}\big)$ in three dimensions, where $t=\min\{s,σ\}-1$. Whenever the dual problem is at least as regular as the primal one ($σ\ge s$), the coarse mesh can be chosen as $H\sim h^{2/5}$ without loss of accuracy. A manufactured-solution test confirms the predicted rates and the quadratic dependence of the two-grid correction on the coarse error.

papers.title: Stability functions inducing stability data
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study when a stability data on an abelian length category is induced by a stability function. We give an intrinsic characterization of such stability data. For at most six phases, an inducing function exists if and only if every semistable subcategory is wide. An example with seven phases shows that this bound is sharp. For finite phase sets and finite rank, an inducing function exists if and only if an inducing red path exists. We also give a maximal green sequence of length eleven in type $D_4$ that no stability function induces. This disproves the red-path conjecture of Brüstle--Smith--Treffinger.

papers.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp dimensional dependence of the asymptotic approximation error for the Euclidean unit ball $B_2^d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ by polytopes with a prescribed number of vertices in the relative symmetric difference metric. Specifically, we prove that $$\lim_{N\to\infty}N^{2/(d-1)}\inf_{P\in P_d(N)}\frac{\operatorname{vol}_d(P\triangle B_2^d)}{\operatorname{vol}_d(B_2^d)}=Θ(d^{-1/2}),$$ where $P_d(N)$ consists of polytopes with at most $N$ vertices and no containment restriction. Equivalently, the classical Laguerre-Delone triangulation numbers satisfy $\operatorname{ldel}_{d-1}=Θ(d^{-1/2})$. This improves the lower bound $Ω(d^{-1})$ of Böröczky (2000) and the upper bound $O(1)$ of Ludwig, Schütt and Werner (2006). In contrast, the corresponding asymptotic coefficient for approximation with a prescribed number of facets has order one, as shown by Kur (2020). We also establish non-asymptotic bounds showing that, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, the ball admits an $\varepsilon$-approximation with at most $\exp(C(\varepsilon)\sqrt d)$ vertices, whereas approximating the hypercube to the same accuracy requires at least $\exp(c(\varepsilon)d)$ vertices. Consequently, the ball does not maximize the optimal relative approximation error among convex bodies, even up to an absolute multiplicative constant at the same vertex budget. Thus Macbeath's theorem (1951) on the extremality of the ball for inscribed approximation does not extend to polytopes in arbitrary position.

papers.title: The Turán number of Berge paths in connected hypergraphs
papers.abstract: A Berge path in a hypergraph is an alternating sequence of distinct vertices and edges $v_1,e_1, v_2, \ldots, e_{k-1}, v_{k}$ such that $v_i, v_{i+1} \in e_i$ for all $i \in [k-1]$. Győri, Katona, and Lemons determined the maximum number of edges in $r$-uniform, $n$-vertex hypergraphs without Berge paths on $k$ vertices. The extremal examples for their bounds are disconnected hypergraphs in which each component has either too few edges or too few vertices to contain such a Berge path. We consider the setting in which the host hypergraph is connected. Let $\operatorname{ex}^{\mathrm{conn}}_r(n,\mathcal{BP}_k)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex, $r$-uniform, connected hypergraph that does not contain a Berge path on $k$ vertices. This number was determined by Zhang, Broersma, Győri, Tompkins, Wang for $k \leq r+2$, and Zhao, Gerbner, Zhou for $k \geq 2r+2$. In this paper, we resolved the remaining cases $r+3 \leq k \leq 2r+1$ when $n$ is sufficiently large, confirming a conjecture of Zhang, et al.

papers.title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
papers.abstract: Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures satisfying Pesin's entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms whose attractors admit extendable continuous invariant splittings. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. For $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with strictly separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. We also construct examples with hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.

papers.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
papers.abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid 3.12.12, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid 4.8.8, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid 3.6.3.6, the elongated triangular grid $3^3.4^2$ and the snub hexagonal grid $3^4.6$. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid 4.6.12, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid 3.4.6.4, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid $3^2.4.3.4$.

papers.title: Pinned configuration sets and slicing theorems via Fourier integral operators
papers.abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_X}$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_Y}$ be open, where $d_X,d_Y\geq2$ and $1\leq p\leq\min\{d_X,d_Y\}$. Let $Φ:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^p$ be a smooth mapping, and suppose that $D_xΦ$ and $D_yΦ$ have rank $p$. For compact sets $A\subset X$ and $B\subset Y$, we give lower bounds on $\dim_H A+\dim_H B$ ensuring that the pinned configuration set \[Δ_Φ^y(A)=\{Φ(x,y):x\in A\}\] has positive Lebesgue measure or nonempty interior for some $y\in B$. The dimensional thresholds are expressed in terms of uniform $L^2$-Sobolev estimates for the generalized Radon transforms associated with $Φ$. Our results extend the Fourier integral operator approach developed by Greenleaf, Iosevich, and Taylor for unpinned $2$-point configuration problems to the pinned setting. We also prove a nonlinear projection theorem that remains valid even when the Peres-Schlag transversality condition fails. Under the smoothing hypotheses used for the pinned configuration theorem, we obtain lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimensions of the corresponding slices of $A$ by the level sets of $Φ$. Applications include distances from points to hyperplanes, spheres and lines; multiparameter distance sets; and a restricted projection family introduced by Harris.

papers.title: Leafrians, Frobenius splittings, and moduli spaces over Poisson surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Poisson surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, and let $s\in H^0(X,ω_X^{-1})$ be nonzero. We construct an anticanonical section associated to $s$, called the leafrian, on moduli spaces $M$ of stable objects on $X$, including the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons. The leafrian splits $M$ if and only if $s^{p-1}$ Frobenius splits the base. It is invariant under the Hamiltonian flows of Bottacin's Poisson structure on $M$, so every compatibly split subvariety of $M$ is a Poisson subvariety. Furthermore, the leafrian extends to an anticanonical section on the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$, and splits $\bar M$ under the same criterion. As a consequence, for $X$ a rational surface, a ruled surface over an elliptic curve, a $K3$ surface, or an abelian surface, and $ρ>0$, the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$ satisfies Kodaira-type cohomology vanishing, including singular $\bar M$, and the same holds in characteristic zero.

papers.title: On Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of non-flat Lorentzian manifolds, called Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds (briefly, LTFSMs). This class contains Lorentzian concircular structure manifolds (briefly, LCSMs), LSP-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds with coefficient $α$, LP-$α$-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds, and LP-$α$-Kenmotsu manifolds. The interrelations among these various classes of manifolds are illustrated in Figures 1 and 2. We investigate several geometric properties of LTFSMs. In particular, we show that the expansion scalar, given by the divergence of $ξ$, is nonzero and nonconstant, and that the flow of $ξ$ is irrotational. In an LCSM, the Ricci operator commutes with the structure tensor $φ$ [12]. However, it is shown that, in an LTFSM, the Ricci operator does not generally commute with $φ$. If the gradient of the torse-forming scalar $α$ is collinear with the torse-forming vector field $ξ$, then the Ricci operator commutes with $φ$, and the manifold reduces to an LCSM. It is known that a conformally flat LCSM is quasi-Einstein and hence is a manifold of quasi-constant curvature. We show that a conformally flat LTFSM is a generalized quasi-Einstein manifold in the sense of Chaki [1] and is also a manifold of generalized quasi-constant curvature. Several curvature-related properties of LTFSMs are established, and their sectional curvature is determined. The existence of LTFSMs is demonstrated through several proper nontrivial examples. We also present examples that are simultaneously LCSMs and LTFSMs, examples of LTFMs characterizing twisted cubic spacetimes, and generalized Robertson-Walker (GRW) spacetimes characterizing LCSMs. Finally, we provide examples of LTFSMs in which the vector field $ξ$ is a unit timelike torse-forming vector field but is not concircular; see Examples 5.6--5.8.

papers.title: A sharp bound on the binding number of $K_k$-free graphs and the Brandt conjecture
papers.abstract: The binding number of a graph is the smallest ratio $|N(S)|/|S|$ among all nonempty vertex sets $S$ whose neighborhood $N(S)$ is not the whole vertex set. We prove that every finite nonempty $K_k$-free graph has binding number at most $k-2$ for every $k\ge6$, confirming Brandt's conjecture; the bound is sharp for complete $(k-1)$-partite graphs with equal nonempty parts. We first prove the case $k=6$ and then extend it to all $k\ge6$ by induction.

papers.title: Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.

papers.title: Quasirandomness from balanced and repeated subgraph counts
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a graph on $m$ vertices with at least one edge, and let $0<p\le1$. We study when prescribed subgraph counts across disjoint vertex classes characterize $p$-quasirandom graph sequences. For positive multiplicities $\bm=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$ summing to $m$ and positive class proportions $\balpha=(α_1,\ldots,α_r)$ with total at most one, we first classify symmetrized repeated-class counts for $r\ge3$: when $0<p<1$, they are forcing precisely if $e(F)>1$ or $\balpha\ne\bm/m$. We also obtain a complete classification of labelled transversal counts: for \rev{$0<p<1$, the only nonforcing profile is $F=K_2$ with class proportions $(1/2,1/2)$.} Together, these results settle conjectures of Janson and Sós [European J. Combin. 46 (2015)], Hatami, Hatami and Li [European J. Combin. 56 (2016)], and Janson [arXiv:2606.20186v1 (2026)]. The common ingredient is a balanced-count theorem for every graph with more than one edge, proved through a degree-sequence inequality, and its consequence of additive rigidity. Our arguments also determine the bad indices of the associated functional nullspaces and isolate the exceptional single-edge profiles. In particular, a non-divisibility theorem for grouped elementary symmetric polynomials excludes the higher-order obstructions in the repeated-class setting. In contrast, for two repeated classes and every $p\in(0,1)$, we construct nonquasirandom graph sequences satisfying the crossing-triangle counts at proportions $(1/3,2/3)$, with limiting edge density strictly below $p$. These counterexamples answer the crossing-triangle question negatively and show why the three-class assumption cannot be omitted.

papers.title: Isolated zeros of the Riemann zeta function and zeros of linear combinations of Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: Let $0<γ_1\leq γ_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity, and fix $c>0$. We say that a non-trivial zero $ρ_n=β_n+iγ_n$ is $c$-isolated if $\min(γ_{n+1}-γ_n, γ_n-γ_{n-1})>2πc/\log γ_n$. Note that any isolated zero is necessarily simple and on the critical line. We prove unconditionally that there exists a positive constant $c>0$ such that at least $13/20$ of the zeta zeros are $c$-isolated. Moreover, we can show that this proportion is more than $1/2$ when $c=1/6$. Previously, it was not known unconditionally that there are infinitely many isolated zeros. We also show that there are positive proportions of $k$ consecutive ``moderate'' gaps (gaps larger than a constant times the average local gap) between the ordinates of the zeta zeros, for $k=3, 4, 5$. As an application we combine our work on isolated zeros (which we extend to Dirichlet $L$-functions) with an unconditional refinement of the Bombieri--Hejhal method to show unconditionally that at least $31\%$ of the zeros of a linear combination of two distinct primitive Dirichlet $L$-functions with the same conductor and parity lie on the critical line and have odd multiplicity. The previous unconditional record for this proportion was $7.38\times 10^{-9}$, which was obtained by Dousselin who refined and made explicit a result of Selberg.

papers.title: The sum-product conjecture holds for fixed-field lattice product constructions
papers.abstract: We study fixed-field analogues of the lattice product construction recently used by Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov to disprove the sum-product conjecture over the real numbers. These sets are of the form $A_n = P_nG_n \subset F$, where $F$ is a fixed number field, $P_n$ can be rescaled to a set of algebraic integers whose conjugates are polynomially bounded in $|P_n \setminus \{0\}|$, and $G_n$ occupies a positive proportion of a bounded box of scale $Y_n$ in a fixed positive-rank multiplicative lattice. We prove that these fixed-field constructions satisfy the sum-product conjecture, $\max\{|A_n+A_n|, |A_nA_n|\} \ge |A_n|^{2-o(1)}$ as $|A_n| \to \infty$, with no restriction on the relative growth of the two factors. More strongly, any fixed power saving in the product set forces an asymptotically maximal sumset: there exists $C > 0$ such that, for each fixed $δ\in (0,1]$, if $|A_nA_n| \le |A_n|^{2-δ}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then $Y_n \to \infty$ and $|A_n+A_n|/|A_n|^2 = 1/2 + O_δ((\log Y_n)^C/Y_n)$. In particular, the additive-box times unit-box construction of Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov cannot produce sum-product counterexamples in any fixed totally real number field, at any relative scales. The proof combines a bound for factorizations of algebraic integers with a more general maximal-sumset theorem for coefficient sets whose nonzero-element ratios have small Weil height. The latter controls multiplication fibers and combines a lattice strip estimate with logarithmic separation derived from the theorems of Yu and Matveev.

papers.title: A fast Laguerre--Fourier spectral method for the polyatomic Boltzmann collision operator with continuous internal energy
papers.abstract: The polyatomic Boltzmann equation extends the classical kinetic description to gases whose molecules possess internal energy in addition to their translational motion. The distribution function then has one more variable than in the monatomic case, and the collision operator becomes an eight-fold integral whose evaluation dominates the cost of solving the equation. In this work, we propose a fast Laguerre--Fourier spectral method for the polyatomic Boltzmann equation with continuous internal energy, which evaluates the collision operator in $O(K^2MN^4\log N + K^3MN^4)$ online operations after a solution-independent precomputation, where $N$ is the number of Fourier modes in each velocity direction, $K$ is the number of Laguerre modes and $M$ is the number of quadrature points on the sphere. Specifically, the distribution function is expanded in generalized Laguerre functions in the internal energy and in Fourier modes in velocity. A sequence of changes of variables then separates the internal-energy integrals from the velocity convolutions, so that the former no longer involve the distribution function and are computed once and stored. Numerical experiments are presented for both the spatially homogeneous and the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation. They confirm the spectral accuracy of the proposed method and its agreement with the direct simulation Monte Carlo method.

papers.title: Optimal Priors for Betting Tests with Bounded Payoffs: An Exact Expected-Time Characterization
papers.abstract: Testing by betting is a powerful framework that recasts hypothesis testing as a betting game. A popular approach spreads the initial wealth over fixed bets according to a prior distribution, using a universal portfolio algorithm. For suitable priors, this approach achieves the optimal expected rejection time as the error probability goes to zero at a fixed alternative. Yet, priors with this guarantee can behave quite differently near the null. This motivates the question: Which prior should we use in testing-by-betting algorithms? We study bounded scalar payoffs and, under technical conditions, prove a sharp formula for expected rejection time, uniform over all bounded alternatives as the error probability tends to zero. The formula shows how the prior's mass around the zero bet determines the cost of adapting to an unknown alternative. We characterize the priors that attain the best possible leading constant when the error probability and alternative vary together. We also show that no valid test can uniformly improve on this cost across ranges of alternatives near the null. In particular, the uniform prior can require arbitrarily more observations than suitable priors that concentrate around the zero bet. A general inversion argument converts our results into sharp expected times to reach a prescribed confidence-sequence width. We also give a concrete prior choice and an FFT-based algorithm with almost linear computational complexity.

papers.title: Free boundary regularity for the porous medium equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we resolve the local cone conjecture proposed by Kienzler, Koch, and Vázquez concerning the free-boundary regularity of the porous medium equation. We prove that the local cone condition guarantees the smoothness of the free boundary lying outside the initial support. The proof relies on new gradient estimates obtained through maximum principle arguments and comparison principles. As an application, we establish the global-in-time smoothness of the free boundary for solutions with convex initial support under standard assumptions on the initial data.

papers.title: Structural stability of cylindrical transonic shocks to the three-dimensional Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring combustion equations
papers.abstract: We address the structural stability of transonic shock solutions to the Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring (ZND) combustion equations in a cylindrical domain under three-dimensional perturbations of the incoming supersonic flow and exit pressure. The perturbed transonic shock is completely free and its strength and position are uniquely determined by the incoming flow and the exit pressure. The solution shares the same regularity for the velocity, the pressure, the entropy and the fraction of unburned gas. The main difficulties are that the shock front is a free boundary to be determined simultaneously with the subsonic flow and the equations for all states are coupled with each other due to the combustion process. One of the key ingredients of the analysis is to reformulate the three-dimensional ZND combustion equations into a deformation-curl system and four transport equations in terms of the deformation tensor and vorticity. Another one is an elaborate decomposition of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions so that the shock front is uniquely determined by an algebraic equation and an unusual second order differential boundary condition is obtained on the shock front for the first order nonlocal deformation-curl system, from which an oblique boundary condition can be derived after homogenizing the curl system and introducing the potential function.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Common Spanning Forests under Color Refinement
papers.abstract: We study the common spanning structure of connected finite simple graphs that are indistinguishable by uniformly initialized color refinement. We prove that any two such graphs with common cyclomatic number $r\ge2$ contain isomorphic spanning forests with at most $r-1$ components. This bound depends only on $r$ and is sharp for every $r\ge2$, even when both graphs have maximum degree at most three. We also determine the maximum, over all such graph pairs without restricting their order, of the minimum edge symmetric difference under vertex bijections: it is exactly $4(r-1)$.

papers.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
papers.abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $Γ$ satisfies $\exp(Γ) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.

papers.title: Mixed moment and joint non-vanishing of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(1)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(1)$ $L$-functions
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the mixed-moment problem for the product of central values of two $L$-functions twisted by a Dirichlet character of large conductor $q$. Precisely, for a fixed $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ Hecke-Maass cusp form $π$, we asymptotically evaluate the first moment, with $\textit{power-saving}$ error term for the product of central $L$-values $L(1/2, π\timesχ)\overline{L(1/2, χ)}$ averaged over the $\textit{full family}$ $\{χ\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{q}): Q\leq q\leq 2Q\}$ of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$. And as a consequence, we also established the simultaneous non-vanishing of the aforementioned central $L$-values.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness Proof for the Transport Equation and the Orthogonal Dynamics Equation for Zwanzig's Projection on Gaussian Spaces: A Vanishing Viscosity Method
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of unique solutions ${u\in H^1(0,T;L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))}$ of the transport equation $u_t=F\cdot\nabla u+f$ and the orthogonal dynamics equation ${u_t= Q_\text{Z} (F\cdot\nabla) Q_\text{Z} u+f}$, where $F$ is a time-independent vector field, $f$ is a forcing term, $P_\text{Z}=1-Q_\text{Z}$ is a Zwanzig projection (conditional expectation) on $L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n)$ defined by $P_\text{Z}h \propto \int h(\cdot ,y) ρ(\cdot,y)\rm{d}y$, and $γ$ is the standard Gaussian measure with density $ρ$. To this end, we develop a vanishing viscosity method based on the maximal regularity theory for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator on $L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The following assumptions guarantee the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions: ${f\in H^1(0,T;L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))}$, ${g\in H^1_γ(\mathbb{R}^n)}$, $F\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $\rm{ess\,sup}_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(x\cdot F-\rm{div}F\right) < \infty$, where $g$ denotes the initial value function.

papers.title: The algebraic theory of non-archimedean intertwining periods
papers.abstract: We develop an algebraic theory of local intertwining periods for symmetric pairs $(G,H,θ)$ over non-archimedean local fields $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and finite-length representations of Levi subgroups of $G$ with coefficients in an algebraically closed field $R$ of characteristic different from the residual characteristic of $F$. For open orbits this algebraic version is essentially contained in the work of Blanc and Delorme. The theory relies on a crucial new uniqueness result, extending a result of Blanc and Delorme for open periods, which asserts that an admissible intertwining period is the only $H$-equivariant linear form extending the corresponding integral on the space of well-supported sections. In the group case it recovers at once the results of Dat on algebraic intertwining operators. Our algebraic construction does not require the unimodularity hypothesis imposed in the work of Matringe--Offen--Yang. When $R=\mathbb{C}$, we also remove this assumption in the classical non-archimedean analytic setting, and prove convergence of intertwining periods for all symmetric spaces. At the same time we extend the context of the whole theory in the following manner: we allow $F$ to be of positive odd characteristic, we allow twisting characters in the periods, and we allow $H$ to lie between $(\mathbb{G}^θ)^\circ(F)$ and $G^θ$. Finally, in the algebraic setting, we obtain explicit polynomial bounds for the singularities of intertwining periods, and compute them in a concrete case.

papers.title: A recurrence in logarithmic Möbius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler--Maclaurin
papers.abstract: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted Möbius sums by combining Möbius inversion with the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also study the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, establishing that they never change sign.

papers.title: Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
papers.abstract: We study the rough differential equation $$ \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) ζ_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d, $$ where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $ζ$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{α-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $α\in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Prömel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $ζ= dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.

papers.title: Poisson occupancy of paths on permuted regular graphs
papers.abstract: In the classical occupancy problem, $B$ balls are placed independently and uniformly into $d$ boxes. We study a graph analogue of this model. Let $G$ be a directed $r$-regular graph on $d$ vertices and fix a vertex $i$. Consider all paths of length $L$ starting from $i$, and let $N_L(i,j)$ denote the number of such paths ending at a vertex $j$. Thus the vertices play the role of boxes and the $r^L$ paths play the role of balls. In general, these occupancies depend strongly on the geometry of $G$. We show that inserting independent uniform permutations between successive layers restores the classical Poisson behavior at the empirical level. Although the path endpoints remain strongly dependent, their empirical occupancy distribution has the same limiting Poisson law as independent balls thrown into boxes. More precisely, at the critical scale $r^L/d\toλ\in(0,\infty)$, provided $rL/d \to 0$, the empirical path multiplicity distribution converges in Wasserstein distance to $\operatorname{Pois}(λ)$, independently of the geometry of the underlying graphs. We also prove a local Poisson limit theorem and a Berry-Esseen bound for the empirical distribution functions. These estimates determine the full total-variation transition of the normalized path multiplicities toward uniformity. For arbitrary doubly stochastic kernels, we further establish exact covariance and Frobenius norm identities, together with an exact contraction formula for the chi-square divergence. As applications, we study synchronous opinion averaging, obtaining an explicit cutoff profile for equal-size groups and quantitative convergence to consensus for heterogeneous group sizes.

papers.title: Dynamical Lie Algebras for Fixed-Gate Quantum Ansätze
papers.abstract: Parameterized Quantum Circuits have emerged as a central framework for variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ regime, with major applications in quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and, more recently, quantum machine learning (QML). By developing a new approach for computing dynamical Lie algebras associated with quantum circuits combining parametrized gates and non-parametrized entangling gates, we aim to extend the applicability of recent algebraic results to architectures that are actually used in quantum machine learning.

papers.title: Intersecting a curve in an abelian variety with multiples of another curve
papers.abstract: Levin asked what can be said about the locus of points lying on a given curve in $\mathbb{G}_m^n$ that have a non-zero integer power on another given curve in $\mathbb{G}_m^n$ for $n \geq 3$. We give a definite answer to the abelian analog of Levin's question, proving what is predicted by the Zilber-Pink conjecture in this case. An important ingredient in our proof is a strengthening of a height inequality by Vojta and Rémond.

papers.title: A deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Bilu--Linial signing problem on bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Bilu--Linial signing problem on bipartite graphs. For every finite simple bipartite graph of maximum degree at most an integer $Δ\ge3$, the algorithm assigns signs to its edges so that the signed adjacency matrix has operator norm strictly less than $2\sqrt{Δ-1}$. Our algorithm builds on the randomized recursive repair framework of Jadbabaie, Saberi, and Sra~\cite{JSS26}, with deterministic rules for sign selection and vertex deletion.

papers.title: Backward stochastic partial differential equations with unbounded random coefficients
papers.abstract: We study a linear backward stochastic partial differential equation with unbounded observation-adapted random coefficients, motivated by the duality approach to nonlinear filtering. The coefficients depend predictably on the observation history through a control with almost surely finite time-integrated squared norm. The drift, diffusion, and coefficient multiplying the martingale integrand may grow linearly in space. The diffusion matrix may grow quadratically in space and is allowed to be degenerate. Under bounded positive-order spatial derivatives and bounded smooth observation-measurable terminal data, we prove existence and uniqueness in a polynomially weighted Sobolev class up to control-energy stopping times. The proof combines conditional parameter estimates, entropy bounds for likelihoods, stability under the reference probability, and stochastic-flow reconstruction.

papers.title: Occupation counts of rarely switching Markov chains: stratified local laws, support selection and the boundary layer
papers.abstract: A Markov chain with exit rates $q_i$ runs for $N$ steps with transition matrix $I+(T/N)Q$. On each irreducible face that carries start mass, we prove a local limit theorem for the occupation counts with an explicit constant and relative error $O(1/T)$, uniformly for $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$ with $\varepsilon\max_iq_i<1$ and on compact subsets of the open face. Up to $O(1)$, minus the log-probability of counts $n$ with support $F$ is $|F|-1$ times $\log(N/\sqrt T)$ plus $N$ times the Donsker and Varadhan functional of $I+(T/N)Q$ at $n/N$. Every admissible face has an explicit power of $T$ in its largest probability for large $T\le N^{1/3}$, and a constant given by a finite-dimensional variational formula. For $T=τ\log N$ the face of the mode minimizes $τλ_F+|F|-1$ at first order, with $λ_F$ the exit rate. If an admissible face has $Δ\ge1$ more states than another and an exit rate smaller by $δ>0$, we locate every crossing of their largest probabilities for large $T\le N^{1/3}$ up to $O(1/\log N)$. For two irreducible faces the crossing is unique for large $N$ in $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$, with coefficient $1/2$ of $\log\log N$. Near a facet, the continuous-time occupation density is the facet density times an explicit kernel, with relative error $O(1/T)$ at times $x\le cT$ off the facet, $c$ small. The counts obey a lattice form with extra error $T^2/N$ for $T\le\varepsilon_1\sqrt N$. The kernel is Bessel for $x=o(T)$ at facet profiles where the removed state has equal entry and exit laws, and at a profile where the rate has a first correction, of order $m\ge3$, if and only if $x=o(T^{1-2/m})$. On the complete graph with the uniform start, each face of at least 2 states crosses a vertex exactly once.

papers.title: Normalised Hamiltonian Elliptic Systems: a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality for bilinear mass
papers.abstract: We study Hamiltonian elliptic systems with prescribed bilinear mass $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}uv=a>0$. We establish a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality in the crossed gradient pairing and bilinear mass, on scaling-invariant component-bounded classes. It identifies the critical curve $1/p+1/q=N/(N+2)$ and the restricted energy trichotomy. For power nonlinearities, we establish uniqueness up to common translations and nondegeneracy of positive profiles throughout the Sobolev-subcritical hyperbola. Exact scaling then classifies positive normalised solutions and identifies the unique critical mass. In dimension two, we develop a bilinear exponential Gagliardo--Nirenberg estimate with a sharp gradient threshold and a truncated scalar refinement with the optimal quartic leading coefficient. Adapting variational ideas from [Cassani-Tarsi, Calc.Var.PDE (2015)] we combine a mass-normalising quotient, reduction over the full negative fibres and compactness below the concentration threshold to obtain least-energy positive radial solutions for pure exponential nonlinearities at every prescribed mass below the cubic limiting mass. Local perturbative branches and a small-frequency exponential branch yield explicit mass-response formulas.

papers.title: The solvable degree of a Schur algebra
papers.abstract: The solvable degree of a Schur algebra $D$ is the greatest common divisor of all integers $n$ such that $D^{n\times n}$ is a direct summand of the rational group algebra $\Q G$ for some finite solvable group $G$. The main result of this paper gives divisibility conditions on the solvable degree depending on the center and the rational primes that divide the discriminant of $D$.

papers.title: On the structure of certain valued fields II
papers.abstract: We study the structure of finitely ramified henselian valued fields of mixed characteristic with arbitrary residue fields via their residue rings of higher length, where a residue ring of length $n$ is the quotient ring of the valuation ring by the $n$-th power of its maximal ideal. We prove an approximate lifting theorem for homomorphisms between residue rings of higher length and explicitly determine the optimal bound of error of lifting. As applications, we obtain several Ax-Kochen-Ershov principles for relative completeness, relative existential completeness, and existential closedness using the pure ring structures on the residue rings. And we show that any formula on a residue ring of length $k$ is equivalent to a normal form of sentences in pure ordered group structure and special formulas at level $n$, uniformly for all finitely ramified henselian valued fields of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ and the same initial ramification index $e$. Here, for $n\ge k$, a special formula at level $n$ represents a definable set on a residue ring of length $k$ given by a projection image of a definable set in pure ring structure on a residue ring of length $n$. Also, such $n$ is optimally computed from the precise estimation of error of lifting and depends only on $k$, residue characteristic $p$, and initial ramification index $e$.

papers.title: Ideal Classes of Order $2^n$ in a Family of Totally Real Cubic Fields and Rational Points on Associated Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: For every prime $\ell\geq5$ and integer $n\geq2$, we construct a totally real cubic field in the family studied by Ennola with a specified prime ideal above $\ell$ whose class has exact order $2^n$. For parameters satisfying two square conditions and explicit congruences, the same squareclass obstructions give four independent rational points on the associated elliptic curves. A Pell equation describes all such parameters. A genus-one base change gives five independent sections that generate a subgroup saturated at two. It also yields infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$, pairwise nonisomorphic over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, with rank at least five.

papers.title: BV rigidity in the string topology of compact Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected compact Lie group and $R$ a commutative ring over which $H_*(G;R)$ is an exterior algebra on odd primitive generators. We prove a rigidity theorem: the Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ of Chas and Sullivan on the homology of the free loop space is that of the product of odd spheres with the classical exponents of $G$, tensored with the group ring of the torsion of $π_1(G)$. Conversely, over an integral domain the graded algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ already determines the exponents and the group ring, hence the BV algebra. The isomorphism with the product of spheres is algebraic: for $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$, $n\geq2$, and $\mathrm{SU}(n)$, $n\geq3$, no map of spaces induces it over $\mathbb{Z}$. If moreover $G$ is simply connected, then $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$, as a BV algebra, is the Hochschild cohomology of $H^*(G;R)$ with the BV operator induced by Poincaré duality.

papers.title: Some arithmetical aspects of the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that any counter-example to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture with integral coefficients and determinant of its Jacobian matrix equals one, has only paths of asymptotic values that can contain only finitely many points of the planar integral lattice. The second part of our paper gives some nontrivial applications of the theory of certain Theta functions to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture over the real field, and over the complex field.

papers.title: A Lean~4 Framework for the Radii Polynomial Method
papers.abstract: Computer-assisted proofs in dynamics establish results about nonlinear systems by rigorous numerical computation. Their correctness rests on a trusted base of interval-arithmetic libraries and analytic estimates checked by hand. We formalize in Lean~4 a framework for the radii polynomial method, which certifies an exact solution near a numerical approximation by verifying four norm bounds and the resulting polynomial inequality. Weighted coefficient algebras provide the common setting for polynomial equations and initial value problems in Taylor and Chebyshev series. Their universal properties construct the bounded operators and the evaluation maps, and the universal property of the free commutative algebra makes polynomial substitution commute with evaluation. Finite/tail reductions turn the four norm bounds into finite rational inequalities, which are checked in Lean. The radii theorem then yields an exact coefficient solution, and realization theorems carry it to a solution of the original equation. The worked examples are a square-root branch given by a convergent power series and polynomial initial value problems, among them the Lorenz system, for which the library proves existence, uniqueness within the trajectory ball, and analyticity of the function-level solution.

papers.title: Arbitrary Stage Spectra for Raikov Remainders Along Quotient Towers
papers.abstract: Let $θ$ be an ordinal and let $(N_α)_{α\leqθ}$ be a continuous increasing tower of closed normal subgroups of a Hausdorff topological group $G$, with $N_0=\{e\}$. Write $ρG$ for the Raikov completion of $G$, and put $K_α=\overline{N_α}^{ρG}$ and $H_α=GK_α$. The successive and limit differences of the groups $H_α$ mark the first stages at which points of $ρG$ become old quotient points. For every nonzero ordinal $θ$ and every set $S\subseteq(0,θ]$, there is a Hausdorff pseudocompact Boolean group with a continuous tower of closed normal subgroups such that every member of the tower is pseudocompact and the nonempty strata occur exactly at the stages in $S$. The terminal quotient can simultaneously be chosen isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, and for every $δ<θ$ the successive factor $N_{δ+1}/N_δ$ is compact exactly when $δ+1\notin S$. Thus a tower may have a single nonempty stratum at a limit stage even when every successive factor is compact. For a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, let $\widehat q:ρG\toρ(G/N)$ extend the quotient homomorphism and put $K=\overline N^{ρG}$. Over $gN\in G/N$, the fiber in $ρG\setminus G$ is $g(K\setminus N)$, homeomorphic to $ρN\setminus N$, while for $y\in\widehat q(ρG)\setminus(G/N)$ the entire $\widehat q$-fiber lies in $ρG\setminus G$ and is homeomorphic to $ρN$. For precompact kernels this gives a canonical decomposition, and nested quotients give the two-stage identity underlying the transfinite filtration.
