Further results concern pseudocompact Raikov remainders and include countable Abelian examples.

papers.title: Toeplitz Infinite GMRES for Parameterized Linear Systems
papers.abstract: We develop Toeplitz infinite GMRES for solving large sparse analytic parameterized systems $A(s)x(s)=z$ at many parameter values. Our method exploits a block upper triangular Toeplitz structure in the companion Krylov sequence to construct the Arnoldi process and recover solution approximations without storing full Arnoldi vectors. We derive incremental recurrences requiring $\mathcal{O}(np^2+p^3)$ arithmetic and $\mathcal{O}(np+p^2)$ storage for $p$ Arnoldi steps, excluding factorization setup and assuming linear-cost coefficient actions and triangular solves. A dynamic generator-refreshing strategy addresses cancellation in this basic recurrence. Moreover, we show that the Arnoldi basis can be simply represented using one block row and a nilpotent matrix. For $A(s)$ admitting a split form, we further use this structure to develop an implicitly rebased method. A residual lower bound for square-summable Taylor coefficients explains the effect of scaling outside the unit disk. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments illustrate the computational efficiency of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Discussion on "Principled type I error rate inflation in two-arm clinical trial designs with external control information borrowing" by Silvia Calderazzo, Manuel Wiesenfarth, Vivienn Weru, and Annette Kopp-Schneider
papers.abstract: Consideration of frequentist type-I error or power based on certain fixed conditions may not fully embrace the aims of a Bayesian analysis; this is particularly true in settings where informative priors are involved. Calderazzo et al. consider adaptations of a testing procedure involving Bayesian borrowing from external control data. Particular caution may be necessary here in order not to condition on parameters and data simultaneously. We consider their example case and argue that (a) the conditioning scheme may have limited practical implications, and (b) if the main concern are assumption violations, these might be better addressed by adapting the likelihood function.

papers.title: Common non-zero graphs of groups with few edges
papers.abstract: Let \( G \) be a finite group, and consider its common non-zero graph, which we denote by \( Γ_{nv}(G) \). In this graph, the vertices represent the non-linear irreducible characters of \( G \). There is an edge connecting two distinct vertices \( χ_1 \) and \( χ_2 \) if there is a vanishing element \( g \in G \) such that \( χ_1(g) χ_2(g) \neq 0 \). A finite group \( G \) is described as a strongly \( \mathcal{H}_1' \)-group if the set of vanishing elements of each of its non-linear irreducible character is equal to the set of vanishing elements of \( G \). In this paper, we prove Conjecture 1 from \cite{ourself}, which states that if \( Γ_{nv}(G) \) is null (has no edge), then \( G \) must either be a strongly \( \mathcal{H}_1' \)-group or a Frobenius group, whose Frobenius complement is isomorphic to \( Q_8 \). Additionally, we show that if there are no triangles in \( Γ_{nv}(G) \), this implies that the group is solvable. We also look at the situation where the common non-zero graph of a finite group \( G \) contains only one edge. This leads us to conclude that \( G \) is either isomorphic to \( S_4 \); or that the single edge in \( Γ_{nv}(G) \) is of the form \( \{θ, ζθ\} \) for some \( ζ\in \Irr(G/G') \) and \( θ\in \Irr(G|G') \), $G$ is a $p$-nilpotent group for some prime $p$ and for all characters \( χ\in \Irr(G|G') - \{θ, ζθ\} \), we find \( \Van(χ) = \Van(G) \). Lastly, our study also explores groups whose common non-zero graph forms a star shape, concluding that such configurations can only occur if \( G \) has exactly one non-linear irreducible character.

papers.title: $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless inclusions for the infinite braid group
papers.abstract: Let $B_\infty$ be the braid group on infinitely many strands and $P_\infty$ its pure braid group. We show that $C^*_r(P_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ and all its intermediate inclusions are $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and completely selfless. This gives natural examples of simple nonnuclear $\mathcal{Z}$-stable $C^*$-algebras. Further examples come from $\mathrm{SL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$. We also show that $C^*_r(\mathbb{F}_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ is completely selfless for the free group $\mathbb{F}_\infty$ of braids in which only the first strand moves. All results hold for twisted group $C^*$-algebras. In contrast, $\mathcal{Z}$-stability fails for $B_n$ with $n$ finite and for groups that are not inner amenable.

papers.title: Spectral gap, internality of relative commutants, and non-hyperlinear groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the relative commutant of a finite unitary tuple in a tracial matrix ultraproduct is internal whenever its conjugation operator has a spectral gap off the commutant. This implies the existence of a non-hyperlinear group.

papers.title: Infinite-Particle Determinantal Dynamics from Brownian Motion on $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$
papers.abstract: We study the edge scaling limit of the logarithms of the squared singular values of multiplicative Brownian motion on the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$ with general initial conditions. Building on earlier work [arXiv:2605.06429], we prove that, for every initial condition in the enhanced state space, the limiting dynamics are determinantal and derive an explicit double-contour formula for their extended multitime correlation kernel. The dependence on the initial state, including information not determined by the particle coordinates, is encoded by the associated Laguerre--Pólya entire function. We further extend the construction of solutions to the corresponding infinite-dimensional system of singular stochastic differential equations to arbitrary initial configurations, including those with coinciding coordinates.

papers.title: $p$-adic spectral zeta functions via the inverse Stieltjes transform
papers.abstract: Spectral zeta functions provide a standard tool for regularizing determinants of differential operators in quantum physics. In a previous paper (J. Math. Phys. 66: 083505, 2025), we introduced a $p$-adic spectral zeta function for discrete spectra via a locally analytic interpolation function. In this paper we extend the framework to continuous spectra using the inverse Stieltjes transform. Starting from the resolvent of a bounded operator, we construct a generalized distribution, called the $p$-adic spectral distribution, and define bosonic and fermionic zeta functions and functional determinants. We establish their analytic properties, special value formulas, and Stirling expansions, and show that our previous framework is embedded into the present one in the discrete case. In this approach, the bosonic and fermionic cases exhibit an interesting symmetry. As an application, we consider the position operator in $p$-adic quantum mechanics on an arbitrary compact subset of $\mathbb{C}_{p}$.

papers.title: Proper circular arc graphs are $e$-positive
papers.abstract: We prove an $e$-positive formula for the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs solving the $q=1$ case of a conjecture of Ellzey and of Alexandersson and Panova. In doing so, we provide a new proof of the $e$-positivity of unit interval graphs, which alongside Guay-Paquet's reduction gives a new proof of the Stanley--Stembridge conjecture. We define color matrices, which count proper colorings, and tableau matrices, whose entries are nonnegative rational numbers and ratios of elementary symmetric functions. We prove the two matrices are related by a single family of change of basis matrices, which become invertible after restricting to finitely many colors, and we show the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs comes from taking the trace of these matrices. Using Hikita's tableaux, this gives an explicit formula for the chromatic symmetric function of a proper circular arc graph as a weighted sum over tableaux whose first and last $k$ vertices lie in the same columns.

papers.title: Singular analysis of the principal eigenvalue for cooperative elliptic systems with drifts
papers.abstract: We determine the small-diffusion limit of the principal eigenvalue for a one-dimensional cooperative elliptic system with component-dependent drifts and Neumann boundary conditions. For scalar equations, this limit is determined by local data at the drift equilibria and boundary points. We show that such localization fails for systems: switching between components can make some intervals spectrally relevant. We first prove that the logarithmic transforms of all component eigenfunctions converge to the same function, which solves a scalar Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The associated Aubry set determines the asymptotic behavior of the principal eigenvalue. Under nondegeneracy assumptions, this set decomposes into isolated points, regular intervals, and composite intervals containing common drift zeros. We then identify the effective value of each class through local Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spectra and interval transport problems, and establish that the limit of the principal eigenvalue is the minimum of these class values. A unique minimizing class also determines the common logarithmic eigenfunction profile.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff instability of the positive mass theorem for Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct a sequence of AE Kähler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^2$ with nonnegative and integrable scalar curvature whose ADM mass tends to zero but which, for a suitable choice of basepoints, fails to converge to Euclidean space in the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff sense.

papers.title: Continuous Data Assimilation for Memristive FitzHugh--Nagumo Neural Networks
papers.abstract: In this study, we investigate continuous data assimilation for a class of partly diffusive FitzHugh--Nagumo neural networks with memristive feedback and linear synaptic coupling. The nudging algorithm implemented here only adds a feedback term to the membrane-potential equations, while the recovery and memductance variables remain unobserved. We obtain weighted energy estimates that give sufficient conditions for exponential convergence of the data-assimilated solution to the reference solution under full or coarse membrane potential observations. Moreover, we prove energy-class uniqueness in dimensions one and two. In dimension three, the uniqueness criterion is an \(L^4\) membrane-potential initial data. We also establish an observational-noise estimate for locally square-integrable forcing, yielding an asymptotic error bound when the noise energy is eventually bounded.

papers.title: On the language of palindromic reduced words in a Coxeter group
papers.abstract: We prove that the language of palindromic reduced words in a Coxeter system is regular if and only if the Coxeter group is a direct product of a finite Coxeter group with finitely many copies of the infinite dihedral group.

papers.title: Robert J. Daverman (1941-2026)
papers.abstract: This is an expanded version of a memorial article that is to appear in the Notices of the American Mathematical Society.

papers.title: Open extension of a genus zero Hurwitz-Frobenius manifold
papers.abstract: Every Dubrovin--Frobenius manifold provides a solution to the WDVV equation, that was initially formulated in the study of the moduli space of curves. During the last two decades special attention was given to the "open" version of the moduli space of curves. Its genus zero intersection theory is governed by the system of equations called open WDVV equation, that extends "classical" WDVV equation. In this note we study Dubrovin--Frobenius manifold structures on the Hurwitz spaces of genus zero. We construct explicitly the solutions to open WDVV equation for these Dubrovin--Frobenius manifolds and show that these solutions appear as the restriction of the Dubrovin--Frobenius structure to its discriminant.

papers.title: Plane separating continua inscribe rectangles
papers.abstract: We prove the following: If $X$ is a plane separating continuum, then every embedding of $X$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains the vertices of a Euclidean rectangle. We arrive to this result by extending a known result by H. Vaughan for Jordan curves to a wider class of topological objects via shape theory and Steenrod homology.

papers.title: Bistationary Traces, Wide Levels, and Branch-Cover Rigidity for an Unrestricted Typed Variant of the Hayut-Magidor Forcing
papers.abstract: For every uncountable regular cardinal $α$, $\mathbb S^{\ast}(α)$ is an explicitly typed four-coordinate forcing motivated by the ladder-system construction of Hayut and Magidor. The forcing is $σ$-closed and, after adjoining a formal maximum, $α$-strategically closed. For $α\geqω_2$, every nonempty countable family of designated generic branches has a stationary and costationary common trace on the generic ladder-coordinate set $L_α$, while no countable family of cofinal branches generates $L_α$. These conclusions persist under a Kurepa-style level-size bound. In the unrestricted forcing, for every infinite cardinal $μ<α$ in the ground model, some level of the generic tree contains a copy of $({}^μ2)^V$. Consequently, the endpoint-corrected restriction family indexed by $\mathcal P_{ω_2}α$ is too wide, whereas the scaled restriction system indexed by $\mathcal P_αα$ has all levels of size less than $α$ exactly when $α$ is strongly inaccessible in the ground model. When these equivalent conditions hold, the branch-covering number of $L_α$ relative to the scaled system is at least $ω_1$. The low-cofinality empty-value convention also ensures that the set of domains of $L_α$ contains no club in $\mathcal P_αα$. The unrestricted tree clause of the motivating presentation is retained, without asserting forcing equivalence.

papers.title: The Smoothability of Embedded Surfaces in 4-Manifolds Under Stabilizations
papers.abstract: We study the smooth stabilization number of a locally flat embedded surface in a smooth $4$-manifold, defined as the minimum number of connected sums with $S^2\times S^2$ needed to make the surface topologically isotopic to a smooth embedding. We prove that a nonsmoothable locally flat surface in a closed, simply connected smooth $4$-manifold becomes smoothable after a single stabilization if its homology class is primitive and noncharacteristic and its complement has abelian fundamental group. This yields infinitely many examples of nonsmoothable surfaces with smooth stabilization number one. We also exhibit examples for which a single stabilization produces infinitely many pairwise smoothly nonisotopic representatives in the same topological isotopy class. In contrast, we construct a locally flat genus-eight surface representing $6h$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ whose smooth stabilization number is exactly two. More generally, we show that smooth stabilization numbers of locally flat embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are unbounded.

papers.title: Biharmonic Conformal Immersions of Hypersurfaces: Dirac Rigidity and Mixed Clifford Geometry
papers.abstract: A biharmonic conformal immersion asks whether a hypersurface can become a critical point of the bienergy after a conformal change of the domain metric. We study when this flexibility can produce compact nonconstant-mean-curvature geometry in space forms. For surfaces in three-dimensional space forms, with $U=λ^2H$, Ou's system is encoded exactly by a Laplace-type operator acting on a restricted ambient Killing spinor. We classify all monic scalar--chiral factorizations of this operator. In nonzero curvature such a factorization exists locally exactly when the principal curvatures are locally constant; the normalized Euclidean branch is equally rigid, and the remaining real spherical non-CMC branch is excluded by a finite-type Frobenius obstruction. For $m>2$, this scalar rigidity does not imply geometric nonexistence. The conformal tension has independent normal and tangential components. We prove that $\mathbb Rξ\oplus TM$ is the minimal natural $O(m)$-equivariant carrier, derive the corresponding strongly elliptic Jacobi block and its two-grade Clifford realization, and identify off-diagonal hybridization as the escape mechanism. Exact cohomogeneity-one reductions, combined with validated interval and Chebyshev/radii-polynomial arguments, yield embedded proper non-CMC, nowhere-umbilical examples in round spheres, including $$ S^1\times\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb S^n\hookrightarrow\mathbb S^{2n+2} \qquad(n\ge1). $$ Thus the scalar obstruction is sharp with respect to coefficient bundle: the smallest enlargement forced by conformal tension already supports compact non-CMC solutions.

papers.title: Wehrl-type entropy problem for compact connected semisimple Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a compact connected semisimple Lie group, and let $π:G\to U(V_λ)$ be a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation associated with the highest weight $λ$. We prove that coherent projectors are the unique minimizers of the Wehrl entropy over all density matrices on $V_λ$. Similar extremal properties hold for power functions in place of the entropy function. The proof uses a second variation at the extremizer by perturbation in directions associated with Killing fields, similar to the strategy of Frank and Lieb used in \cite{FrankLieb}. Then the problem reduces to the uncertainty principle characterizing coherent states. This solves the Wehrl-type entropy problem for arbitrary compact connected semisimple Lie groups.

papers.title: Maximal Algebraic Ideals in Nonunital $C^*$-Algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of maximal algebraic two-sided ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras. We formulate singular-distribution estimates in terms of lower semicontinuous $2$-quasitraces and introduce a novel criterion, which we call an admissible compact quasitracial triple set. These tools allow us to control membership in algebraic ideals and to prove the nonexistence of maximal ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras under a closed finite-scale face condition. This nonexistence result applies to a broad class of simple $C^*$-algebras including simple separable stable AF algebras, and nonunital, simple, separable, stably finite, $\mathcal Z$-stable $C^*$-algebras $A$ that admit an approximate identity consisting of increasing projections $(p_n)$ and for which the simplex $\operatorname{QT}_2^1(A,p_1)$ of normalized traces at $p_1$ has finitely many extreme points. Moreover, we construct a simple AF algebra whose finite-scale face is dense but not closed and which nevertheless has a maximal dense algebraic ideal. This example yields a negative resolution to a question raised by Ozawa, asking whether every maximal algebraic two-sided ideal in a $C^*$-algebra must be closed.

papers.title: Mixing time under monotone censoring
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Ding and Mossel~\cite{DM}: the lazy random walk on the discrete cube, censored to any increasing set of fixed positive density, mixes in time $O(n\log n)$. More precisely, for every nonempty increasing set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, with $a=μ(A)$ and $μ$ uniform on the cube, we prove $$ t_{\mathrm{mix}}(P)\le C_a n\log(en), $$ where $C_a$ depends only on $a$. The proof uses hypercontractivity on the ambient cube to strengthen the Poincaré inequality on coordinate sections. An optimal stopping time occupation inequality for increasing sets converts the resulting local bound into a uniform bound on hitting times of large sets. An appendix by Y.~Peres improves the density dependence to $C_a=13a^{-1}\log(e/a)$, within a logarithmic factor of the conjectured $a^{-1}$ dependence.

papers.title: On smooth and bundle structures on topological manifolds homotopy equivalent to $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$
papers.abstract: We first verify the expected calculations of the topological structure set, in the sense of surgery theory, for the total spaces of $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$ for $k\ge3$, in which manifolds homotopy equivalent to the total spaces are organized. Next, we investigate the question of which of the elements in these structure sets can be realized as such bundles. Moreover, we study the forgetful map from the smooth version to the topological version of the structure set; we determine its image. All elements in the image turn out to have the underlying manifold such a bundle.

papers.title: Generating pairs in $\mathfrak g_2$ related by an involution
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb O$ be the real octonion division algebra, let $\mathfrak g_2=\operatorname{Der}(\mathbb O)$, and fix a quaternionic subalgebra $H\subset\mathbb O$. We ask when an element $Z$ preserving $H$ and its conjugate $TZT^{-1}$ generate $\mathfrak g_2$, where $T$ is a prescribed involutive octonion automorphism. We prove that such a $Z$ exists if and only if $T(H)\ne H$. Moreover, a fixed set of six derivations preserving $H$ contains a generating choice for every such $T$. For an arbitrary $Z\in\mathfrak g_2$, we construct a polynomial criterion with two factors: one detects reducibility on the imaginary octonions, and the other detects generated algebras of dimension at most three. An irreducible proper generated algebra must be a principal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. We characterize the elements admitting this case by their rotation frequencies and parametrize all corresponding involutions. For one specified involution and quaternionic subalgebra $H$, we describe the nongenerating set by four geometric families and six irredundant systems of scalar equations, and prove that it has real dimension four.

papers.title: Variational properties of Perron's extremal solutions in the Bernoulli one-phase problem
papers.abstract: We study the Perron extremal solutions of the stationary one-phase Bernoulli problem. These solutions are important in several applications, but not much is known about the regularity of their free boundaries due to their non-variational construction. We show that, in fact, Perron extremal solutions retain some variational features; specifically, they are solutions in the sense of inner variations. We establish this property by showing that extremal solutions arise as infinite-time limits of monotone solutions of the parabolic Bernoulli problem. As a consequence, we are able to describe the structure of singularities for Perron extremal solutions in two dimensions: largest subsolutions have smooth free boundaries, while smallest supersolutions have free boundary points that are either smooth, or whose blow-up limits are two-plane wedges with equal slope.

papers.title: Proximal-Linearized NEP Method for Composite Optimization with Set-Inclusion and Manifold Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on difference-of-convex (DC) composite optimization problems with set-inclusion and manifold constraints. We develop an inexact proximal-linearized nonsmooth exact penalty (NEP) method that penalizes the conic constraint while retaining the manifold constraint explicitly. At each outer iteration, the method approximately solves a strongly convex proximal-linearized subproblem over the current tangent space, using computable inexactness criteria, adaptive parameters, and a retraction-based acceptance mechanism. Under boundedness of the iterates and penalty parameters, we establish an $O(ε^{-2})$ worst-case outer iteration complexity for finding an $ε$-approximate KKT point of the original problem. We further develop a complexity-transfer framework relating uniform primal objective-gap and KKT-residual decay, or dual objective-gap decay, to total inner-iteration complexity bounds. This yields an $O(ε^{-4})$ overall oracle complexity with either accelerated semi-proximal ADMM or FISTA applied to the dual subproblem as the inner solver. Using semi-proximal ADMM as the inner solver improves the bound to $O(ε^{-2}\log(1/ε))$ under an additional uniform error-bound condition. We further establish convergence of the entire iterate sequence to a KKT point under the same boundedness assumption and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property of the associated potential function. Numerical experiments demonstrate the competitive performance of the proposed method on row-sparse PCA, clustering, robust SVMs, and nonconvex SOCPs.

papers.title: Hodge-Deligne and Poincaré polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$
papers.abstract: By studying wall crossings of Hassett moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we prove a recursive formula that reduces the computation of the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ to that of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,(0^+)^n}$ of stable pointed curves of minimal weights. For $g=1$, we further prove an explicit formula for the Hodge-Deligne and Poincaré polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,(0^+)^n}$. Combining these, we prove formulas that enable us to compute the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$ efficiently.

papers.title: Critical Schatten exponents for the Berger-Coburn endpoint problem
papers.abstract: Berger and Coburn showed that boundedness of a Toeplitz operator $T_g$ on the Fock space controls the heat transform $g^{(t)}$ for $1/4<t<1$, and conjectured that $T_g$ is bounded if and only if $g^{(1/4)}$ is bounded. Looi recently disproved the forward implication by constructing a bounded $T_g$ with unbounded $g^{(1/4)}$. We prove that the reverse implication also fails, even for a real-valued admissible symbol $g$ with $g^{(1/4)}\in C_0(\mathbb{C}^n)$, and that the forward implication fails even when $T_g\in S_p$ for every finite $p>1$. Our counterexamples come from Baire category and closed graph arguments, which yield no explicit symbols. Despite this two-sided failure, the forward implication has a sharp Schatten-class form: $\|g^{(1/4)}\|_\infty\le 2^n\|T_g\|_{S_1}$ for every admissible symbol $g$ with $T_g$ trace class. We show that the constant $2^n$ is optimal and that the same estimate holds with $S_p$ in place of $S_1$ for $T_g\in S_p$ when $0<p\le1$. For $p>1$, no corresponding uniform estimate holds, even for smooth compactly supported symbols. We also determine the optimal constants in the Berger--Coburn estimates for $1/4<t\le1$. Finally, for $1\le p<\infty$, we show that the equivalence $T_g\in S_p$ if and only if $g^{(1/4)}\in L^p$ holds exactly when $p=2$, answering a question of Bauer, Coburn, and Isralowitz.

papers.title: The maximum spectral radius of outerplanar and planar $k$-uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: For $k\ge3$, a $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected outerplane graph whose interior faces are bounded by $k$-cycles, and a closed $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected plane graph all of whose faces are bounded by $k$-cycles. Their face hypergraphs have the same vertices as the graphs; the hyperedges are the vertex sets of the interior faces, respectively all faces. For $k=3$, the extremal problems over these hypergraphs agree with those for the outerplanar and planar $3$-uniform hypergraphs of Ellingham, Lu and Wang, who determined the outerplanar maximizer for large $n$ and conjectured the planar one. In this paper, for each fixed $k$, we determine the hypergraphs of maximum spectral radius in both classes for all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying the corresponding face-count divisibility condition. In the outerplanar case, the unique extremal hypergraph is the face hypergraph of the fan, in which one vertex lies on every interior face. In the planar case with $k=3$, it is the face hypergraph of $K_2+P_{n-2}$, which confirms the conjecture of Ellingham, Lu and Wang. For $k\ge4$, the extremal hypergraphs are the face hypergraphs of balanced theta graphs, in which two vertices lie on every face. For $k=4$, the result holds for every $n\ge5$, with extremal hypergraph ${\mathcal H}(K_{2,n-2})$. For $k\ge6$ and an even number of faces, there are exactly $\lfloor(k-2)/2\rfloor$ extremal hypergraphs up to isomorphism.

papers.title: Matchings and shape-Wilf-Equivalence of sets of patterns of length three I: Triples
papers.abstract: Permutation pattern avoidance on Ferrers boards has become a central topic in enumerative combinatorics with important connections to matchings, set partitions, and other combinatorial structures as it allows one to build families of Wilf-equivalent patterns. While shape-Wilf-equivalence classes have been completely determined for individual patterns and pairs of patterns of length three, the corresponding classification for larger pattern sets has remained open. In this paper, we provide a complete classification of the shape-Wilf-equivalence classes of triples of patterns of length three. Our proofs use a bijective encoding of pattern avoiding transversals to establish all equivalence classes. As an application, we enumerate matchings avoiding triples of patterns of length three for all, extending previous results of Bloom and Elizalde. These enumerative results identify additional families of combinatorial objects counted by the Fuss-Catalan numbers and by other integer sequences appearing in the OEIS.

papers.title: Asymmetric Periodic Water Waves in Finite Depth
papers.abstract: We consider the full two-dimensional water-wave equations in finite depth, with and without surface tension. Water waves have been studied mathematically for more than two centuries. Reflection symmetry remains a common assumption in constructions of periodic steady waves, although asymmetric profiles have been observed in experiments and numerical computations. We construct families of periodic stationary solutions whose free surfaces have no axis of reflection, in both the pure-gravity and capillary--gravity cases. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous construction of asymmetric periodic pure-gravity waves for the full two-dimensional water-wave problem in finite depth. The proof combines localized vorticity laws with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. In the pure-gravity case, we introduce a small background shear flow to obtain an invertible boundary operator and couple the interior and free-surface approximations at leading order.

papers.title: Central non-vanishing of Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every sufficiently large modulus $q\not\equiv2\bmod4$, at least $3/8-o(1)$ of the primitive Dirichlet characters $χ$ modulo $q$ have $L(1/2,χ)\ne0$. We also establish stronger proportions for moduli $q$ satisfying certain arithmetic conditions.

papers.title: Minimum Cardinalities of Multipartite Unextendible Product Bases
papers.abstract: In quantum information theory, the state space of a multipartite quantum system is modeled by a tensor product. In the tensor-product space $\C^{d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\C^{d_p}$, a nonzero vector is a \emph{product state} if it can be written as $\ket{\varphi_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\ket{\varphi_p}$ with $\ket{\varphi_j}\in\C^{d_j}\setminus\{0\}$. An \emph{unextendible product basis} (UPB) is a finite family of pairwise orthogonal product states such that no nonzero product state is orthogonal to all of them. UPBs play a key role in investigating quantum entanglement and nonlocal phenomena. Finding a smallest UPB is a natural extremal problem: it asks how few pairwise orthogonal product states suffice to prevent any further product state from being added. The general minimum-size problem for UPBs has been studied for over two decades since the seminal work of Alon and Lovász. Let $f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)$ be the minimum cardinality of a UPB in the space, and let \(f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=1+\sum_{j=1}^{p}(d_j-1)\) be the natural lower bound. Alon and Lovász determined exactly when \(f_m\) attains the lower bound \(f_{LB}\), but the obstructed multipartite cases remained open in general. We prove a stabilization theorem: for every non-all-qubit system with $p\ge3$, whenever the natural lower bound $f_{LB}$ is unattainable, the true minimum is exactly $f_{LB}+1$. Precisely, if the number of even local dimensions $d_i$ is positive and even, and at least one local dimension is greater than two, then \(f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)+1\). The proof is built on a unified graph-theoretic framework. Our result, together with earlier work, settles the minimum size problem for UPBs in all finite quantum systems.

papers.title: Finite Directional Coefficient Modules over Euler Fibers of $A$-Hypergeometric Systems
papers.abstract: Let A be a d-by-n integer matrix of rank d, let beta belong to the d-dimensional complex vector space, and consider the A-hypergeometric system defined by the ideal H_A(beta), with relation lattice L equal to the integer kernel of A. No homogeneity, pointedness, or positivity assumption is imposed on A. We study directed formal logarithmic solutions simultaneously over all exponent lattices in the Euler fiber over beta, which form an uncountable family when L has positive rank. For a fixed L-generic direction, negative-support strata are described by rational sign polyhedra, and their directional boundedness is characterized by recession cones. On each exponent lattice, normalization reduces the infinitely indexed coefficient equations to a finite system of Euler, transit, and directional vanishing relations, represented by a finitely presented directional coefficient module. We prove that only finitely many exponent lattices contribute nonzero directed solution spaces and that every contributing coefficient module has finite length. Macaulay inverse-system duality then identifies the dimension of the all-lattice directed formal logarithmic solution space with the length of the all-lattice coefficient module. We also give an explicit formal-series realization and a polynomial colon-ideal criterion for all realizable lowest exponents.

papers.title: On the invariance of risk-sensitive LQR gain under input randomization
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the optimal gain of the risk-sensitive linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem is invariant under input randomization when the cost penalizes the realized noisy input. This may appear counterintuitive at first glance because certainty equivalence does not hold for risk-sensitive LQR and input randomization inflates the effective process noise. Nonetheless, the gain is preserved because the input noise enters not only the system dynamics but also the cost functional, and its total effect eventually vanishes. Consequently, the optimal gain and the Riccati recursion need not be recomputed, and the increment in the optimal cost can be readily evaluated in closed form. This result facilitates the use of risk-sensitive LQR in applications that employ input randomization for privacy or exploration, such as dynamic watermarking for replay attack detection.

papers.title: Failure of the local decay formula for Arnold multiplicities under twisted Kähler--Ricci flow
papers.abstract: Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu asked whether local Arnold multiplicities under maximal weak twisted Kähler--Ricci flow with fixed cohomology class satisfy $λ(\varphi_t,x)=\max\{λ(\varphi_0,x)-t,0\}$. We construct counterexamples with analytic initial singularities in every dimension $n\ge2$. On the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$, $e\ge2$, the initial current $[S]+(e+1)[F]$ yields $λ(\varphi_t,x)=1/2-t/e$ for $x\in S\setminus F$ and $0<t<e/2$, where $S$ is the negative section and $F$ a fibre. Products with smooth stationary factors give higher-dimensional examples. The Zariski negative part of $\{S\}+\{F\}$, the reduced support class, forces extra divisor mass. For pure divisorial data with simple normal crossings support, a smooth semipositive representative of the reduced support class's positive part gives exact short-time formulas. On one surface we construct flows with identical initial current germs, background data and global initial Arnold multiplicity, but different local rates.

papers.title: A note on the center of the queer super Yangian ${\rm Y}(\mathfrak{q}_1)$
papers.abstract: We investigate two families of central elements of the queer super Yangian ${\rm Y}(\mathfrak{q}_1)$, arising from the constructions of Poletaeva-Serganova and from Nazarov's quantum Berezinian. We establish an explicit relation between their generating series, thereby giving an answer to the question raised by Nazarov in \cite{Na22}.

papers.title: Mirror descent algorithms with logarithmic barriers
papers.abstract: We derive convergence guarantees for mirror descent and proximal mirror descent with a logarithmic barrier as the distance-generating function. When the solution lies on the boundary, the Bregman divergence blows up and classical guarantees become vacuous. While existing remedies recover $O(\log k/k)$ rates by adapting classical bounds, we propose a more direct route in which the Bregman distance to the solution never appears, and which achieves the same rate with constant stepsize. We also construct an example showing that this rate cannot be improved in general. Finally, we compare the proposed approach with interior-point methods.

papers.title: A characterization of the reversibility of linear cellular automata
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group, let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field, and let $V$ be a $\mathbb{K}$-vector space. We prove that there exists a bijective linear cellular automaton $V^G\to V^G$ whose inverse is not a cellular automaton if and only if $G$ is not locally finite and $\dim_{\mathbb{K}}V \geq |\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$. In particular, $|\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$ is the exact dimension threshold for non-reversibility. This answers an open problem proposed by T. Ceccherini-Silberstein and M. Coornaert.

papers.title: Minimum attaining operators on reducing subspaces: Spectral structure and density
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce and study the class $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ of minimum attaining operators on a separable Hilbert space $H$ whose restrictions to every nonzero reducing subspace are minimum attaining. This class lies between the classes of absolutely minimum attaining operators and minimum attaining operators. We establish a spectral characterization of positive operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$: a positive operator $T$ belongs to $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ if and only if $T=\sum_{λ\inΛ}λP_λ$, where $Λ\subseteq[0,\|T\|]$ is a countable well-ordered set, $(P_λ)_{λ\inΛ}$ is a family of mutually orthogonal nonzero projections, and $\sum_{λ\inΛ}P_λ=I$ in the strong operator topology. We also establish a connection between $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ and the class of operators attaining their norm on every nonzero reducing subspace. Further, we obtain stability results under suitable finite-rank and compact perturbations, and prove that $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ is norm dense in $\mathcal{B}(H)$. We also establish the norm density of operators in this class having a nontrivial invariant half-space. Finally, we characterize normal operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$, obtain a corresponding characterization for multiplication operators on $L^2(\mathbb{T})$, and characterize the condition $\mathcal{R}_T=\mathcal{R}_{|T|}$ in terms of the von Neumann algebra generated by $|T|$, showing that this condition forces $T$ to be normal.

papers.title: Exponential Growth of Mean Multiplicities in Length Spectra of Semi-Arithmetic Surfaces of Arbitrary Arithmetic Dimension
papers.abstract: For a semi-arithmetic Fuchsian group $Γ$ of arithmetic dimension $r$ with a generalized modular embedding, EGMM holds for $r\leq2$, and for $r\geq3$ under an explicit \emph{strong contraction condition}, via a multi-dimensional Schwarz-Pick bound and a geometry-of-numbers estimate. A covering construction turns every known example into an infinite explicit family with the same exponent via principal congruence towers. We add new $r\leq2$ examples (genus-$3$/$4$ Prym eigenform loci, a different commensurability class from the known triangle groups and McMullen genus-two family) and attempt a direct flat-geometric bound on the contraction constant $δ$ for the latter via its Lyapunov exponents ($δ=2/3$ on ergodic average, by Bainbridge exact computation), explaining why an average bound does not yet certify the pointwise one \eqref{eqstrong-contraction} needs.

papers.title: Comparing positive Toeplitz operators on holomorphic and pluriharmonic Fock spaces
papers.abstract: We prove sharp norm comparisons between positive Toeplitz operators associated with the same positive Borel measure, acting respectively on holomorphic functions and on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions, both equipped with the Gaussian-weighted $L^2$ norm. For every positive Borel measure $μ$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $0<p<\infty$, both operators are compact with summable $p$th powers of their singular values (i.e. Schatten) exactly when $z\mapstoμ(B(z,r))$ belongs to $L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$ for some fixed radius $r>0$. For other weights, this agreement can fail dramatically. We construct a weight $e^{-2φ}$ and a finite positive measure $μ$ on $\mathbb{C}$ for which the operator on holomorphic functions has the same singular values as with the Gaussian weight and the same measure $μ$. These values have summable $p$th powers for every $p>0$, yet the quadratic form on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions is unbounded in weighted $L^2$. The example still satisfies $Δφ=2$, as for the Gaussian choice $φ(z)=|z|^2/2$.

papers.title: Two improved Liouville-type theorems for the 3D stationary tropical climate model without temperature assumptions
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we establish two improved Liouville-type theorems for the three-dimensional stationary tropical climate model without imposing any temperature assumptions. Compared with previous results, we achieve significant improvements on the growth assumptions imposed on $u$, $v$ and $
abla v$. Owing to the special structure inherent to the equations, we fully exploit the $L^2$-estimate for the oscillation of the temperature, refined interpolation techniques and an iteration argument to establish a Liouville-type theorem under flexible and relaxed power-law growth conditions. As an interesting consequence, we obtain the triviality of solutions under the integrability conditions imposed only on $(u,
abla v)$ or $(
abla u,
abla v)$. Furthermore, by developing a systematic framework to handle the energy function associated with the non-trivial solutions and with the aid of delicate ODE analysis and a contradiction argument, we refine our Liouville-type theorem by introducing logarithmic corrections to the growth rates.

papers.title: On The Spectral Properties of Discrete Landscape Functions
papers.abstract: We study the landscape function on a discretized interval. The discrete landscape has an explicit closed form, and its spectral coefficients can be computed exactly. We show that these coefficients lie in explicit abelian extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ and obtain the bound $$[\mathbb{Q}(c_k(N)):\mathbb{Q}]\leq\varphi(N)$$ for every odd $k$. The Chandra--Jain conjecture, asserting that $[\mathbb{Q}(c_1(N)):\mathbb{Q}]=\varphi(N)$ for all $N\geq3$, has since been proved by Q. Zhou (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21935814). We then reduce higher modes to the coprime case. Exact computations for all 624 pairs with $3\leq N\leq50$ reveal only the degrees $\varphi(N/d)$ and $2\varphi(N/d)$ for non-coprime modes, where $d=\gcd(N,k)$. This motivates the Second Chandra--Jain Conjecture that this degree dichotomy holds generally. We also discuss connections with parity, the Arnold cat map, and Lefschetz numbers.

papers.title: High-order $L^2$-Galerkin schemes for the decoupled potential integral equations
papers.abstract: We prove Sobolev space well-posedness of the decoupled potential integral equations. Using basic pseudo-differential techniques, discrete stability is obtained for the standard $L^2$-pairing, and we deduce spectral convergence for high-order schemes employing discontinuous basis functions, or with additional element-wise tangential continuity imposed in the vectorial part of the system. The schemes are shown to be much better conditioned than a mature commercial EFIE/CFIE solver. In many cases appearing almost independent of wavenumber, mesh density, and the order.

papers.title: Entropy Scales in Topological Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we define topological and measure-theoretic entropy scales in dynamical systems for the scaling introduced by Helfter. Firstly, we establish a variational principle between Bowen and lower entropy scales on compact subsets. Secondly, we prove factor inequalities for Bowen and upper capacity entropy scales on arbitrary subsets; unlike the classical additive case, the fiber contribution is described by a transfer function and need not be additive. We also study entropy scales and sequence entropy scales under the induced action. Under suitable conditions, zero values are preserved in both directions, while positive values become infinite; counterexamples show that additional assumptions are generally necessary. As an application, we use entropy scales to distinguish zero-entropy systems sharing the same entropy dimension but differ in finer orbit-growth rates.

papers.title: Polyhedral Outer Approximation for MISOCP: Geometry and Progressive Integrality
papers.abstract: Polyhedral outer approximation (OA) is widely used to solve mixed-integer second-order cone programs (MISOCPs) by iteratively strengthening polyhedral relaxations of conic constraints. However, the accumulation of cutting planes can increase the difficulty of solving the resulting mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs), while repeatedly solving these MILPs can be computationally expensive. To address these challenges, we investigate the geometry of supporting cuts and the computational role of integrality in OA. First, we establish theoretical bounds showing that the marginal contribution of a new supporting cut decreases at least linearly as its supporting direction approaches an existing one. Motivated by this analysis, we develop a closed-form cut-generation strategy that balances separation depth and directional diversity. Second, we propose a progressive-integrality OA framework that strengthens the polyhedral approximation through linear programs and partially integral relaxations before solving full MILPs. We theoretically characterize the transfer of cut-induced bound improvements across integrality levels and provide a branch-and-bound interpretation of the framework. Computational experiments on CBLIB instances and large-scale AC unit-commitment models demonstrate substantial improvements over classical OA and direct MISOCP solution, with runtime reductions of up to 62\% relative to classical OA on the reported power-system instances.

papers.title: New Bounds on Distributional Sectional Category and Applications to Distributional Homotopic Distance
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish several new bounds for the distributional sectional category ($\mathrm{dsecat}$). We first prove Jauhari's conjecture, thereby establishing a cohomological lower bound for $\mathrm{dsecat}$ with arbitrary coefficients. We then obtain an analogous lower bound with rational coefficients by constructing a natural graded $\mathbb{Q}$-linear section of the homomorphism induced in cohomology by the symmetric diagonal. As applications, we provide several computations of the distributional sectional category. We also establish multiplicative product and composition inequalities for $\mathrm{dsecat}$. Finally, we apply these results to distributional homotopic distance. A sequential version of this invariant was recently introduced by Jauhari and Oprea; we give an equivalent formulation in terms of distributed homotopies and derive new fibration and multiplicative triangle inequalities.

papers.title: Online Multi-Level Aggregation with Maximum Delay
papers.abstract: We study Multi-Level Aggregation with Maximum Delay (MLA-MD) on finite weighted rooted trees. Each service pays for a rooted subtree and for the maximum waiting time among the requests it clears. For the offline problem, we give an exact polynomial-time algorithm that computes both the optimum and an optimal service schedule. For the online problem, we give a deterministic $2$-competitive algorithm and, against an oblivious adversary, a randomized $e/(e-1)$-competitive algorithm. Both competitive ratios are optimal, even on rooted paths. We also extend the offline result and both online guarantees to service systems with submodular costs.

papers.title: On graphs without cycles of length $0$ modulo $3$ or $4$ modulo $6$
papers.abstract: We study graphs containing no cycle whose length is divisible by $3$ or congruent to $4$ modulo $6$. We prove that every such $n$-vertex graph $G$, where $n \ge 2$, satisfies $e(G) \le (11/8)n-7/4$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $n=8k+2$ for some nonnegative integer $k$ and $G$ is isomorphic to the explicitly constructed graph $H_k$. We also construct, for every $n\geq2$, an $n$-vertex graph with $\left\lfloor (11/8)n-7/4 \right\rfloor$ edges satisfying the same cycle restriction. Consequently, this is the exact maximum number of edges for every $n \ge 2$.

papers.title: Rigidity of Averages over the Two Largest Prime Factors
papers.abstract: Let $P_1(n)$ and $P_2(n)$ be the largest and second-largest distinct prime factors of $n$. Alladi and Johnson asked whether there is a bounded function $f$ on the primes such that the averages $\frac{1}{x}\sum_{2\le n\le x}f(P_1(n))$ and $\frac{1}{x}\sum_{2\le n\le x}f(P_2(n))$ converge to different limits, where $f(P_2(n))=0$ when $n$ is a prime power. We show that this cannot happen. In fact, whenever the first average converges, the second also converges to the same limit.

papers.title: The crossmetric tensor and the geometrical meaning of the imaginary numbers
papers.abstract: The product of two Cartesian quaternions can be written as a quadratic form based on a 4x4 matrix made of the imaginary numbers i,j,k introduced by Hamilton. We generalized this matrix to non-Cartesian bases, and showed that the matrix is made of the metric and the cross tensors. We called it crossmetric tensor. Its symbols are ia,ib,ic; they are the elementary crystallographic quaternions. We determined the crossmetric tensors for the six crystal families. We also showed that any unit crystallographic quaternion can be geometrically represented by an infinity of pairs of oriented planes intersecting along the vectorial component of the quaternion such that the angle between them is the semiangle of the rotation. The composition of quaternions follows the intuitive source-target rule. The elementary quaternions ia,ib,ic are geometrically represented by pair of perpendicular and oriented planes intersecting along the axis a,b,c, respectively. Three other complementary quaternions were also introduced. They are the pairs of planes ma, mb, mc. The elementary quaternions follow Hamilton rules on the squares of imaginary numbers. The complementary quaternions follow Hamilton rules on the bi and tri-products. For Cartesian basis, the quaternions i,j,k appear as a specific case of crystallographic quaternions. They are formed by the pairs of perpendicular faces of the cube mx, my, mz.

papers.title: A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
papers.abstract: We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by Tartar's vision of a point-free theory, we derive explicit norm resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting technique and a flux corrector obtained by inverting the microscopic derivative on the residual field; this controls the error for regular macroscopic data in terms of explicit, $\varepsilon$-independent operator norms. This abstract perspective places on one footing stationary, non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions between these media---and their respective convergence rates---are captured by the behavior of the spectral measure of the microscopic derivative operator, evaluated on the residual field, near zero frequency; in the periodic case the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ is proved, while in the stochastic case the rates are conditional on a density-of-states hypothesis. Furthermore, our results apply for multiscale systems that do not uphold subadditivity of energy quantities or do not have a well-defined Brillouin zone.

papers.title: A sharp almost sure upper bound for partial sums of random multiplicative functions
papers.abstract: We prove that, for either a Steinhaus random multiplicative function or a Rademacher random multiplicative function $f$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, almost surely $|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)|\ll_{\varepsilon,f}\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}$. Together with Harper's almost sure lower bound, this determines the sharp logarithmic exponent in both models. This settles Harper's conjecture on the large fluctuations of random multiplicative functions.

papers.title: Strong convergence of Euler-Maruyama schemes for additive fractional SDEs with Lipschitz drift
papers.abstract: We study the strong convergence rate of the Euler--Maruyama scheme for additive stochastic differential equations driven by a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1)$. Assuming the drift coefficient to be Lipschitz continuous, we establish strong convergence bounds of order $1$ if $H\in(1/2,1)$, and $1/2+H-\varepsilon$, for any $\varepsilon>0$, if $H\in(0,1/2]$. The main ingredient is a shifted stochastic sewing argument, which exploits the conditional Gaussian structure of fractional Brownian motion to control the noise discretization error.

papers.title: Neural-Manifold Primal-Dual Model Order Reduction and Hyper-Reduction for Nonlinear Parametric Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: We propose a model order reduction framework for nonlinear parametrized variational inequalities arising in computational mechanics. The high-dimensional model is written in mixed primal-dual form with projection-based complementarity conditions, leading to nonlinear nonsmooth algebraic systems solved by a semi-smooth Newton method. On this basis, reduced models are constructed by proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of both primal and dual solution snapshots. To address cases where low-dimensional linear spaces provide limited approximation efficiency, we introduce a neural-network-augmented reduced model. Two feedforward networks learn corrections in the truncated POD coordinates of the primal and dual variables from solutions of enlarged Galerkin ROMs. The learned reconstructions enter the coupled equilibrium and constraint equations directly, defining a nonlinear reduced system solved by approximate semi-smooth Newton iterations. The online cost associated with high-dimensional residual evaluations is reduced through hyper-reduction, using a sparse cubature approach based on greedy nonnegative least squares. The proposed methodology is assessed on two nonlinear variational inequalities with distinct sources of nonlinearity: a two-dimensional obstacle problem with a cubic nonlinearity in the state equation, and a three-dimensional frictional contact problem in which the Coulomb law induces a nonlinear projection in the constraint equation. Numerical results compare the high-dimensional model, the linear reduced model, the neural-network-augmented reduced model, and their hyper-reduced variants, demonstrating accurate approximations with substantial reductions in online computational cost. The performance study also evaluates feasibility over the complete constraint set and measures how errors in the reconstructed obstacle and contact forces affect the primal response.

papers.title: A complete solution to the Boots-Royle/Cao-Vince conjecture
papers.abstract: Boots and Royle, and independently Cao and Vince, conjectured that the join of an edge and a path on $n-2$ vertices is the unique planar graph of maximum adjacency spectral radius for $n\geq 9$. Tait and Tobin (JCTB, 2017) proved the conjecture for sufficiently large order. In this paper, we completely resolved the Boots-Royle/Cao-Vince conjecture.

papers.title: Admissible bases and generic lattice ideals
papers.abstract: Let $L\subseteq\mathbb Z^4$ be a rank-three lattice possessing an admissible basis, and let $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_4]$ be the polynomial ring over a field $K$. We show that the associated lattice ideal $I_L \subset S$ is generic and that $S/I_L$ is a Cohen--Macaulay ring. We also identify the neighbors of the origin in $L$ and the indispensable binomials of $I_L$. Moreover, we prove that the Betti numbers of $S/I_L$ are $β_0(S/I_L)=1$, $β_1(S/I_L)=7$, $β_2(S/I_L)=12$, and $β_3(S/I_L)=6$. In addition, we show that $I_L$ is a set-theoretic complete intersection over an arbitrary field.

papers.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
papers.abstract: The running-time distribution of a randomized algorithm is computed under independent randomness, but independence is rarely what a source guarantees. We study sources $ν$ satisfying $ν[w]\le DP[w]^s$ for every finite prefix $w$ of the random tape, where $P$ is an independent reference law, $0<s\le1$, and $D\ge1$; individual choices may be predictable, even determined by the past. The worst-case probability of any closed tape event $E$ is exactly $\min\{1,DC_s(E)\}$, where $C_s(E)$ is the infimum cost of covering $E$ by prefixes of varying depth, a tree max-flow/min-cut identity that makes worst-case survival probabilities exact and optimizable over the algorithm's choices. Three applications follow. For $n$ tasks on one machine, each retried until the next random symbol lies in its success set, every schedule has the same makespan distribution under independent randomness, yet under our constraint two fixed orders miss a linear deadline with worst-case probabilities $1$ and $\exp[-Θ(n)]$; a static priority rule is optimal at every deadline. For the standard local walk on a $k$-CNF with an assignment that satisfies a majority of each clause, we determine the sharp source threshold $s_*$. Below $s_*$, on some instances a single admissible source forces nontermination however clauses are selected; at $s_*$, with fixed $D$, the expected number of flips is at most cubic in the initial Hamming distance, against linear under independence, with matching worst-case instances; and any fixed margin above $s_*$ restores linear dependence on the distance. Third, verified backtracking for noisy predecessor search remains correct under a sufficiently strong bound on the comparison errors. In every setting the algorithm may also restart, which supplies no fresh randomness; restarting restores exponential tails exactly when the nontermination event has a prefix cover of cost below one.

papers.title: Twisted Yangians of split types BI, CI, DI and Drinfeld type current relations
papers.abstract: We study twisted Yangians associated with the split symmetric pairs of types BI, CI and DI. We introduce a new presentation of these algebras, which we call the transposed presentation, governed by a twisted reflection equation that interacts naturally with the Gaussian decomposition of the generating matrix. Working entirely within the $R$-matrix presentation, we derive Drinfeld-type current presentations of the special twisted Yangian $SY^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ and of the extended twisted Yangian $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$, in which the Serre relations are stated in a closed current form. Extracting coefficients recovers the Drinfeld presentation of Lu, Wang and Zhang, in the normalisation of Lu. As a consequence, we establish an explicit isomorphism between the $R$-matrix and Drinfeld presentations conjectured by Lu, Wang and Zhang. As a byproduct, we obtain a tensor product decomposition of $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ into the twisted Yangian in the Drinfeld presentation and a polynomial ring in countably many central variables. We also obtain Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt bases in the Drinfeld generators and the coideal coproduct on the low Drinfeld modes at all but the last node.

papers.title: Survey on periodic vortex patches
papers.abstract: This survey revisits classical results on the existence of periodic solutions in incompressible fluid dynamics. Owing to the breadth of the subject, we restrict our attention to the simplest and most illustrative framework: the two-dimensional Euler equations and vortex patch solutions. The aim is not to present new results, but rather to provide a unified and streamlined exposition of several classical constructions by combining ideas from the original works with more recent developments.

papers.title: $π$-Properties, Uniformly Convexity and Uniform Ball Coverings Properties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a sufficient condition for the uniform ball-covering property of closed operator subspaces invariant under selected truncations. We use uniform convexity of the range space and near-contractive finite-rank projection approximations to obtain quantitative coverings with finite-rank centres whenever the truncated images are separable. A weak-star version gives the same covering parameters for quotients by arbitrary weak-star closed subspaces. In the completely bounded setting, the covering parameters are independent of the matrix level. In particular, the duals of all closed subspaces of $S_1(\ell_2)$ admit coverings with centre norm $2$ and radius $1+\varepsilon$, for $0<\varepsilon<1$, at every matrix level. Applications include operator-valued Schur multipliers and, for $1<p<\infty$, prescribed-support Fourier multipliers on countable amenable groups and finitely generated free groups. The Fourier coverings have finite-support centres in the given operator or completely bounded norms. An endpoint example shows failure of the ball-covering property at $p=1,\infty$.

papers.title: The Dirac equation in (split-)octonions: origins, variants, and modern context
papers.abstract: Octonions and split-octonions have been used to express the Dirac equation in physics in several conceptually distinct ways. This review organizes them into four groups: the 2-factor, 3-factor, and projection representations, which use (split-)octonion basis elements natively to model a spacetime basis, and the conventional use of octonions to carry Dirac algebra acting on spinors. For each group we identify the originating construction, relate later variants to it, and point to modern applications and to recent methods for native split-octonionic analysis. Because the multiplication table of the (split-)octonions is not unique, forms that look different in print can coincide after a norm-preserving linear isometry and a multiplication-preserving change of basis; we make such relations explicit and tabulate the basis conventions used across select sources. The 2-factor representation is treated in most detail: we document its origin and show that a recently proposed split-octonionic Dirac equation coincides with it after such an isometry and change of basis, while crediting the independent contributions of that work.

papers.title: Involution-equivariant topological recursion and mirror symmetry for the affine binary dihedral Calabi--Yau threefold
papers.abstract: We prove a closed-string remodeling statement for the affine binary dihedral Calabi--Yau orbifold threefold $\mathcal X=[\mathbb C^2/Γ]\times\mathbb C$, where $Γ$ is a binary dihedral subgroup of $SU(2)$. This target lies outside the toric setting of the Bouchard--Klemm--Mariño--Pasquetti remodeling conjecture: the toric mirror curve is replaced by the type-$D_l$ relativistic Toda curve of Brini--Ma--Strachan, and the Chekhov--Eynard--Orantin topological recursion is replaced by the $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant topological recursion of Giacchetto--Kramer--Lewański, run in the sign sector of the Toda-curve involution with the Prym kernel as its two-point input. We identify the equivariant orbifold quantum cohomology Frobenius manifold of $\mathcal X$ with the invariant Jacobian Frobenius structure of the Toda curve, and we prove that the B-model $R$-matrix, defined by regularized stationary phase, equals the A-side normalized canonical Givental--Teleman $R$-matrix on a chosen simply connected domain; this equality is anchored at the orbifold point through a semistable degeneration of the Toda curve. Comparing the resulting Givental--Teleman and Dunin-Barkowski--Orantin--Shadrin--Spitz graph sums then identifies, after a parity-twisted leaf substitution, the sign-sector recursion with the descendant Gromov--Witten generating functions of $\mathcal X$ in the stable range ($2g-2+n>0$ with $n>0$), and identifies the recursion free energies with the equivariant Gromov--Witten free energies of $\mathcal X$ for $g\geq2$. We also match the genus-one potential defined by the reduced calibrated tau function with the Gromov--Witten potential up to an additive constant.

papers.title: The Randomized BH Procedure: A Generalized Framework Encompassing Conformal and Competition Tests
papers.abstract: We propose the Randomized BH procedure, a generalized framework that introduces randomization into the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure for false discovery rate (FDR) control. We show that the classical BH procedure as well as two recently developed families of null-distribution-free methods, competition tests and conformal tests, share a common theoretical foundation and arise as special cases of this framework. The Randomized BH relaxes the classical conditions required for FDR control, frees conformal tests from the strict exchangeability assumption while allowing calibration sets to be constructed via pre-screening, and enables competition tests to be analyzed through the well-developed theory of p-values. We illustrate the framework through two applications. The first is a deeper analysis of compound p-values through the lens of randomization. The second is a general approach for integrating distributed multiple testing problems while maintaining global FDR control. Numerical simulations confirm the validity of our theoretical results.

papers.title: Iwasawa invariants of sharp/flat $2$-adic $L$-functions for quadratic twists of elliptic curves
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to study the variation under quadratic twists of the analytic Iwasawa invariants of Sprung's sharp/flat 2-adic $L$-functions for elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good supersingular reduction at $2$. Under the hypothesis that the $μ$-invariant vanishes, we obtain an explicit formula for the sharp/flat $λ$-invariants. This formula gives a supersingular analogue of Matsuno's formula in the good ordinary case. As an application, we show that the sharp/flat $λ$-invariants can be made arbitrarily large even among quadratic twists by single primes. Moreover, using the method of Hatley-Ray, we obtain an asymptotic lower bound for the number of quadratic twists with a prescribed sharp/flat 2-adic Iwasawa $λ$-invariant.

papers.title: Asynchronous Sensitivity-Based Distributed NMPC
papers.abstract: This paper presents a cooperative distributed model predictive control (MPC) scheme for nonlinear continuous-time systems. The centralized optimal control problem is solved asynchronously via a fixed number of sensitivity-based distributed programming (SBDP) iterations. The proposed scheme requires only neighbor-to-neighbor communication and no synchronization between agents during optimization. Under nominal MPC stability and bounded information delay, local exponential stability is established for a sufficiently large number of per-agent SBDP iterations. Numerical and hardware-in-the-loop results on both Ethernet and Wi-Fi demonstrate the benefits of an asynchronous execution, reducing execution times by over 60% while maintaining comparable closed loop performance.

papers.title: Degree growth, orbit graphs, and functoriality for birational dynamical systems
papers.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to give a natural divisor-theoretic formulation of the counting method introduced by Halburd for computing degree growth, in a form applicable to birational dynamical systems on varieties of arbitrary dimension. Instead of counting only preimages of special values, we follow time-indexed divisorial conditions through singularity patterns. These conditions are recorded on normalized finite-window orbit graphs, where the relevant multiplicities are realized as divisorial valuations of pullbacks of time-indexed divisors. This construction explains how the elementary computations appearing in singularity patterns can be interpreted as degree relations on a single normal variety. We then show that further relations arise from the failure of functoriality of pullbacks: when the center of a divisor enters the relevant indeterminacy locus, a degree-drop divisor appears. Under suitable finite-type assumptions, the two kinds of relations lead to closed linear difference systems governing degree sequences. Several examples, including higher-dimensional ones, demonstrate that the two mechanisms are complementary and that their combination determines the degree growth in cases where either mechanism alone is insufficient.

papers.title: How to Untwist Twisted Gauge Fields
papers.abstract: This paper provides an isomorphism between the space of twisted gauge fields on a principal bundle $\mathcal{P}(M,H)$ and the space of standard gauge fields on a different principal bundle $\mathcal{Q}(M,G)$ associated to $\mathcal{P}$. This isomorphism extends to local fields on the base manifold, which enables the use of local twisted fields in standard gauge theories (e.g. Yang-Mills-like theories). This allows one to deal with two symmetry groups, coming from $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$, respectively. The construction makes use of a larger principal bundle $\mathcal{S}$ which has $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ as quotient bundles. $\mathcal{S}$ is a Hilsum-Skandalis bibundle between the action groupoids $H\ltimes\mathcal{P}$ and $G\ltimes\mathcal{Q}$. The gauge structure on $\mathcal{S}$ encodes both standard and twisted gauge structures on $\mathcal{P}$. In addition, the isomorphism classes of bundles $\mathcal{S}$ up to an isomorphism covering the identity map on $\mathcal{P}$ are in 1:1 correspondence with the equivalence classes of cocycles (up to a coboundary). This paper also provides a new interpretation of (full) dressing fields as dynamic (or active) sections of a principal bundle.

papers.title: Neural-Spectral and Newton-HUM Methods for Reconstructing Controls of Wave Equations
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for constructing and rigorously validating controls for semilinear wave equations with localized interior control. We analyze the continuous energy-space problem and certify exact control for finite-dimensional Galerkin systems. Under explicit smallness and neighborhood conditions, our a posteriori theorem proves the existence of an exact Galerkin control near a computed candidate. It combines a validated terminal-state error, a bounded right inverse of the derivative of the control-to-terminal-state map, and a Lipschitz bound for that derivative. Under additional uniform right-inverse and neighborhood conditions, we also show that Newton correction converges with quadratic decay of terminal-state errors. We use residual estimates and interval arithmetic to enclose the nonlinear trajectory and its linearized controllability Gramian. For the specified eight-mode tanh problem, we rigorously bound a source-response operator to prove contraction of the exact source-frozen iteration. We compare deterministic controls based on the Hilbert Uniqueness Method with neural approximations of temporal modal coefficients. Two Newton corrections reduce the computed terminal-state errors of all six tested neural candidates below $10^{-8}$. For the three certified candidates, we obtain smaller bounds on the distance to an exact Galerkin steering control by refining the validation mesh while keeping the computed controls fixed.

papers.title: Strong counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture in every uniformity
papers.abstract: The supersaturation problem asks, for a fixed $r$-graph $\mathcal F$, for the minimum number of copies of $\mathcal F$ in an $n$-vertex $r$-graph with $\ex(n,\mathcal F)+q$ edges. Mubayi conjectured a local form of supersaturation under a stability hypothesis: if $\mathcal F$ is non-$r$-partite and stable, meaning roughly that the extremal $\mathcal F$-free construction is unique and all near-extremal $\mathcal F$-free $r$-graphs are close to it, then this minimum should be at least $q c(n,\mathcal F)$, where $c(n,\mathcal F)$ is the minimum number of copies created by adding one edge to the extremal $\mathcal F$-free $r$-graph. We disprove this conjectured local lower bound in the strongest possible quantitative sense that the ratio to the conjectured lower bound can be made arbitrarily small. More precisely, for every $r\ge2$ and every $K>1$, we construct a stable non-$r$-partite $r$-graph $\mathcal F$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and every $1\le q\leδn$, there is an $n$-vertex $r$-graph with $\ex(n,\mathcal F)+q$ edges containing at most $K^{-1}q c(n,\mathcal F)$ copies of $\mathcal F$. This arbitrarily large failure already occurs when $q=1$.

papers.title: Ubiquity in the setting of forward-reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequalities
papers.abstract: The ubiquity of geometric Brascamp-Lieb data, which refers to a certain density property of geometric data within the set of all feasible Brascamp-Lieb data, has recently been studied. Motivated in part by a question of Bennett-Tao concerning a possible connection or analogue of the adjoint Brascamp-Lieb inequality to the forward-reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality, we establish ubiquity in the forward-reverse setting. Our proof takes an analytic approach and, to overcome the difficulties arising in extending ubiquity to the forward-reverse setting, makes use of tools from the calculus of variations such as Danskin's theorem and Ekeland's variational principle.

papers.title: High-Order Invariant-Domain Preserving Continuous Finite Elements via Graph-Poisson Convex Limiting
papers.abstract: We develop a high-order, locally conservative, invariant-domain preserving continuous finite element method for nonlinear scalar conservation laws. A first-order graph-viscosity scheme is built on the fine-$\mathbb P_1$ submesh induced by the high-order nodes, so that it remains compact and has positive lumped masses for every polynomial degree, while the high-order candidate can be any stabilized Galerkin method; here we use residual-based artificial viscosity and continuous interior penalty methods. The two updates conserve different discrete masses, and comparing each in its own conserved measure gives a nodal difference with zero sum, which a graph-Poisson problem represents as antisymmetric edge fluxes. For polynomial degrees with positive $\mathbb P_k$ lumped masses (e.g., $\mathbb P_1$, $\mathbb P_3$, $\mathbb P_5$ on triangles), convex limiting of these fluxes conserves the $\mathbb P_k$ mass exactly and in local flux form. For degrees with zero or negative lumped masses (e.g., $\mathbb P_2$, $\mathbb P_4$), limiting perturbs the mass only on the elements where it acts, and this perturbation is removed inside each such element without violating the bounds, exactly whenever the element has enough room within its bounds. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy for smooth solutions, robustness near discontinuities, and agreement with the entropy solution on standard benchmarks.

papers.title: The conditional expectation of the product of the first $n-1$ Hermite polynomials in a multivariate normal distribution with respect to the $n$-th variable. A fresh perspective on the Kibble-Slepian formula
papers.abstract: We calculate the conditional expectation of $\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}H_{k_{j}}% (X_{j})$ given $X_{n}=z,$ if random vector $(X_{1},\ldots,X_{n})^{T}$ has multivariate normal distribution and $H_{n}(x)$ denotes $n$-th Hermite polynomial. This expectation is a polynomial in $z$ of order $\sum_{j=1}% ^{n-1}k_{j}$. Our formula has an iterative form with respect to $n$. We also present some auxiliary observations concerning the expansion of the density of the $n$-dimensional normal distribution in the series of the Hermite polynomials. Mostly concerning the properties of the coefficients of this expansion. To perform these calculations, we give a few auxiliary formulas concerning Hermite polynomials and multivariate normal distributions. We apply this result to obtain exact, simple forms of these expansions for $n=2$ and $3$, thus looking at known results from a different perspective. We believe that the results can be very useful in Probability Theory, in particular in the Theory of distributions, Statistics, and the Theory of Stochastic Processes, in particular Gaussian ones.

papers.title: The algebraic K-theory of $k[\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$
papers.abstract: We compute via trace methods the higher algebraic $K$-theory of the group ring $k[\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$, as well as the related groups $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, $\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, and $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, where $k$ is a finite field of characteristic $p$ and $q=p^r$. At the core of the computation is the algebraic $K$-theory of the group ring of the Sylow $p$-subgroup, $k[C_p^r]$, which we determine via a theorem of Lück--Reich--Rognes--Varisco on cyclic assembly for topological cyclic homology. In the process, we reprove the cyclic assembly result in the language of Nikolaus--Scholze, analyse assembly for smaller families of subgroups, and develop further tools for computing topological cyclic homology of group rings.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for coupled stiff transport systems
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) struggle with stiff, regime-changing transport equations due to instability, loss imbalance, and violations of physical consistency. This paper investigates these failures through the Marshak wave equations, a canonical benchmark from radiative transport, where initial and boundary conditions differ by up to 12 orders of magnitude, and proposes modifications to the standard PINN framework to overcome them. Three modifications are introduced: a ScaledSigmoid final activation enforcing physical bounds and positivity of the unknowns; a logarithmic MSE loss replacing the standard quadratic loss for initial and boundary conditions, enabling training across extreme scale disparities; and explicit enforcement of global conservation laws as an additional physics loss term. Monte Carlo sampling with exponential time weighting is used throughout.
