The proposed framework recovers the Marshak wave dynamics - including the hot, cold, and wave-front regions - in good agreement with a reference Implicit Monte Carlo solution (sub-millimeter absolute error on the front position, although the relative error remains substantial at early times), with run times under 5 minutes. Ablation studies confirm that each ingredient is essential: linear activation, absence of the logarithmic loss, or removal of the PDE term each independently cause the method to fail qualitatively. This work identifies and resolves three concrete failure modes of standard PINN on stiff hyperbolic systems with nonlinear coupling. The combination of bounded activations, scale-aware loss functions, and conservation law enforcement constitutes a framework validated on the present one-dimensional Marshak wave problem, with potential extension to other coupled stiff transport systems in engineering.

papers.title: The $p$--Bloch--Carleson measure problem for $0<p<\infty$: A complete characterization via Carleson tents
papers.abstract: We characterize the boundedness and compactness of the embedding $$ \operatorname{id}:\mathcal B \longrightarrow L^p(μ),\qquad 0<p<\infty, $$ where $\mathcal B$ denotes the Bloch space and $μ$ is a positive Borel measure on the unit disc. The criteria depend only on the dyadic Carleson tents. These results refine our earlier $L^2(μ)$ characterization based on a full dyadic resolution of the disc and extend it to all positive exponents. The proof combines discretization on Carleson tents, representations of Bloch functions by series of analytic polynomials, and weighted matrix estimates. We also obtain corresponding boundedness and compactness characterizations for $$ \textrm{id}:\mathcal Q_p\longrightarrow L^q(μ),\qquad 0<p\le1,\quad 0<q<\infty. $$ These results resolve the general $p$--Bloch--Carleson measure problem studied by Girela, Peláez, Pérez-González and Rättyä in 2008.

papers.title: On Perfectoidization of Finite Algebras over a Perfectoid Ring
papers.abstract: We study general properties of the perfectoidization of finite algebras over a perfectoid ring, which helps to understand some precise and explicit descriptions. For example, we prove that if $A=R[t]/(m(t))$ where $m(t)$ is monic, $R$ is perfectoid and the discriminant $d$ of $m(t)$ is a non-zero divisor of $R$ satisfying a bounded torsion condition, then $dA_{\mathrm{pfd}}\subset A$. We also prove a density criterion reducing the construction of the perfectoidization to adjoining suitable $p$-power roots modulo $p$. In the second part of the paper, we compute perfectoidizations in several families of examples, including Kummer-type extensions and split finite algebras.

papers.title: Invariant measures for the one-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes-Korteweg equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the long-time behaviour of a one-dimensional compressible viscous fluid with general capillarity and density dependent viscosity, driven by a stochastic force. In particular, we prove the existence of invariant measures by applying the Krylov-Bogoliubov method in a setting where the dynamics is supported on a non-complete phase space. This analysis is further enhanced by the derivation of a refined stability result determining the continuous dependence with respect to the initial data. The present paper exhibits some properties and results for Korteweg fluids which are not known in absence of the capillarity tensor. In particular, we prove that the Markov semigroup associated with strong solutions is Feller and we can consider ranges of the adiabatic and viscosity exponents $γ$ and $α$ larger than those available in the current ergodic literature for compressible fluids. Also the interplay between the choice of the physical domain and the use of a damping term is discussed.

papers.title: Decomposition Theorem for Perfectoid Rings along General Ideals
papers.abstract: Using André's lemma and the excision square for perfectoidization coming from $p$-complete arc descent, we prove new structural results about perfectoid rings and perfectoidization. The main result is a tameness theorem for torsion in perfectoid rings: if $R$ is a perfectoid ring and $I\subset R$ is an ideal, then the $I$-torsion in $R$ is $I_{\mathrm{perfd}}$-almost zero. This yields an excision-type decomposition of $R$ along its $I$-torsion part. We also study (semi)perfectoid rings and perfectoid ideals and take the opportunity to make some structural remarks about them.

papers.title: Differentiable FEM versus PINN for pavement layer inverse analysis: enforcing physics as hard or soft constraints
papers.abstract: Automatic-differentiation-based inverse analysis methods, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and differentiable programming, have recently shown great promise due to their ability to compute accurate gradients and convergence efficiency. However, their applicability to falling weight deflectometer (FWD) backcalculation remains unexplored. This study critically evaluates PINN-based inverse analysis for a multilayer pavement system and investigates differentiable finite element method (DiffFEM) as an alternative based on a synthetic benchmark. The standard PINN does not recover layer moduli because of the sharp domain discontinuities inherent to layered pavement systems. Although we use an extended PINN with domain decomposition (XPINN), which shows better performance on discontinuous domains, its performance remains highly sensitive to loss weighting and network architecture, and degrades under measurement noise. By contrast, DiffFEM consistently achieves more accurate, stable, and computationally efficient inversion results. These results show and quantify the expected advantage of DiffFEM, which enforces the governing physics as a hard constraint in the solver, over PINN-based approaches, where the governing physics is imposed as a soft constraint through the loss function. More broadly, the findings suggest that the choice between PINN- and DiffFEM-based inverse analysis needs careful consideration, with DiffFEM offering practical advantages when an efficient and robust differentiable forward solver is available.

papers.title: Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Unlike classical optimal transport, weak transport costs depend nonlinearly on the conditional law of couplings. This feature is essential in problems involving barycenter, conditional moments, and martingale-type constraints. Meanwhile, such conditional dependence makes ordinary Wasserstein geometry insufficient and calls instead for an adapted Wasserstein viewpoint. In this paper, we investigate the entropy-regularized weak optimal transport via gradient flows in adapted Wasserstein space. We derive, from the formal tangent structure of adapted Wasserstein space and the projection onto the set of couplings with prescribed marginals, a coupled McKean--Vlasov SDE. A novel and subtle term is a projection that, at each $Y$-location, averages a weak-transport force that already depends on the conditional law of $Y$ given $X$, thereby preserving marginals while retaining the nonlinear weak-transport structure. Under mild integrability and regularity assumptions, we prove weak existence and uniqueness in law for this projected McKean--Vlasov equation. We then prove that the flow converges, in the adapted Wasserstein topology, to the unique minimizer of the entropic weak optimal transport problem. We also describe a particle approximation and illustrate the dynamics on optimal transport and martingale optimal transport examples.

papers.title: Free maps in critical dimension on low-dimensional tori and closed surfaces
papers.abstract: We present a method to build free immersions in critical dimension on $m$-tori for $m = 2, 3, 4, 5$ by using a factorization trick inspired by tori immersions in critical dimension. As an application, we show that the set of smooth free maps from a closed surface $M$ to $\mathbb R^5$ is nonempty. In particular, every closed surface embeds freely in $\mathbb R^5$. Finally, we find the homotopy invariants of free maps in our environment and study which invariants are achieved by our maps.

papers.title: Quasihelix properties of selected Volterra Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: We study local quasihelix and generalized quasihelix properties of several Gaussian Volterra processes with tempered, power-weighted, and logarithmic kernels, including tempered fractional Brownian motions and generalized fractional Brownian motion-type processes. These properties depend significantly on the values of the parameters involved, and we consider all possible cases in detail.

papers.title: Representation theory of the real Gelfand order and real Harish-Chandra modules for $\mathsf{SL}_2(\mathbbm{R})$
papers.abstract: In this article we study the principal block of the category of real Harish-Chandra modules for the group $\mathsf{SL}_2(\RR)$ and relate it to the category of finite dimensional modules over the so-called real Gelfand order. We describe several distinguished classes of the corresponding indecomposable representations.

papers.title: Analytical and numerical study of nonlinear Riesz-Caputo boundary value problems
papers.abstract: Fractional boundary value problems are often used to model complex systems and processes characterized by memory effects and anomalous diffusion. In this paper, we consider nonlinear fractional boundary value problems of arbitrary order α involving the Riesz-Caputo operator, which is particularly suited for modelling physical phenomena exhibiting symmetric diffusive effects. By reducing the problem to a dominant singular integral equation of Cauchy type and inverting it in closed form, we derive an integral representation of the solution, which we use to prove existence and uniqueness. The closed-form inversion also describes the typical behaviour of the solution near the endpoints of the interval and provides an exact singular solution, which we use as a test case. We then analyse a B-spline collocation method for the approximation of the solution, proving its convergence and illustrating it by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Euclidean distance degree defect of singular projective varieties
papers.abstract: The unit Euclidean distance degree and the generic Euclidean distance degree are two well-studied invariants of projective varieties. These quantities measure the algebraic complexity of nearest-point problems on a variety, and in many examples arising in optimization, engineering, statistics, and data science, there is a significant gap between them. We refer to this difference as the defect of the Euclidean distance (ED) degree. In this paper, we provide a constructible enhancement and a topological formula for the defect of the ED degree of an arbitrary complex projective variety, extending our previous results from the smooth setting. Since the generic Euclidean distance degree is typically more tractable, our approach offers a new method for computing ED degrees in broad generality.

papers.title: Generalized Wasserstein Flow Matching: Nested Couplings for Point Cloud Generation
papers.abstract: We formulate flow matching on probability measures over probability measures. Directly from the Wasserstein-on-Wasserstein (WoW) continuity equation, we show that admissible nested outer and inner couplings induce a valid metameasure flow and non-local velocity field. Validity requires neither optimal plans nor a smooth manifold. Practically, this opens up the design space of multisample flow matching: exact Wasserstein plans are distinguished by energy and straightness, while sliced and lazy linear plans yield scalable alternatives. Point-cloud experiments, including controlled Bures-Wasserstein and Euclidean minibatch baselines, demonstrate the resulting geometry-cost trade-off.

papers.title: Cross-validated feature selection using least-squares support vector machines for binary classification
papers.abstract: Support vector machines (SVMs) are widely used for binary classification. However, irrelevant or redundant features can degrade classification accuracy and model interpretability, making feature selection important for SVMs. Most SVM feature selection methods rely on sequential search or regularization and do not directly identify the best feature subset. Mixed-integer optimization (MIO) is a direct approach to best subset selection. Cross-validation (CV) is broadly applicable to feature selection because it evaluates predictive performance on validation data without model assumptions. Although Purcaru et al. (2026) proposed an MIO formulation for CV-based linear-SVM feature selection (SVM-CV), this method suffers from high computational cost. We develop computationally efficient CV-based MIO formulations for feature selection in linear SVM classification by using least squares support vector machines (LS-SVMs). We formulate the problem as a bilevel MIO problem, where the lower-level problem trains LS-SVM classifiers and the upper-level problem selects features based on validation sets. We then reformulate it as a single-level MIO problem by exploiting the optimality conditions of LS-SVM. We propose two formulations: a hinge-loss-based validation model and a least-squares-based validation model. We compare our methods with SVM-CV and other SVM-based and logistic-regression-based methods through simulation experiments on synthetic data. The hinge-loss-based validation model attained high feature selection accuracy under the high-noise and moderate-noise conditions, particularly with more candidate features, and the least-squares-based validation model performed well in feature selection under the low-noise condition at the lower correlation level. Furthermore, our two models achieved substantially faster computation than the existing SVM-CV model.

papers.title: PREFER: Personalized Review Summarization with Online Preference Learning
papers.abstract: Product reviews significantly influence purchasing decisions on e-commerce platforms. However, the sheer volume of reviews can overwhelm users, obscuring information most relevant to their individual needs. Existing e-commerce summarization systems typically produce generic, static summaries that fail to account for the fact that (i) different users prioritize different product characteristics, and (ii) these preferences may evolve with interactions. To address these challenges, we propose an online learning framework that generates personalized summaries for each user by representing user interests in a latent aspect space and selecting preference-aligned review evidence. Our system then iteratively refines its understanding of user preferences by incorporating feedback on the generated summaries directly over time. We evaluate our framework on Amazon Reviews'23 using controlled feedback simulations and robustness checks with held-out-history, independent-embedding, and external LLM-based evaluators. These experiments show improvements in preference-aligned evidence selection under the evaluated feedback settings. A separate human-based study finds that scenario-conditioned summaries are preferred over generic (uniformly-aggregated) alternatives in 69.9% of paired comparisons.

papers.title: Numerical study of the 2D Kaup-Broer-Kuperschmidt Boussinesq system
papers.abstract: In this work we consider the well posed version of the Kaup-Broer-Kuperschmidt system in two dimensions. We numerically construct soliton type solutions and show that they are unstable both against dispersion and singularity formation. Further, we study line solitons and their stability, as well as generally localised initial data. In either case we fail to find stable structures.

papers.title: On the Architectural Complexity of Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We introduce a unified theoretical framework for the rigorous analysis and systematic construction of deep neural networks (DNNs). This framework addresses a gap in existing theory by explicitly modeling the structure of tensor operations -- lower level information that is often abstracted. Our framework enables two novel objectives: (1) analysis of the evolution of architectural complexity over deep learning history, and (2) automatic construction of novel architectures based on new types of tensor operations. Our study of DNNs introduced over the past 40 years reveals a connection between groundbreaking architectures and increases in different types of architectural complexity. Moreover, we identify several large classes of higher complexity architectures that have not yet been explored. We then collect a dataset of 3,000+ higher complexity architectures, which we publicly release at: https://github.com/combinatoriallabs/ArchitecturalComplexity.

papers.title: Generalization of Zeroth-Order Method for Quotients of Quadratic Functions
papers.abstract: Optimization of quadratic functions and their quotients is relevant in subspace and iterative optimization methods. In this paper, we consider the matrix-free computation of the generalized operator norm and the maximization of a generalized Rayleigh quotient when only forward evaluations of two linear operators $A$ and $B$ are available. The proposed method samples search directions uniformly from the full unit sphere, thereby avoiding tangent-space sampling and explicit access to the metric matrix $B^{\mathrm T}B$. The exact line search along each sampled direction reduces to a $2\times2$ generalized eigenvalue problem on specific Gram matrices. In the generic case its maximizing step has a closed form. We prove that the objective values converge almost surely to the largest generalized eigenvalue and that the distance of the iterates to the leading generalized eigenspace converges to zero. We also relate full-sphere moment estimators to the Riemannian gradient and Hessian. The numerical experiments on synthetic Gaußian operators illustrate the behavior of the methods, and further studies of the proposed algorithms indicate favorable empirical convergence and weak dependence on the tested problem dimensions.

papers.title: Distributed Optimization with Nesterov Momentum and Finite-Time Quantized Averaging over Directed Networks: Extended Version
papers.abstract: In modern large-scale networked systems, rapidly solving optimization problems while utilizing communication resources efficiently is critical for addressing complex tasks. However, distributed optimization over bandwidth-limited networks must cope with two obstacles: limited-bandwidth communication, and slow convergence when the objective is ill-conditioned. In this paper, we consider unconstrained distributed optimization over strongly connected directed networks, where nodes exchange quantized (i.e., compressed) messages. We propose QANM (Quantized Averaged Nesterov Momentum), an algorithm that combines Nesterov momentum with a finite-time quantized averaging protocol. At every iteration, QANM enables all nodes to reach exact agreement, without requiring doubly stochastic weight matrices or undirected communication. For strongly convex and smooth objectives, we show that the objective gap of QANM decays at the accelerated rate $1-κ^{-1/2}$ (where $κ$ is the condition number), up to a residual of order $Δ^2$ determined by the quantization level $Δ$. This improves the condition-number dependence of the transient iteration complexity from $κ$ to $\sqrtκ$ compared with gradient descent that utilizes the same quantized averaging mechanism. Finally, we evaluate QANM on a distributed sensor fusion problem, showing that our algorithm exhibits the fastest initial error reduction compared with other methods from current literature.

papers.title: Gradient Descent's Last Iterate is Often (slightly) Suboptimal
papers.abstract: We consider the well-studied setting of minimizing a convex Lipschitz function using either gradient descent (GD) or its stochastic variant (SGD), and examine the last iterate convergence. We prove that $Θ(\sqrt{\log(T)/T})$ is the optimal anytime rate attainable with a fixed stepsize schedule (that does not depend on the total number of steps $T$). The upper bound holds already for SGD, and improves on the $\log(T)/\sqrt{T}$ rate of Shamir and Zhang [2013], as well as the $\sqrt{\log(T)/T}$ rate of Zamani and Glineur [2023] which was proven only for deterministic GD. The matching lower bound holds already for GD, and confirms the conjecture of Jain et al. [2019], namely that the optimal $1/\sqrt{T}$ rate for the last iterate cannot be obtained without prior knowledge of $T$.

papers.title: The estimates for Boolean surface area of polynomial threshold functions
papers.abstract: Polynomial threshold functions (PTFs) are an important low-complexity class of Boolean functions, with strong connections to learning theory and approximation theory. Recent work on learning and testing PTFs has exploited structural and isoperimetric properties of the class, especially bounds on average sensitivity, one of the central themes in the study of PTFs since the Gotsman--Linial conjecture recently solved by OpenAI, \cite{GLsol}. In this work we study PTFs through the lens of the Boolean surface area (or Talagrand boundary) \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]=\mathbb{E}|\nabla f|=\mathbb{E}\sqrt{s_{f}(x)}, \] a natural measure of vertex-boundary complexity on the discrete cube. Our main result is that every degree-$d$ PTF has polylogarithmic Boolean surface area: \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le C_d(\log(en))^{C_d}. \] The proof is based on the PTF Restriction Lemma of Kabanets, Kane, and Lu \cite{KKL2017} and proceeds through a tail bound for the pointwise sensitivity. In particular, it controls all subcritical fractional moments of the sensitivity. We also record a random block partition principle for Boolean surface area and an alternative recursive argument following Kane's work \cite{DK} on average sensitivity, which independently yields the second bound \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le \exp(C(d)\sqrt{\log n}). \] This bound was obtained in \cite{FSVZ} without clarifying the magnitude of $C(d)$, which we do below. For lower moments $\bE |\nabla f|^η \le C(d, η)$ there is no dependence on $n$ for $0<η<1$.

papers.title: On local solutions to time-varying linear systems
papers.abstract: This paper develops an intrinsic framework for local solutions to time-varying linear systems with real meromorphic coefficients. Local solutions on compact intervals naturally form a sheaf of vector spaces. We introduce regularity triples to distinguish regularity across singularities, one-sided regularity at singularities, and regularity away from singularities. The local formulation isolates a continuation property implicit in established global frameworks and yields a simple definition of behavioural controllability. We establish an algebraically verifiable sufficient condition for continuation, prove its necessity for controllability, and derive an algebraic characterization of controllability based on the Teichmüller-Nakayama form, recovering and slightly generalizing established results.

papers.title: Consensus-based optimization with $α$-stable jump processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a CBO method that incorporates jumps driven by an $α$-stable stochastic process within a kinetic framework. This approach naturally induces nonlocal stochastic effects, enhancing the exploration capabilities of the method. We formulate the dynamics at the particle level, providing a detailed description of the associated stochastic system and its asymptotic behavior. In particular, by means of a Fourier-based representation, we derive the corresponding fractional Fokker-Planck equation, which captures the nonlocal diffusion mechanisms generated by $α$-stable processes. As a central result, we establish a rigorous convergence analysis for the proposed method. Finally, we assess its performance through a series of numerical experiments, highlighting the effectiveness of $α$-stable jump dynamics and their advantages over standard diffusion based strategies, especially in complex optimization landscapes.

papers.title: Stabilizing the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure by randomization
papers.abstract: Extracting approximate eigenpairs from a prescribed subspace is of fundamental importance in eigenvalue computation. Although the standard Rayleigh--Ritz procedure is widely used for this purpose, it may suffer from deteriorated convergence of Ritz values and may even fail to produce convergent Ritz vectors, unless the compressed eigenvalue problem is assumed to be well-conditioned. In this paper, we address the eigenpair extraction problem by introducing a randomized Rayleigh--Ritz procedure. Our analysis shows that, for a simple eigenpair, the eigenvalue and eigenvector condition numbers of the randomly compressed generalized eigenvalue problem are, with high probability, comparable to those of the original problem, which yields a reliable approximate eigenpair from the extraction. The result also extends naturally to nonlinear eigenvalue problems.

papers.title: Sharp Riemannian heat kernel estimates on the cut locus and the Parabolic Anderson model
papers.abstract: Using sharp global heat kernel bounds and geodesic comparison geometry, we show that the Dalang condition for well-posedness of the parabolic Anderson model with measure-valued initial conditions, first introduced on Euclidean space, holds on general compact Riemannian manifolds. We furthermore establish upper and lower moment bounds for all such solutions, providing evidence for intermittency in this generality. This extends and simplifies earlier work that required non-positive curvature.

papers.title: Second order Recurrences, quadratic number fields and cyclic codes
papers.abstract: Wall-Sun-Sun primes (shortly WSS primes) are defined as those primes $p$ such that the period of the Fibonacci recurrence is the same modulo $p$ and modulo $p^2.$ This concept has been generalized recently to certain second order recurrences whose characteristic polynomials admit as a zero the principal unit of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d}),$ for some integer $d>0.$ Primes of the latter type we call $WSS(d).$ They correspond to the case when $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ is not $p$-rational. For such a prime $p$ we study the weight distributions of the cyclic codes over $\mathbb{F}_p$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$ whose check polynomial is the reciprocal of the said characteristic polynomial. Some of these codes are MDS (reducible case) or NMDS (irreducible case).

papers.title: Analytic Study of $p$-Bessel Functions: Fractional Calculus, Integral Representations, and Complex Extensions
papers.abstract: We present a systematic analytic study of the $p$-Bessel functions $\mathcal{J}_{ω,\varphi}^{[p]}$, a novel class of generalized Bessel functions arising from Fourier analysis on planar domains bounded by $p$-circles, including astroid-type shapes with $0<p\le2$ satisfying $(2/p)\in\mathbb{N}$. While previous work established Hardy-type oscillatory identities for these domains, expressing lattice point discrepancies via $p$-Bessel functions, the present paper focuses on the intrinsic analytic properties of the functions themselves. In particular, we (i) construct a hierarchical structure of $\{\mathcal{J}_{ω,\varphi}^{[p]}\}_{ω\ge0}$ using Erdélyi-Kober-type fractional derivatives, (ii) derive explicit real-analytic integral representations and obtain asymptotic formulas on the coordinate axes, and (iii) extend the functions to the complex domain through Poisson-type integral formulas. These results establish $p$-Bessel functions as genuinely new oscillatory kernels, providing a rigorous framework for studying anisotropic oscillatory phenomena and laying the analytic foundation for applications in $p$-circle lattice point problems.

papers.title: A heterogeneous nonlocal advection--diffusion system
papers.abstract: We present a self-contained investigation of the local and global well-posedness of a system of nonlocal advection--diffusion equations for a heterogeneous population over $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d \in \mathbb{N}$. Each convolution kernel $K_{ij}$, which describes the nonlocal advection of species $i$ according to the distribution of species $j$, is assumed to have its own regularity $\nabla K_{ij} \in L^{q_{ij}}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $1 < q_{ij} < \infty$. Local well-posedness of the mild solution and its regularity is obtained using semigroup theory and contraction mapping arguments. For kernels that satisfy a given interaction cycle condition, global existence is established using a Nash-type inequality to show an \textit{a priori} energy bound. For a class of kernels that need not satisfy the interaction cycle condition, a dynamical property satisfied by a normalised \(L^p\) norm of each species is used to obtain a uniform-in-time bound under a smallness condition on the initial data. An example family of kernels with varying regularities, supplemented by numerical simulations, is then considered to illustrate the theory developed in this work and how it may be generalised.

papers.title: Model Order Reduction for Parametric Hermitian Eigenvalue Problems: Local High-Order Approximation with Taylor-Reduced Basis Method
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the Taylor-reduced basis method (Taylor-RBM) for the efficient approximation of eigenspaces of large-scale parametric Hermitian matrices. The Taylor-RBM is a local model order reduction method, which constructs an approximation space by using the ranges of scaled derivatives of the spectral projector at a reference point in the parameter domain. For a prescribed order $n$, under local $\mathrm{C}^{n+1}$-regularity, we prove local convergence of orders $n+1$ and $2n+2$ for the eigenspace and the Ritz-value sum, respectively, and present a computationally efficient procedure for assembling the Taylor reduced basis space. Since this method is tightly connected to multivariate perturbation theory, we also analyze a projector approximation obtained from the finite Taylor polynomial of the eigenprojector and compare it with the Taylor-RBM.

papers.title: The extended future cover and desynchronization of sofic shifts
papers.abstract: The paper describes a cover of the future cover of a sofic shift which is canonical in the same way as the future cover itself. In some cases the cover is isomorphic to the future cover and in other it is a genuine extension. The extended future cover is then used to introduce and describe the desynchronization of sofic shifts.

papers.title: Lubin's conjecture for height-one $p$-adic dynamical systems over $p(p-1)$-tame extensions
papers.abstract: We prove Lubin's conjecture for height-one commuting pairs of formal power series defined over the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}$ of finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ whose ramification index is coprime to $p(p-1)$. For such a pair $(f, u)$, with $f$ noninvertible and $u$ invertible, we show that $(f, u)$ is a pair of endomorphisms of a formal group defined over $\mathcal{O}$. The proof relies on extracting a crystalline character of weight $1$ from the Galois set $T_f$ of $f$-consistent sequences, using it to define a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module structure on $T_f$ for which $f$ is an endomorphism, and applying explicit functors in integral $p$-adic Hodge theory to recover the latent formal group.

papers.title: Prolongation rigidity of sub-free Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that if the 0-th Tanaka prolongation $\mathfrak{g}_0=\mathfrak{der}_0(\mathfrak{m})$ of a fundamental graded nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{g}_{-s}\oplus\dots\oplus\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$ is irreducible on $\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$, then $\mathfrak{m}$ is prolongation rigid: $\text{pr}_+(\mathfrak{m})=0$. The only exceptions are given by negative gradations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of a simple Lie algebra.

papers.title: Magnetic Hardy inequalities with singular integral weights
papers.abstract: In this paper we present Hardy type inequalities for magnetic Dirichlet forms with singular integral weights. We analyze the local and global optimality of the integral weight and discuss several examples in details. An application of our results to spectral estimates for magnetic Schrödinger operators is provided as well.

papers.title: Improved well-posedness for the limit flow of differentiation of roots of polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the partial differential equation on the circle that was heuristically obtained by Steinerberger \cite{steinerberger2019nonlocal} on the real line and which represents the evolution of the density of the roots of polynomials under differentiation. After integrating the partial differential equation in question, we observe that it can be treated with the theory of viscosity solutions. This equation at hand is a non linear parabolic integro-differential equation which involves the elliptic operator called the half-Laplacian. Due to the singularity of the equation, we first restrict our study to strictly positive initial condition. We obtain a comparison principle for solutions of the primitive equation which yields uniqueness, existence, continuity with respect to initial condition. We then extend these results to general initial data. We finally prove that the system of particles on the circle introduced by Steinerberger indeed approximates the solution of the equation.

papers.title: The Hasse principle for diagonal forms restricted to a hypersurface of adjacent degree
papers.abstract: We investigate the Hasse principle for Diophantine systems consisting of one diagonal form of degree $k$ and one general form of degree $k-1$. By refining the method of Brandes and Parsell (arXiv:2003.04350) in this specific setting, we improve the bound $n > 2^k k$ to $n > 2^{k-1}(2k-1)$; in particular, the requirement $n > 24$ in the case of degrees three and two is relaxed to $n > 20$.

papers.title: A global stochastic maximum principle for delayed forward-backward stochastic control systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a delayed forward-backward stochastic control system in which all the coefficients depend on the state and control terms, and the control domain is an arbitrary nonempty set. To handle the terms involving $y$ and $z$ in the second-order expansion, we derive two decompositions of $\big(\hat{y}^\e(\cd), \hat{z}^\e(\cd)\big)$. More precisely, we use the second decomposition to handle the terms involving $f^\e_{yy}, f^\e_{yz}$ and use both decompositions to handle the term involving $f^\e_{zz}$. Finally, a global stochastic maximum principle is obtained.

papers.title: On the Dirichlet boundary value problem on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
papers.abstract: We study bounded solutions of Dirichlet boundary value problems for semilinear elliptic equations on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature. We prove nonexistence when the asymptotic boundary has zero Hausdorff measure at an exponent determined by the upper curvature bound and the spectral parameter. The result holds for continuous viscosity solutions under a one-sided bound on the nonlinearity, including the Allen-Cahn equation. The proof combines convex barriers at infinity, distance comparison for $C^{1,1}$ hypersurfaces and a spectral maximum principle. For surfaces, no lower curvature bound is needed.

papers.title: Nonlinear Inverse Iterations for Spin-Orbit Coupled Quantum Gases
papers.abstract: This work concerns the computation of ground states of two-component spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates (SO-coupled BECs), modelled by a coupled nonlinear eigenvalue problem of Gross-Pitaevskii type. In regimes with strongly modulated densities, including supersolid-like phases, conventional numerical approaches such as generalized inverse iterations or gradient descent may converge slowly. To address this issue, we apply the J-method [E. Jarlebring, S. Kvaal, W. Michiels. SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 36-4, 2014], which allows nonlinear inverse iterations to be accelerated through spectral shifting. A central analytical challenge arises from global phase invariance, which causes the target eigenvalue of the J-operator to be multiple and prevents the direct application of existing convergence results based on simple eigenvalues. Under a quasi-isolation assumption, we establish that this eigenvalue has algebraic and geometric multiplicity exactly two. By introducing an auxiliary phase-fixed iteration, we prove local linear convergence rates for the shifted J-method, determined by spectral gaps, in a quotient metric modulo global phase rotations. The particle densities converge at the same rate. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted linear convergence for fixed shifts and indicate superlinear convergence for adaptively chosen shifts.

papers.title: Online Ramsey numbers of the claw versus cycles
papers.abstract: The online Ramsey number $\tilde r(G,H)$ is defined via a Builder--Painter game on an empty graph with countably many vertices. In each round, Builder reveals an edge, which Painter immediately colors either red or blue. Builder wins once a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$ appears, and $\tilde r(G,H)$ is the minimum number of edges Builder must reveal to force a win. For a long cycle $C_\ell$, the online Ramsey numbers $\tilde r(G,C_\ell)$ are known only for a few specific choices of $G$. In particular, exact values were determined for $G=P_3$ by Cyman, Dzido, Lapinskas, and Lo (Electron. J. Combin., 2015), while asymptotically tight results were obtained when $G$ is an even cycle by Adamski, Bednarska-Bzdȩga, and Blažej (SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2024). In this paper, we consider the case where $G$ is the claw $K_{1,3}$ and determine the exact value of $\tilde r(K_{1,3},C_\ell)$. We show that \[ \tilde r(K_{1,3},C_\ell)=\left\lfloor \frac{3(\ell+1)}{2} \right\rfloor \quad \text{for all } \ell \ge 13. \]

papers.title: Fractional Besov-Sobolev Spaces on Chord-arc Curves
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a bounded rectifiable Jordan curve, with complementary domains $Ω_i$ and $Ω_e$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$, we study the spaces $\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(Ω)$ of harmonic functions satisfying \[ \iint_Ω|\nabla u(z)|^p \operatorname{dist}(z,Γ)^{(1-s)p-1}\,dA(z)<\infty, \qquad Ω\in\{Ω_i,Ω_e\}. \] When $Γ$ is the unit circle, the traces of these two spaces coincide with the fractional Besov-Sobolev space $B^s_{p,p}(Γ)$. The equivalence of boundary seminorms and harmonic energies on the circle raises a geometric question: which rough curves preserve these estimates? For every radial-Lipschitz curve $Γ$, we prove \[ \operatorname{Tr}_Γ\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(Ω_i) =B_{p,p}^s(Γ) =\operatorname{Tr}_Γ\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(Ω_e) \] whenever either $1 < p < 2$ and $2/p - 1 \leq s < 1$, $2 < p < \infty$ and $0 < s \leq 1/2 + 1/p$ or $p=2$ and $0<s<1$. For arbitrary chord-arc curves, the same trace identities hold when $1/p\le s<1/2+1/(2p)$. Taking $s=1-1/p$ yields an almost-Dirichlet principle for the unweighted $p$-energy on radial-Lipschitz domains when $3/2\le p\le4$. Here, the upper bound $4$ is sharp. In particular, every Riemann map $g:Ω_i\to\mathbb D_i$ from a bounded radial-Lipschitz domain satisfies $g'\in L^4(Ω_i)$, and the exponent $4$ is optimal uniformly over this class. This gives a sharp endpoint counterpart of Brennan's integrability conclusion for radial-Lipschitz domains.

papers.title: Representations of generalized linear Reedy categories and abelian model structures
papers.abstract: We study representations of generalized $k$-linear Reedy categories, extending both the linear Reedy categories of Dalezios and Št'ovíček and $k$-linearizations of generalized Reedy categories of Berger and Moerdijk. We establish homological properties of standard modules and classify irreducible representations in terms of simple modules over the local endomorphism algebras. We give criteria for a decomposition of the representation category into a product of local module categories; under the hypotheses of our non-degeneracy criterion, this decomposition holds if and only if the category is Hom-finite over $k$. Applications include span categories and representations of combinatorial categories. Using Grothendieck bifibrations, we then lift families of complete cotorsion pairs on the local module categories to complete cotorsion pairs on the representation category. Under compatibility assumptions, this also lifts families of (hereditary) Hovey triples and yields abelian model structures, with applications to Gorenstein homological algebra.

papers.title: Symbolic Integration of Differential Forms: From Abel to Zeilberger
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on symbolic integration of differential forms, with a particular emphasis on historical and modern developments, from Abel's addition theorems for Abelian integrals to Zeilberger's creative telescoping for parameterized integrals. It explores closed rational $p$-forms and provides algorithmic approaches for their integration, extending classical results like Hermite reduction and Liouville's theorem. The integration of closed differential forms with parameters is further examined through telescopers, offering a unified framework for handling both algebraic and transcendental cases.

papers.title: A note on characterization of $H^1$ Sobolev spaces by square functions
papers.abstract: We establish characterization of $H^1$ Sobolev spaces by certain square functions, improving previous results.

papers.title: Curvature of left-invariant complex Finsler metric on Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be an even-dimensional connected real Lie group admitting a left-invariant complex structure $J$. Let $\mathfrak g$ be the Lie algebra of $G$, and $\mathfrak g^{1,0}$ the $(1,0)$-part of the complexification $\mathfrak g^{\mathbb{C}}$ of $\mathfrak g$. We derive explicit formulas for the holomorphic sectional curvature and holomorphic bisectional curvature of any left-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric $F$ on $G$, expressed in terms of the complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g^{1,0}$. We also obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for $F$ to be a Kähler-Finsler metric (resp. weakly Kähler-Finsler metric). As an application, we prove a rigidity result: if $G$ is a complex Lie group and $F$ is a left-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric on $G$, then $F$ must be a complex Berwald metric with vanishing holomorphic bisectional curvature; moreover, $F$ is a Kähler-Berwald metric if and only if $G$ is an abelian complex Lie group.

papers.title: The Radon--Nikodym topography of acyclic measured graphs
papers.abstract: The classical Adams dichotomy [Ada90] characterizes amenability of probability-measure-preserving treed equivalence relations in terms of the ends of a given treeing. We extend this dichotomy to the measure-class-preserving (mcp) setting by analyzing the Radon--Nikodym topography of an acyclic mcp Borel graph, i.e., the interaction between the graph geometry and the associated Radon--Nikodym cocycle. In the general mcp setting one must count not all ends, but only the nonvanishing ends: those ends which have positive upper cocycle-weight. More precisely, we prove that a locally countable acyclic mcp graph is amenable if and only if a.e. component has at most two nonvanishing ends, while it is nowhere amenable exactly when a.e. component has a nonempty perfect closed set of nonvanishing ends. At the heart of our analysis lies the study of acyclic countable-to-one Borel functions. Our critical result is that, outside of the essentially two-ended setting, all back ends in a.e. orbit are vanishing and have cocycle-finite geodesics. We also give several characterizations, including topographical and cocycle-free, of essential one-endedness of such functions, and show that the number of barytropic ends controls the essential number of ends. Our proofs utilize mass transport, end selection, and the notion of the Radon--Nikodym core for acyclic mcp graphs, a new concept that serves as a guiding framework for our topographical analysis.

papers.title: Non-separable arrangements of convex bodies revisited
papers.abstract: A problem posed by Erdős in 1945 initiated the study of non-separable arrangements of convex bodies. A finite collection of convex bodies in Euclidean $d$-space is called a non-separable family (or NS-family) if every hyperplane intersecting their convex hull also intersects at least one member of the family. Recent work has focused on minimal coverings of NS-families consisting of positive homothetic convex bodies. In this paper, we strengthen these results by establishing their stability analogues and analyze weakly non-separable families of convex polytopes. We also examine weakly $k$-impassable families of convex $d$-polytopes for $0<k<d-1$ and study tightness of NS-lattice arrangements.

papers.title: An energy- and helicity-conserving enriched galerkin method for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We develop an enriched Galerkin (EG) method for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations that conserves both kinetic energy and helicity in the inviscid limit without introducing any additional projection variables. The method employs an EG velocity space, which is the first-order continuous Galerkin space enriched with piecewise constants defined on mesh faces, together with piecewise-constant pressure. Two numerical schemes based on the rotational form of the convective term are proposed: a nonlinear scheme and a linear variant. Both schemes exactly preserve the discrete helicity and kinetic energy, and the Picard iteration maintains the conservation properties of the nonlinear scheme. We prove the conservation properties of both the methods, and establish stability and rigorous error estimates for the nonlinear scheme. Numerical examples demonstrate the accuracy and conservation of the proposed linear scheme.

papers.title: Modulus estimates and cavitation in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: We explore the phenomenon of cavitation in higher-dimensional elasticity, defining it as the mapping of a punctured ball onto a non-degenerate ring domain. Crucially, for the class of locally quasiconformal mappings (or more general mappings) defined on the punctured ball $0<|x|<1$ in $\mathbb R^n$ that we examine, cavitation is equivalent to a failure of continuous extension to the origin. While existing modulus estimates prove insufficient for reliably detecting cavitation in this setting, our study establishes refined modulus bounds. This is achieved by introducing a novel directional dilatation which, in conjunction with the known angular dilatation, overcomes the limitations of previous methods. We illustrate our theoretical findings with several examples that demonstrate both cavitation occurrence and its absence.

papers.title: Certified bounds on optimization problems in quantum theory
papers.abstract: Semidefinite relaxations of polynomial optimization have become a central tool for addressing the non-convex optimization problems over non-commutative operators that are ubiquitous in quantum information theory and, more in general, quantum physics. Yet, as these global relaxation methods are solved numerically, the bounds issued by the semidefinite solver can - and often do - exceed the global optimum, undermining their certifiability. To counter this issue, we introduce a framework for extracting rigorous certified bounds on non-commutative optimization problems from inexact numerical data, and apply it to several paradigmatic problems in quantum information theory. An extension to sparsity and symmetry-adapted semidefinite relaxations is also provided and compared to the general dense scheme. Our results establish rational post-processing as a practical route to reliable certification, pushing semidefinite optimization toward a certifiable standard for quantum information science.

papers.title: Löwner equations and de Branges--Rovnyak spaces
papers.abstract: We study one-parameter families of de Branges--Rovnyak spaces associated with the radial and chordal Löwner equations. Our approach is based on a little-known technique developed by the de Branges school. In this paper, we recast this technique in the theory of direct integrals and integral operators. As an application, we prove Fourier-type expansion theorems induced by the Löwner equations and give answers to a problem posed by Fricain--Hartmann--Ross.

papers.title: The Bennati-Dragulescu-Yakovenko model in the continuous setting: PDE derivation and long-time behavior
papers.abstract: In this manuscript, we develop and analyze a continuous version of the well-known Bennati-Dragulescu-Yakovenko (BDY) dollar-exchange discrete model. Starting from the conservative BDY exchange mechanism, we rely on kinetic theory for multi-agent systems in order to propose an analogous Boltzmann-type continuous dynamics, which does not belong to the class of other popular kinetic models for wealth exchange. We employ the quasi-invariant limit procedure to rigorously derive a nonlinear PDE on the half-line, which is a Fokker-Planck equation featuring the boundary value in the drift term. The PDE is supplemented with a nonlinear Robin-type boundary condition encoding conservation of total agents and wealth. We prove relative entropy decay to the unique stationary state that is the Boltzmann-Gibbs (exponential) distribution with a $\mathrm{e}^{-c\sqrt{t}}$ convergence rate. We determine a new entropy production term which is a Fisher information minus a competing term which measures the temporal distance of the boundary term from its equilibrium value. Thanks to an inequality relating the Fisher information relative to the Boltzmann-Gibbs equilibrium to the $L^1$-norm, we prove $L^1$-convergence toward equilibrium and convergence of the boundary term (up to a subsequence), as well as convergence in both the Hellinger and Fourier distances. This represents an advancement in classical arguments of entropy decay for Fokker-Planck equations in a kinetic framework.

papers.title: Group Competition Test: A P-value-free False Discovery Rate Control Framework for Grouped Hypotheses
papers.abstract: Grouped multiple testing arises in many high-dimensional applications, where hypotheses may differ across groups and valid p-values are unavailable. Applying competition-based procedures separately within groups can inflate the global false discovery rate (FDR), while conservative corrections may substantially reduce power. We extend the competition test framework to the grouped setting and propose two procedures. The group competition (GC) test provides finite-sample FDR bounds under arbitrary inter-group dependence. For homogeneous groups, the required correction has logarithmic order in the number of groups, and this order is unavoidable for the GC test. The consistent group competition (CGC) filter instead couples group-specific thresholds through a single global normalization. Under the stated basic-independence conditions, it controls the FDR in finite samples without a correction that grows with the number of groups; under arbitrary inter-group dependence, the same guarantee is retained with a per-group correction that depends on the symmetry parameter of each group. We further develop a parameterized-threshold analysis to establish asymptotic guarantees and to characterize when the per-group correction can be dropped, so that a simple filter still controls the FDR approximately. Simulation studies show that the GC test and the CGC filter can improve power over pooled competition testing in heterogeneous settings, whereas the pooled test may remain more powerful under homogeneity. A peptide-spectrum matching benchmark involving post-translational modifications illustrates the practical relevance of the proposed methods.

papers.title: The $ρ$-Fourier transform
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a reductive group over a local field $F$ and let $ρ:{}^LG \to \mathrm{GL}_{V_ρ}(\mathbb{C})$ be a representation of its $L$-group satisfying suitable assumptions. Braverman, Kazhdan and Ngô conjectured that one has a $ρ$-Fourier transform satisfying certain desiderata. We give a uniform construction of the Fourier transform for arbitrary local fields. This complements work of L.~Lafforgue in the non-Archimedean case, and proves a portion of the conjectures of Braverman, Kazhdan and Ngô. Our methods are spectral in nature.

papers.title: Uniform decay of function norms
papers.abstract: We introduce and study two new relations between function spaces over measure spaces of infinite measure, motivated by the question of establishing compactness. The first relation captures the uniform decay of function (quasi-)norms ``at infinity''. It appeared implicitly in the first author's recent work on the compactness of Sobolev embeddings of radially symmetric functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$. The second is a suitably localized version of the relation of almost-compact embeddings, which has been successfully used to study compactness in function spaces over measure spaces of finite measure, but becomes of no use in the case of infinite measure. Our framework is that of quasi-Banach function spaces, which need not be normable or rearrangement invariant. This level of generality leads us to introduce the notion of extremal fundamental functions associated with a (quasi-)Banach function space. We provide several concrete examples and establish an abstract compactness principle involving the new relations. Finally, we demonstrate a possible application of this principle to embeddings of inhomogeneous Sobolev spaces on $\mathbb{R}^n$.

papers.title: Martingale dimensions for a class of metric measure spaces
papers.abstract: We study the martingale dimension of diffusion processes associated with strongly local regular Dirichlet forms on metric measure spaces. The martingale dimension is an intrinsic quantity describing the probabilistic complexity of a diffusion, but its precise determination in non-smooth settings is highly nontrivial. In this paper, we establish a purely analytic criterion, formulated in terms of energy measures and relative capacities, which guarantees that the AF-martingale dimension equals one. Our approach does not rely on self-similarity, heat kernel estimates, or global geometric assumptions, and applies to settings where such structures are unavailable. The proof is based on a blow-up analysis of harmonic functions combined with a push-forward argument for energy measures, which excludes the coexistence of multiple independent martingale directions. As applications, we verify the assumptions of the theory for a class of inhomogeneous Sierpinski gaskets, including genuinely non-self-similar examples, and for the two-dimensional standard Sierpinski carpet, where the criterion yields a new capacity-based proof of the one-dimensionality of the martingale structure. In these examples, self-similarity or local symmetry enters only in verifying the hypotheses; the mechanism that forces the one-dimensionality is the analytic balance condition itself.

papers.title: Wasserstein-Cramér-Rao Theory of Unbiased Estimation
papers.abstract: The quantity of interest in the classical Cramér-Rao theory of unbiased estimation (e.g., the Cramér-Rao lower bound, its exact attainment for exponential families, and asymptotic efficiency of maximum likelihood estimation) is the variance, which represents the instability of an estimator when its value is compared to the value for an independently-sampled data set from the same distribution. In this paper we are interested in a quantity which represents the instability of an estimator when its value is compared to the value for an infinitesimal additive perturbation of the original data set; we refer to this as the "sensitivity" of an estimator. The resulting theory of sensitivity is based on the Wasserstein geometry in the same way that the classical theory of variance is based on the Fisher-Rao (equivalently, Hellinger) geometry, and this insight allows us to determine a collection of results which are analogous to the classical case: a Wasserstein-Cramér-Rao lower bound for the sensitivity of any unbiased estimator, a characterization of models in which there exist unbiased estimators achieving the lower bound exactly, and various results on the asymptotic achievement of the lower bound. More precisely, we show that Wasserstein projection estimators (and one-step approximations thereof) are asymptotically sensitivity-efficient under suitable assumptions, and that there exist Hodges-type estimators which exhibit super-sensitivity-efficiency. We use these results to treat many statistical examples, sometimes revealing new optimality properties for existing estimators and other times revealing entirely new estimators.

papers.title: Integration in Hensel minimal fields
papers.abstract: We develop a framework of motivic integration in the style of Hrushovski--Kazhdan in arbitrary Hensel minimal fields of equicharacteristic zero. Hence our work generalizes that of Hrushovski--Kazhdan and Yin, but applies more broadly to discretely valued fields, almost real closed fields with analytic structure, pseudo-local fields, and coarsenings. In more detail, we obtain isomorphisms of Grothendieck rings of definable sets, with or without volume forms, in the valued field sort and in the leading term sort. Along the way we develop a theory of effective 1-h-minimal structures, where finite definable sets can be lifted from the leading term sort to the valued fields sort. We show that many natural examples of 1-h-minimal structures are effective, and develop dimension theory and a theory of differentiation in $\mathrm{RV}$ for effective structures.

papers.title: Abstract second-order boundary control systems
papers.abstract: Many physical systems, such as vibrating elastic bodies, acoustic media and electromagnetic fields, are governed by second-order evolution equations $\ddot x+D\dot x+Sx=0$ and interact with their environment through their boundary. The classical analysis via the operator matrix $\mathcal{A}=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&I\\-S&-D\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ requires $S$ to be self-adjoint, which typically fixes a boundary condition a priori and thus excludes boundary control. We therefore use $S$ only to define the energy space and govern the dynamics by a maximal operator $S_{\max}\supset S$ whose domain carries no boundary condition. Based on a factorization $S=A^*A$, we construct a boundary triplet for the associated operator matrix and define boundary inputs and outputs of Robin type, parametrized by an operator $P$ on the boundary space. We show that the resulting system is impedance passive and internally well-posed if $P$ is a contraction, and that for $D=0$ this covers all boundary conditions under which the free dynamics generate a contraction semigroup. Moreover, we show that the position-momentum formulation (e.g., $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&I\\Δ&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ for the wave equation) and the strain-momentum formulation (e.g., $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&\nabla\\\operatorname{div}&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$) describe the same open system, including its boundary inputs and outputs. We illustrate our results by an $n$-dimensional wave equation and Maxwell's equations.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous branching trees with symmetric and asymmetric offspring and their genealogies
papers.abstract: We define symmetric and asymmetric branching trees, a class of processes particularly suited for modeling genealogies of inhomogeneous populations where individuals may reproduce throughout life. In this framework, a broad class of Crump-Mode-Jagers processes can be constructed as (a)symmetric Sevast'yanov processes, which count the branches of the tree. Analogous definitions yield reduced (a)symmetric Sevast'yanov processes, which restrict attention to branches that lead to extant progeny. We characterize their laws through generating functions. The genealogy obtained by pruning away branches without extant progeny at a fixed time is shown to satisfy a branching property, which provides distributional characterizations of the genealogy.

papers.title: Reservoir computing based predictive reduced order model for steel grade intermixing in an industrial continuous casting tundish
papers.abstract: Continuous casting is a widely adopted process in the steel industry, where maintaining high steel quality is paramount. Efficient prediction of grade intermixing during ladle changeover operations is critical for maintaining steel quality and minimizing material losses in the continuous casting process. Among various factors influencing grade intermixing, operating parameters play a significant role, in addition to tundish geometry and flow control devices. In this study, three-dimensional, transient, two-phase turbulent flow simulations are conducted to investigate the ladle changeover operation. During this process, the molten steel level in the tundish typically varies over time, significantly affecting the grade intermixing phenomena. The influence of ladle change time on intermixing time has been presented. However, high-fidelity full-order simulations of such complex transient phenomena are computationally expensive and are impractical for real-time monitoring or design-space exploration in industrial-scale applications. To address this issue, a reduced order modelling approach based on proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and reservoir computing (RC) is employed to efficiently predict intermixing time. The proposed reduced order model (ROM) demonstrates excellent predictive accuracy using limited training data while requiring significantly less computational resources and training time. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed methodology as a fast, reliable tool for real-time process monitoring and optimization in industrial continuous casting operations.

papers.title: Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights: weighted maximal inequalities and fundamental structural properties
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal H_{\infty}^δ$ denote the Hausdorff content of dimension $δ\in(0,n]$ defined on subsets of $\mathbb R^n$. The principal problem, considered in this paper, is to characterize the non-negative function $w$ for which the weighted $L^p$ inequality with $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the weighted weak $L^1$ inequality on Hardy-Littlewood maximal operators associated with Hausdorff content hold true. To achieve this, we introduce a class of Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights, denoted as $\mathcal A_{p,δ}$, and then show that, for any $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $δ\in(0,n]$, the weighted $L^p$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{p,δ}$, and the weighted weak $L^1$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{1,δ}$ by proposing a novel approach. As the second objective, applying this approach, the seminal structural properties of classical Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weights, such as the reverse Hölder inequality [R. R. Coifman and C. Fefferman, Studia Math. 51 (1974), 241-250], the self-improving property [B. Muckenhoupt, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 165 (1972), 207-226], and Jones' factorization theorem [P. W. Jones, Ann. of Math. (2) 111 (1980), 511-530], are all established for $\mathcal A_{p,δ}$. The main novelties of this paper lies in: (i) we discover $\mathcal A_{p,δ}$ weights with rich structural properties, that increase strictly on dimension exponent and hence reduce to the classical $A_p$ class at the endpoint dimension, forming proper subsets of it for smaller dimension exponent; (ii) by proposing a novel approach, this work naturally extends the classical theory beyond measure-theoretic frameworks, while also provides novel insights even when reduced to the classical $A_p$ weight case.

papers.title: Leaky Zero Forcing on Subgraphs of $d$-dimensional Grid Graphs with an Application to Diamond Rectangles
papers.abstract: We study zero forcing and $\ell$-leaky zero forcing on Diamond rectangle graphs $DR(a,b)$, a family of induced subgraphs of 2-dimensional grid graphs. Motivated by this family, we develop more general results for subgraphs of $d$-dimensional grid graphs. Using $\ell$-leaky forts, we show that for $\ell\leq 2d-1$, every nonempty $\ell$-leaky fort in a subgraph of $P_{n_1}\square\cdots\square P_{n_d}$ must contain a vertex of degree at most $2d-1$. This gives bounds and, in certain cases, exact values for the $\ell$-leaky forcing number of such subgraphs. We then apply these results to Diamond rectangle graphs, for which we show that the zero forcing number equals the maximum nullity and completely characterize the $\ell$-leaky forcing number for all $\ell\geq 1$.

papers.title: Multiprecision computations with Schwarz methods
papers.abstract: Schwarz methods and preconditioners, where the approximate solution of the local problems is performed at a lower precision, i.e., with fewer digits of accuracy than in the underlying (double precision) computation. Conditions for the appropriate round-off criteria for the lower precision are presented. It is found experimentally that for the model problems about 5 digits of accuracy are sufficient to achieve the theoretical restrictions, and thus, single precision suffices for the local solves. Several numerical experiments illustrate the obtained results.

papers.title: A Computational Method for the Inverse Robin Problem with Convergence Rate
papers.abstract: The inverse Robin problem consists in determining the Robin parameter in an elliptic partial differential equation posed on a domain $Ω$. In this work it is assumed that the right-hand sides of the elliptic problem are known, that the associated solution is available on a subdomain $ω\subset Ω$ and that this solution vanishes at most at isolated points on the boundary $\partial Ω$. Within this framework, a computational method for the reconstruction of the Robin parameter is established, which is inspired by a unique continuation method. The proposed scheme relies solely on first-order Lagrange finite elements ensuring a straightforward implementation. Under the main assumption that the Robin parameter is in a finite dimensional space of continuously differentiable functions it is shown that the numerical method is second order convergent in the finite element's mesh size. For noisy data this convergence rate is shown to hold true until the noise term dominates the error estimate. Numerical experiments are presented that highlight the feasibility of the Robin parameter reconstruction and that confirm the theoretical convergence results numerically.

papers.title: Comparing classes of highly symmetric graphs: From $2$-arc-transitive to $2$-distance-transitive
papers.abstract: A $2$-distance-transitive graph is a vertex-transitive graph whose vertex stabilizer is transitive on both the first- and second-step neighborhoods. This concept simultaneously generalizes both distance-transitive graphs and $2$-arc-transitive graphs. In this paper, we first determine the vertex-quasiprimitive types of $2$-distance-transitive graphs of odd order, partially answering a question posed by A. Devillers, M. Giudici, C. H. Li and C. E. Praeger in 2012. We then prove that a $2$-distance-transitive graph of valency $p+1$, where $p$ is a prime, is $2$-arc-transitive if and only if it has girth at least $4$. We also show that every locally-primitive $2$-distance-transitive graph of valency at most $8$ is $2$-arc-transitive, with the icosahedron as the unique exception. Finally, we prove that if $Γ$ is a $G$-locally-primitive, $(G,2)$-distance-transitive graph of valency at least $3$ and $G$ is soluble, then either $Γ\cong \K_{p,p}$ for some prime $p$, or the order of $Γ$ is not square-free.

papers.title: Endoscopy for representations of disconnected reductive groups over finite fields
papers.abstract: Let G be the group of rational points of a connected reductive group over a finite field. Based on work of Lusztig and Yun, we make the Jordan decomposition for irreducible G-representations canonical. It comes in the form of an equivalence between the category of G-representations with a fixed semisimple parameter s and a category of essentially unipotent representations of an endoscopic group of G, enriched with an equivariant structure with respect to the component group of the centralizer of s. Next we generalize these results, replacing the connected reductive group by a smooth group scheme with reductive neutral component. Again we establish canonical equivalences for both the rational and the geometric series of G-representations, in terms of essentially unipotent representations of endoscopic groups.

papers.title: A meta-modal logic for bisimulations
papers.abstract: We propose a novel modal study of bisimulations. Our contribution is threefold. First, we extend the basic modal language with a new modality $\nbi$, whose intended meaning is universal quantification over all states that are bisimilar to the current one under a given bisimulation. We show that bisimulations are definable in this object language via frame validity (for the forth and back conditions) and model validity (for the atomic harmony condition). Additionally, some other related notions (refinements, simulations, bisimulations for a restricted set of variables, and $n$-bisimulations) are also shown to be definable. Second, we provide a sound and complete axiomatisation of the class of all pairs of Kripke models that are bisimulation-related. Third, we show that the satisfiability problem of this logic is decidable and PSPACE-complete via a translation to standard modal logic $K$ under a simple frame condition. All our results are encoded and verified by Isabelle/HOL.

papers.title: Identically vanishing $k$-generalized Fibonacci polynomials
papers.abstract: The recurrence for the $k$-Fibonacci polynomials is usually iterated upwards to positive values of $n$ only. When the recurrence is iterated downwards to $n<0$, there are indices where the polynomials vanish identically. This fact does not seem to have been noted in the literature. We derive the set of such indices. We establish the connection of our results to the solution of the Skolem problem for the $k$-Fibonacci numbers. For $k\ge3$ and $n<0$, we show that the degree of the polynomial does not increase monotonically with $|n|$. The so-called `left-justified $k$-nomial triangle' is extended to treat negative indices. We derive expressions for the individual polynomial coefficients (the elementary symmetric polynomials of the roots). We present results for the properties of the polynomials, for both $n>0$ and $n<0$, including factorization of the polynomials and properties of the roots. Results are also derived for real roots. We present new, tighter, bounds on the amplitudes of the nonzero roots. We derive new combinatorial sums for the polynomial coefficients, which are more concise and computationally efficient than previously published expressions.

papers.title: Functional second-order Gaussian Poincaré inequalities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we work in the framework of Hilbert-valued Wiener structures and derive a functional version of the second-order Gaussian Poincaré inequality that leads to abstract bounds for Gaussian process approximation in $d_2$ distance used by Bourguin and Campese (Electron. J. Probab., 2020). As pointed out by Bassetti, Bourguin, Campese, and Peccati (Statist. Probab. Lett., 2026) this distance alone does not imply weak convergence in infinite dimensions, we also consider $d_2^\dagger$, obtained by adding the absolute difference of the second moments. This metric metrizes $2$-Wasserstein convergence and agrees with $d_2$ for centered variables with matching covariance operators. Our abstract bounds are flexible and can be applied in various examples including functional Breuer-Major central limit theorems, shallow neural networks, and spatial statistics of SPDE solutions. In these applications, the covariance estimates also give the second-moment convergence needed for weak convergence in the corresponding Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: Position: Adopt Constraints Over Fixed Penalties in Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Deep learning models are increasingly subject to explicit requirements, or constraints, such as safety levels, fairness limits, and sparsity budgets. In practice, such requirements are often handled through fixed weighted-sum penalization: the constraints are added to the task loss with fixed coefficients, and the resulting scalarized objective is minimized. This position paper argues that fixed penalization is often ill-suited to deep learning problems with non-negotiable requirements, for three main reasons. First, in non-convex settings, the penalized and constrained problems are not, in general, equivalent, so a minimizer of the penalized objective need not solve the constrained problem. Second, a penalty coefficient sets an objective-constraint trade-off rather than the constraint level, so finding an acceptable coefficient often takes trial and error, each trial a full training run. Third, fixed penalization weakens hard requirements into soft penalties to be traded off against task performance. As a result, compliance is no longer built into the problem, and requirements can be quietly relaxed. We therefore argue that, when a deep learning problem specifies non-negotiable requirements, one should solve the constrained problem itself instead of a surrogate defined by fixed penalization.

papers.title: Hyper-dual group inverse: existence, characterizations, and applications
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent work of Xiao and Zhong [AIMS Math. 9 (2024), 35125--35150: MR4840882], we propose a generalized inverse for a hyper-dual matrix called hyper-dual group generalized inverse (HDGGI). Firstly, we characterize the existence of the HDGGI of a hyper-dual matrix and we show that it is unique, whenever exists. The HDGGI is then used to solve a linear hyper-dual system. We discuss the minimal $P$-norm least-squares properties of hyper-dual group inverse. We also exploit some sufficient conditions under which the reverse and forward-order laws for a particular form of the HDGGI and hyper-dual Moore-Penrose generalized inverse (HDMPGI) hold. Using the definition of dual matrix of order $n$, we finally establish necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of the group inverse of a dual matrix of order $n$.

papers.title: On shallow feedforward neural networks with inputs from a topological space
papers.abstract: We study feedforward neural networks with inputs from a topological space (TFNNs). We prove a universal approximation theorem for shallow TFNNs, which demonstrates their capacity to approximate any continuous function defined on this topological space. As an application, we obtain an approximative version of Kolmogorov's superposition theorem for compact metric spaces.

papers.title: A Smoothing Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method with Nonmonotone Backtracking Strategy for Convex Nonsmooth Composite Multiobjective Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper studies convex nonsmooth composite multiobjective optimization problems, whose objectives combine a convex term admitting a smooth approximation with a proper, closed, and convex term. A natural way is to smooth the nonsmooth term and apply proximal gradient method, but reducing the smoothing parameter shrinks step sizes, and solving successive smooth approximations to approach the original solution is computationally expensive. To address this issues, we propose a smoothing accelerated proximal gradient method with nonmonotone backtracking strategy. Each outer iteration starts from a reduced base smoothness estimate, which is increased only if the criterion fails, while the momentum update is linked to the estimate through an exact identity used in the convergence analysis. Under a compact level-set assumption and bounds of parameters, we use merit function to establish rates of $\mathcal{O}(k^{-σ})$, $\mathcal{O}((\log k)/k)$, and $\mathcal{O}(k^{σ-2})$ for different smoothing parameters. Then quasi-Fejér monotonicity yields convergence of the full sequence to a weak Pareto solution. Numerical experiments show that the method can reduce computational cost while preserving high-quality Pareto fronts and examine how the smoothing parameter affects performance.

papers.title: Equidistribution of integers represented by standard quadratic form under arithmetic constraints
papers.abstract: We study the equidistribution of integers of the form $n= x_1^2 + \cdots + x_d^2$ under the arithmetic constraints given by $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^d$. The first step in addressing this problem is to construct modular forms whose Fourier expansion coefficients correspond to the counting problem over the quadric in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ induced by the standard quadratic form, subject to the aforementioned arithmetic constraints. The weak modular property of these modular forms allows us to use representation theory to identify the congruence subgroup to which our modular forms correspond. We then establish a necessary and sufficient condition for functions on $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^d$ that defines a cusp form. Finally, we conclude that the equidistribution phenomenon occurs locally on $p+1$ orbits for $d \geq 4$.

papers.title: On group rings of the simple group of order 168, 504 or 360 and their modules
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $\mathbb{Z}_p$ the ring of $p$-adic integers. Let $G$ denote the simple group of order 168, 504 or 360. In this paper, we study the structure of the $χ$-part of a $\mathbb{Z}_p[\mathrm{Im}(χ)][G]$-module come from ideal class groups, Artin $L$-functions and Iwasawa theory. After this manuscript was posted, it was pointed out to the author that the main theorem holds for an arbitrary finite group and follows directly from the structure theorem for group rings; see the note added after Theorem 1.1.

papers.title: Low Genus Curves on Compact Shimura Surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate and compare the behaviors of complex curves on two major types of compact Shimura surfaces: compact variants of Picard and Hilbert modular surfaces. They are quotients of complex hyperbolic balls corresponding to moduli problems for abelian varieties with certain endomorphism types. We prove that if we fix a genus bound, then when the defining discriminant is large enough, low genus curves on the compact variant of Picard modular surfaces do not exist, while low genus curves may persist on the compact variant of Hilbert modular surfaces only if they are special curves, which parametrize those with extra endomorphisms. These results are special cases of a complex function field analogue of uniform boundedness on endomorphism types of abelian varieties. The proof requires understanding the repulsion of special subvarieties and relies on volume estimates in hyperbolic geometry.

papers.title: The Integrable Snake Model
papers.abstract: A pure snake configuration is a bijection $σ:\mathbb{Z}^2 \to \mathbb{Z}^2$ containing no two-cycles and such that for each $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ we have $σ(x) \in \{ x , x+ \mathbf{e}^1, x+\mathbf{e}^2 , x- \mathbf{e}^2 \}.$ The non-trivial cycles of a pure snake configuration may be regarded as a collection of non-intersecting paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ that may travel right, up, or down (but not left) from a given vertex.
