We then derive the separated relations and write the Hamilton equations in canonical separated variables, thus decomposing the original Hamiltonian system into two separated subsystems. To the best of our knowledge, this explicit derivation of the separating variables and, in particular, of the conjugate momenta for the generalized Kaup--Kupershmidt system is new. For the KdV$_5$ and Sawada--Kotera cases we show how the same bi-Hamiltonian scheme applies, emphasizing both the common geometric mechanism and the features peculiar to each system. In this way, the three generalized cubic Hénon--Heiles systems are treated within a unified framework based on compatible Poisson structures, recursion operators, control matrices, and Darboux--Nijenhuis coordinates.

papers.title: High-order kernel regularization of singular and hypersingular Helmholtz boundary integral operators
papers.abstract: This paper extends and analyzes the high-order kernel regularization framework of Beale & Tlupova (arXiv:2510.13639) to all four on-surface boundary integral operators of the Helmholtz Calderon calculus in three dimensions: the single-layer, double-layer, adjoint double-layer, and hypersingular operators. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first high-order kernel regularization of the hypersingular operator for both the Helmholtz and Laplace equations in three dimensions. The regularization replaces each singular kernel with a smooth modification constructed from error functions together with a polynomial correction whose coefficients are determined through moment conditions. Alongside the derivation of the regularizing functions, the paper provides a unified error analysis of the combined regularization and quadrature discretization procedure. By coupling the regularization parameter to the mesh size, the two error contributions can be balanced, leading to explicit overall convergence rates that depend jointly on the order of the regularization and the degree of exactness of the surface quadrature rule. A key practical feature of the method is its implementation simplicity. Once the regularizing functions are determined, the numerical task reduces entirely to the evaluation of smooth surface integrals using standard quadrature, without the need for element-local solves, singularity-specific precomputations, or specialized quadrature rules. Although the modified kernel is generally incompatible with kernel-specific fast methods, this limitation is addressed through H-matrix acceleration, applicable in a black-box manner. Numerical examples -- including verification of the predicted convergence rates and solution of sound-soft and sound-hard scattering problems by smooth obstacles -- demonstrate the accuracy and practicality of the proposed methodology.

papers.title: Enumerations and Bijections for Stanley Polyominoes
papers.abstract: Stanley polyominoes are a subclass of parallelogram polyominoes in which each row begins strictly to the right of the beginning of the previous row and ends strictly to the right of the end of the previous row. In this paper, we derive generating functions for Stanley polyominoes with respect to the numbers of columns and rows, area, semiperimeter, and numbers of interior points and edges. We also establish combinatorial connections through bijections with other combinatorial structures such as Dyck paths, skew Ferrers diagrams, and peakless Motzkin paths. As a byproduct, we answer the open question of finding a bijection between parallelogram polyominoes of area $n$ with $k$ columns and coin fountains with $n$ coins in the odd-numbered rows and $n-k$ coins in the even-numbered rows.

papers.title: On $c_0$ quotients of nonseparable Bourgain-Pisier $\mathscr{L}_\infty$-spaces
papers.abstract: Lopez-Abad extended the Bourgain-Pisier construction to Banach spaces of arbitrary density: every Banach space $X$ embeds isometrically into an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space $Y$ such that $Y/X$ has the Radon-Nikodym and Schur properties. We study $c_0$ quotients of these spaces. For every $X$ of uncountable density $κ$, we describe a realization of the construction that admits an explicit surjection $T: Y \to c_0$, given by coordinate functionals built along the construction, whose kernel is an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space of density $κ$. We also note that an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space with a non-Grothendieck quotient has a $c_0$ quotient, and that every Lopez-Abad space has an $\ell_2$ quotient; all of them have $c_0$ quotients if no infinite-dimensional Banach space is both Schur and Grothendieck, a question we leave open. In an appendix we characterize when the kernel of a quotient map from an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space onto $c_0$ is an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space, give a quotient map from $C[0,1]$ onto $c_0$ whose kernel is not, and show that every non-Grothendieck $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space admits one whose kernel is. This version corrects errors in version 1.

papers.title: Minimaxity and Admissibility of Bayesian Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) offer a natural probabilistic formulation for inference in deep learning models. Despite their popularity, their optimality has received limited attention through the lens of statistical decision theory. In this paper, we study decision rules induced by deep, fully connected feedforward ReLU BNNs in the normal location model under quadratic loss. We show that, for fixed prior scales, the induced Bayes decision rule is not minimax. We then propose a hyperprior on the effective output variance of the BNN prior that yields a superharmonic square-root marginal density, establishing that the resulting decision rule is simultaneously admissible and minimax. We further extend these results from the quadratic loss setting to the predictive density estimation problem with Kullback--Leibler loss. Finally, we validate our theoretical findings numerically through simulation.

papers.title: Optimal control for a class of linear evolution equations with transformed proper orthogonal decomposition
papers.abstract: Solving optimal control problems for high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) is computationally expensive. As a workaround, reduced-order models (ROMs) are often employed, which replace the full PDE system and alleviate the computational burden while solving optimal control problems. However, when the underlying PDE exhibits transport-dominated behavior, standard reduced-order modeling techniques like proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) that rely on linear approximation spaces may require a large number of modes due to the slowly decaying Kolmogorov $n$-width. To overcome this challenge, we focus on the use of transformed POD as a reduced-order model, which is particularly effective in capturing low-dimensional representations of high-fidelity transport-dominated phenomena. In this work, a reduced-order model is constructed first, followed by the optimization of the reduced system. For linear systems generated by strongly continuous groups, we prove existence and uniqueness of solutions for the ROM under an explicit smallness condition on the control, as well as the existence of an optimal control for sufficiently large regularization. The numerical experiments concern the 1D linear advection equation with a subset of the general transformation groups called the shift transformations. Additionally, we compare the computational performance of the shifted POD (sPOD) method against the standard POD.

papers.title: Optimality and annealing path planning of dynamical analog solvers
papers.abstract: Recently proposed analog solvers based on dynamical systems, such as Ising machines, are promising platforms for large-scale combinatorial optimization. Yet, given the heuristic nature of the field, there is very limited insight on optimality guarantees of the solvers, as well as how parameter schedules shape dynamics and outcomes. Here, we develop a dynamical mean-field framework to analyze Ising-machine dynamics for finding the ground state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick(SK) model of spin glasses and identify mechanisms that enable rapid convergence to provenly near-optimal energies. For a fixed target energy density Ec, we show that solutions are typically reached within O(1) matrix vector multiplications, indicating constant time complexity. We further delineate theoretical limitations arising from different parameter-scheduling trajectories and demonstrate a pronounced benefit of temperature-only annealing for the Coherent Ising Machine. Building on these insights, we propose a general framework for designing optimized parameter schedules, thereby improving the practical effectiveness of Ising machines for complex optimization tasks. The superior performance of the dynamical solvers is illustrated by the attainment of the ground state energy of the SK model.

papers.title: An error control framework for computing the exponential of matrices arising from the finite element discretization
papers.abstract: Several methods for computing the action of the matrix exponential $\mathrm{e}^{\boldsymbol{A}} \boldsymbol{b}$ are expressed by substituting $\boldsymbol{A}$ into a rational approximation of the scalar exponential function. When $\boldsymbol{A}$ is a general sparse matrix, the approximation error of such methods can be bounded using the numerical range of $\boldsymbol{A}$, which enables the computation of $\mathrm{e}^{\boldsymbol{A}} \boldsymbol{b}$ with a prescribed accuracy. This study extends this error control framework to matrices of the form $\boldsymbol{A} = τ\boldsymbol{M}^{-1} \boldsymbol{K}$, where $\boldsymbol{M}$ is a well-conditioned symmetric positive definite matrix. A direct application of the framework faces two challenges: determining the numerical range of $\boldsymbol{A}$ is not straightforward, and the resulting error bounds can significantly overestimate the approximation error. In this paper, we show that these issues can be resolved by using the numerical range of the similarity transformed version of $\boldsymbol{A}$. Numerical experiments confirm that the computations can be performed within the prescribed error tolerance.

papers.title: Failing to keep the balance: explicit formulae and topological recursion for leaky Hurwitz numbers
papers.abstract: Recently a new family of enumerative invariants called leaky Hurwitz numbers was introduced by Cavalieri-Markwig-Ranganathan in the context of logarithmic intersection theory. They admit an interpretation via tropical covers where the balancing condition fails. We employ tropical geometry to prove a generalisation of the piecewise polynomiality of Accadia-Karev-Lewanski for leaky completed cycles Hurwitz numbers, and a different wall crossing that is cubic instead of quadratic. Using tropical combinatorics and generatingfunctionology, we also find closed formulae for one-part and two-part completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers in genus $0$. Working more generally with a view towards topological recursion, we use Hamiltonian flows to associate spectral curves to very general cut-and-join operators. Under mild analytic constraints, we find the appropriate spectral curves, and in case the leakiness is fixed, we show that the resulting enumerative invariants satisfy topological recursion. This provides a partial inverse to recent work of Alexandrov-Bychkov-Dunin-Barkowski-Kazarian-Shadrin producing differentials satisfying topological recursion for KP $τ$-functions. In particular these results specialise to completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers.

papers.title: Graded Algebras over Polynomial Rings
papers.abstract: Given a trivially graded polynomial ring $P_0=K[a_1,\dots,a_m]$ over a field $K$ and a positively graded polynomial ring $P=P_0[x_1,\dots,x_s]$, we study graded rings $R=P/I$, where $I$ is a homogeneous ideal of $P$ satisfying $I\cap P_0=\{0\}$. The induced morphism $Θ: {\rm Spec}(R)\rightarrow {\rm Spec}(P_0) = \mathbb{A}^m_K$ is used to prove that ${\rm Spec}(R)$ is connected. Next, we characterize and compute the following loci in $\mathbb{A}^m_K$: the set ${\rm Sing}_0(Θ)$ of all points whose corresponding point in the zero section of $Θ$ is singular in ${\rm Spec}(R)$, the set ${\rm Sing}_v(Θ)$ of all points $Γ$ such that the origin of the fiber $F_Γ$ of $Θ$ is singular, and the set ${\rm Sing}_s(Θ)$ of all points $Γ$ such that $\dim({\rm Sing}(F_Γ))\ge 1$. Finally, we apply these results to MaxDeg border basis schemes. Their coordinate rings are non-negatively graded by the total arrow degree and satisfy the above hypotheses. In particular, we explicitly determine the singular loci of the $\mathcal{O}$-border basis schemes with $\mathcal{O} = \{1,x,y,z,z^2\}$ and $\mathcal{O} = \{1,x,y,z,yz\}$.

papers.title: Block Diagonalization and Multiplicativity of Quaternion $Z$-Block Circulant Matrices with Applications
papers.abstract: The motivation of this paper is twofold. We firstly investigate the block-diagonalization of the $z$-block circulant matrix $\mathtt{bcirc_z}(\mathcal A)$, and develop the algorithm $\mathtt{bcirc_z}$-inv for computing the inverse of $\mathtt{bcirc_z}(\mathcal A)$. Second, we establish the multiplicativity of the operator $\mathtt{bcirc_z}$, which yields the equivalence between the QT-product of tensors and the multiplication of their corresponding $z$-block circulant matrices. As applications of these results, we conduct large-scale numerical experiments and analyze the scalability of the Tikhonov-regularized model. We also obtain polar decompositions under the QT-product, develop an algorithm for computing them, and present a large-scale test and a scalability analysis. In addition, we evaluate several rotation strategies based on the QT-polar decomposition through video rotation applications. The results show that the decomposition remains stable and maintains inter-frame consistency while accurately preserving colors.

papers.title: When Does Cheap Physics Help? Gated Multi-Fidelity Physics-Informed Networks with Provable Sample Savings and Conformal Guarantees
papers.abstract: High-fidelity (HF) simulations of parametric partial differential equations are expensive, whereas low-fidelity (LF) models such as coarse grids or simplified physics are cheap but biased. Multi-fidelity physics-informed neural networks combine the two, yet it remains unclear when cheap physics actually reduces the number of HF solves, and existing methods silently fail when the LF model is misleading and offer no guaranteed uncertainty. We answer the first question with a sharp sample-complexity bound: learning the HF field through its discrepancy from the LF model reduces the number of HF samples needed for accuracy $\varepsilon$ by the factor $κ^{2γ}$, where $κ$ is the ratio of the complexity of the discrepancy to that of the HF field and $γ$ is the effective-dimension exponent, and we confirm the predicted scaling with exact risk computations in a kernel model. Guided by the analysis, we propose GaMF-PINN, a gated multi-fidelity PINN that learns where to trust the LF model and falls back to physics-only learning where it does not, together with a function-level conformal procedure that returns uncertainty bands containing the entire HF solution with probability at least $1-α$ in finite samples. We release MFPDE-Bench, an open benchmark of paired LF/HF solvers for four parametric PDEs with coarse-grid and simplified-physics LF models. Across MFPDE-Bench, GaMF-PINN reaches the accuracy of a standard HF-PINN with up to 8x fewer HF solves, remains robust when the LF model is deliberately corrupted, and attains the nominal coverage where Bayesian PINNs and deep ensembles under-cover.

papers.title: Recurrence Relations for the Maclaurin Coefficients of Products of Elementary Functions and the Bessel Functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate recurrence relations for the Maclaurin coefficients of the products of a elementary function and the Bessel function of the first kind $\mathcal{J}(z) = h(z) J_ν(z)$ and the modified Bessel function of the first kind $\mathcal{I}(z) = h(z) I_ν(z)$ in the complex plane corresponding to several specific choices of $h(z)$. In particular, we specialize $h(z)$ as $e^{pz}$, $(1-θz)^p$, $e^{-p \arctan z}$, $\sin(pz)$, $\cos(pz)$, $\sinh(pz)$, $\cosh(pz)$, $\arcsin(pz)$ and $\arccos(pz)$.

papers.title: Pluriclosed 3-folds with vanishing Bismut Ricci form: General theory in the quasi-regular case
papers.abstract: We study compact complex $3$-dimensional non-Kähler Bismut Ricci flat pluriclosed Hermitian manifolds (BHE) via their dimensional reduction to a special Kähler geometry in complex dimension $2$, recently obtained by Barbaro, Streets and the first and third authors. We show that in the quasi-regular case, the reduced geometry satisfies a 6th order non-linear PDE which has infinite dimensional momentum map interpretation, similar to the much studied Kähler metrics of constant scalar curvature (cscK). We use this to associate to the reduced manifold or orbifold Mabuchi and Calabi functionals, as well as to obtain obstructions for the existence of solutions in terms of the authomorphism group, paralleling results by Futaki and Calabi-Lichnerowicz-Matsushima in the cscK case. This is used to characterize the Samelson locally homogeneous BHE geometries in complex dimension 3 as the only non-Kähler BHE $3$-folds with $2$-dimensional Bott-Chern $(1,1)$-cohomology group, for which the reduced space is a smooth Kähler surface. We also discuss explicit solutions of the PDE on orthotoric Kähler orbifold surfaces, extending examples found by Couzens-Gauntlett-Martelli-Sparks in the framework of supersymmetric ${\rm AdS}_3 \times Y_7$ type IIB supergravity. Our construction yields infinitely many non-Kähler BHE structures on $S^3\times S^3$ and $S^1\times S^2 \times S^3$, which are not locally isometric to a Samelson geometry. These appear to be the first such examples.

papers.title: Freidel-Maillet type equations on fused K-matrices over the positive part of $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$
papers.abstract: The positive part $U_q^+$ of the quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ has a reflection equation presentation of Freidel-Maillet type (Baseilhac 2022). Its defining K-matrix has size $2 \times 2$ and can be expressed, using Rosso's embedding of $U_q^+$ into a $q$-shuffle algebra, as generating functions whose coefficients are Terwilliger's alternating PBW basis elements. This and older PBW bases of $U_q^+$ due to Damiani and Beck are unified by linear combinations of Catalan words (Ruan 2025). In this paper, we use this unification to define K-operators of any dimension $\geq 2$ in matrix form; the entries are explicit generating functions over $U_q^+$. Our main result is that any pair of such K-matrices, possibly of different dimensions, satisfy a Freidel-Maillet type equation. This yields a family of algebraic relations over $U_q^+$ that generalize Baseilhac's equation and can be used to study integrable systems or higher-spin representations. We conjecture that, for every spin, these K-matrices coincide with Lusztig's quasi R-matrix evaluated with its first leg on the corresponding finite-dimensional irreducible module.

papers.title: Structured Continuity Equations in Fibred Wasserstein Spaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we develop a comprehensive ODE-theory for structured continuity equations in fibred probability spaces, which represent a class of heterogeneous PDEs arising as the meanfield limit of nonexchangeable particle systems. After investigating in depth the topologies induced by the so-called fibred (or conditional) and classical Wasserstein metrics on such probability spaces, we establish quantitative Cauchy-Lipschitz and qualitative Carathéodory-Peano well-posedness results for structured continuity equations, along with precise correspondences between this class of evolutions, classical Lagrangian dynamics, and continuity equations. In keeping with what has long been known for exchangeable dynamics, we derive a general meanfield approximation result by solutions of nonexchangeable particle systems, along with a quantitative variant thereof under practically reasonable regularity assumptions on the driving field and initial data.

papers.title: New Empirical Process Tools and Their Applications to Robust Deep ReLU Networks and Phase Transitions for Nonparametric Regression
papers.abstract: This paper introduces new empirical process tools for analyzing a broad class of statistical learning models under heavy-tailed noise and complex function classes. Our primary contribution is the derivation of two Dudley-type maximal inequalities for expected empirical processes that remove restrictive assumptions such as light tails and uniform boundedness of the function class. These inequalities enlarge the scope of empirical process theory available for statistical learning and nonparametric estimation. Exploiting the new bounds, we establish robustness guarantees for deep ReLU network estimators in Huber and quantile regression. In particular, we prove a unified non-asymptotic sub-Gaussian concentration bound that remains valid even under infinite-variance noise and provide a comprehensive analysis of non-asymptotic robustness for deep Huber estimators across all noise regimes. For deep quantile regression, we provide the first non-asymptotic sub-Gaussian bounds without requiring moment assumptions. As an additional application, our framework yields estimation error bounds for nonparametric least-squares estimators that simultaneously accommodate infinite-variance noise, non-Donsker function classes, and approximation error. Moreover, unlike prior approaches based on specialized multiplier processes, our framework extends to broader empirical risk minimization problems, including the nonparametric generalized linear models and the ``set-structured'' models.

papers.title: Hilbert squares of genus 16 K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We consider the geometry of a general polarized K3 surface $(S,h)$ of genus 16 and its Fourier-Mukai partner $(S',h')$. We prove that $S^{[2]}$ is isomorphic to the moduli space $M_{S'}(2,h',7)$ of stable sheaves with Mukai vector $(2,h',7)$ and describe the embeddings of the projectivization of the stable vector bundle of Mukai vector $(2,-h',8)$ over $S'$ into these two isomorphic hyper-Kähler fourfolds. Following the work of Frédéric Han \cite{Frederic}, we explicitly construct a 3-form $t_1\in \wedge^3 V_{10}^*$, such that $S^{[2]}$ is isomorphic to the Debarre-Voisin fourfold in $G(6,V_{10})$ associated to $t_1\in \wedge^3 V_{10}^*$. Then the reconstruction program is also explained from two perspectives, i.e. in terms of families of stable representations and families of twisted cubics.

papers.title: Case Studies in Generalized Kantorovich-Rubinstein Duality
papers.abstract: The classical Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality guarantees coincidence between metrics on the space of probability distributions defined on the one hand via transport plans (couplings) and on the other hand via price functions. Both constructions have been lifted to the level of generality of set functors, with the construction based on couplings referred to as the Wasserstein or simply the coupling-based lifting, and the price-function-based construction as the Kantorovich or codensity lifting, both based on a choice of quantitative modalities for the given functor. It is known that every coupling-based lifting can be expressed as a price-function-based lifting; however, the latter in general needs to use additional modalities. We give an example showing that this cannot be avoided in general. We refer to cases in which the same modalities can be used as satisfying the generalized Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality. We establish the generalized Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality in this sense for two important cases: The Lévy-Prokhorov distance on distributions, which finds wide-spread applications in machine learning due to its favourable stability properties, and the standard metric on convex sets of distributions that arises by combining the Hausdorff and Kantorovich-Rubinstein distances. Furthermore we generalize (coupling-based) functor liftings from set functors to functors which act on (pseudo-)metric spaces, thus incorporating new example functors that map to closed subsets respectively Radon measures.

papers.title: On intertwined polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be polynomials of degree at least two over $\mathbb C$. We say that $A_1$ and $A_2$ are intertwined if the endomorphism $(A_1, A_2)$ of $\mathbb C\mathbb P^1 \times \mathbb C\mathbb P^1$ given by $(z_1, z_2) \mapsto (A_1(z_1), A_2(z_2))$ admits an irreducible periodic curve that is neither a vertical nor a horizontal line. For a polynomial $A$, we denote by $\mathrm{Inter}(A)$ the set of all polynomials $B$ such that some iterate of $B$ is intertwined with some iterate of $A$. In this paper, we prove a conjecture of Favre and Gauthier describing the structure of $\mathrm{Inter}(A)$. We also obtain a sharp bound on the periods of periodic curves for endomorphisms $(A_1, A_2)$ in terms of the sizes of the symmetry groups of the Julia sets of $A_1$ and $A_2$.

papers.title: Global coalitions in graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G=(V, E)$ be a graph. A subset $S \subseteq V$ is called a global dominating set of $G$ if it is a dominating set of both $G$ and its complement $\overline{G}$. Two disjoint subsets $V_1, V_2 \subseteq V$ form a global coalition if neither $V_1$ nor $V_2$ is a global dominating set, but their union $V_1 \cup V_2$ is. A global coalition partition (abbreviated $gc$-partition) of $G$ is a vertex partition $π$ of $V(G)$ such that every class of $π$ forms a global coalition with some other class of $π$. The global coalition number $GC(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of a $gc$-partition of $G$. In this paper, we initiate the study of these concepts. We prove that every graph of order at least two admits a $gc$-partition, give general lower bounds on $GC(G)$, and bound the number of global coalitions in which a single class of a $gc$-partition can be involved. We show that $GC(G)$ coincides with the coalition number $C(G)$ whenever $G$ is disconnected or has radius at least three, and consequently that $GC(G)=C(\overline{G})$ for every join of two graphs. We determine the global coalition number of complete multipartite graphs with at most three parts, wheels, fans, paths, cycles and trees of radius two, characterise the graphs $G$ with $GC(G)=|V(G)|$ in terms of antitwins, relate global coalitions to perfect coalitions, and study unicyclic graphs of radius at most two. Finally, we interpret $gc$-partitions in the language of fair division of indivisible goods and pose several open problems.\\ \textbf{2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:} 05C69, 91B32.\\ \textbf{JEL Classification:} C72, C78, D63.\\ \textbf{Keywords}: Global domination, coalition, global coalition partition, antitwins, trees, unicyclic graphs, fair division.

papers.title: Bertini's theorem for $F$-rational $F$-pure singularities
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $X\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n_k$ be a quasi-projective variety that is $F$-rational and $F$-pure. We prove that if $H \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n_k$ is a general hyperplane, then $X \cap H$ is also $F$-rational and $F$-pure. Of related but independent interest, we present a relationship between the characteristic and index of a $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein variety with isolated non-$F$-regular locus which is $F$-pure but not $F$-regular.

papers.title: The spectral Turán problem: Characterizing spectral-consistent graphs
papers.abstract: Let ${\rm EX}(n,H)$ and ${\rm SPEX}(n,H)$ denote the families of $H$-free graphs of order $n$ with maximum size and maximum spectral radius, respectively. A graph $H$ is called spectral-consistent if ${\rm SPEX}(n,H)\subseteq {\rm EX}(n,H)$ holds for all sufficiently large $n$. Cioabă, Desai, and Tait put forward the following conjecture: Let $H$ be a graph for which every graph in ${\rm EX}(n,H)$ is a Turán graph plus $O(1)$ edges. Then $H$ is spectral-consistent. Wang, Kang, and Xue settled this conjecture. Recently, Liu and Ning raised a general problem in spectral extremal graph theory: Characterize all graphs that are spectral-consistent. In this paper, we establish that for any finite graph $H$, if its decomposition family is matching-good, then $H$ is necessarily spectral-consistent. Notably, this structural condition is strictly weaker than the condition for spectral-consistency established by Wang, Kang, and Xue in their earlier work, thereby broadening the class of graphs known to satisfy the spectral-consistency property. Our main result enables us to fully characterize spectral consistency for several important families of forbidden graphs $H$, including generalized color-critical graphs, odd-balloonings of nontrivial trees and complete bipartite graphs $K_{s,t}$ with $t\geq s\geq 2$ and $(s,t)\neq(2,3)$, as well as edge blow-ups of non-bipartite graphs and even cycles. Furthermore, we present a streamlined proof of the Chen--Lei--Li theorem on the spectral-consistency of disjoint unions of suspensions of unions of color-critical graphs. Finally, we propose an open problem to motivate future research in this area.

papers.title: Descent problem for certificate of non-negativity on semi-algebraic sets
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a subfield of $\mathbb R$ and let $K$ be a basic closed semi-algebraic set in $\mathbb R$ with $\partial K\subset F$. Let $\mathcal N$ be the natural choice of generators of $K$. We show that if $f\in F[x]$ is $\geq 0$ on $K$, then $f$ can be written as $$f=\sum_{e\in\{0,1\}^s } a_eσ_e g^e $$ where $a_e\in F_{\geq 0}$, $σ_e\in \sum F[x]^2$ and $g^{e}=g_1^{e_1} \cdots g_s^{e_s}$. In other words, the preordering $T_{\mathcal N}$ of $F[x]$ is saturated. In case $F=\mathbb R$, this result is due to Kuhlmann and Marshall. As an application, we prove that if $K$ is compact, then $M_{\mathcal N}=T_{\mathcal N}=Pos(K)$. In other words, the quadratic module $M_{\mathcal N}$ of $F[x]$ is saturated.

papers.title: Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, Nijenhuis Lie bialgebras and \sss-equation
papers.abstract: We develop a bialgebraic framework for Nijenhuis operators on pre-Lie algebras and coalgebras. Starting from dual triangular pre-Lie bialgebras and weak pseudo-Hessian structures, we construct Nijenhuis operators on pre-Lie algebras and establish the corresponding coalgebraic construction. We introduce Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, characterize them through matched pairs, and identify compatibility conditions linking the two constructions. For triangular structures, we formulate the $S$-Nijenhuis $\mathbb{S}$-equation, give an operator characterization, and obtain constructions using relative Rota-Baxter operators. We also show that balanced Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras give rise to Nijenhuis Lie bialgebras. Finally, we introduce crossed modules and braided Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, and characterize when compatible algebraic and coalgebraic data assemble into a Nijenhuis pre-Lie biproduct. These results connect Nijenhuis operators with pre-Lie bialgebra structures, Yang-Baxter-type equations, and constructions on representations.

papers.title: Bayesian Predictive Inference Beyond Martingales
papers.abstract: There is growing interest in the so-called Bayesian Predictive Inference approach, which enables Bayesian inference without specifying a likelihood function or prior distribution and without resorting to MCMC methods. Instead, only a sequence of predictive distributions for the observations is required, and inference on the unknown estimand can be performed, cheaply in parallel, using bootstrap-type schemes. Understanding which classes of predictive distributions can be used within this framework, is still a key open question. We relax commonly used probabilistic assumptions on the observations, namely exchangeability and conditionally identical distribution, and on their predictive distributions, which are measure-valued martingales, by introducing the new class of Almost Conditionally Identically Distributed (a.c.i.d.) random variables. This class assumes that the predictive distributions are measure-valued almost supermartingales, and is parametrized by a sequence of parameters $(ξ_{n})_{n\geq 0}$, which regulate the decay of conditional dependence among future observations. Under mild summability assumptions on $(ξ_{n})_{n\geq 0}$, the resulting sequence of observations is shown to be asymptotically exchangeable, hence amenable to Bayesian Predictive Inference techniques. A.c.i.d. random variables arise naturally in recursive algorithms, and include classic approaches in Statistics and Learning Theory, such as kernel estimators, and more novel ones, such as the parametric Bayesian bootstrap.

papers.title: Crossings and diffusion in Poisson driven marked random connection models
papers.abstract: We first study crossing statistics in random connection models (RCM) built on marked Poisson point processes on $\mathbb R^d$. Under general assumptions, we show exponential tail bounds for the number of crossings of a box contained in the infinite cluster for supercritical intensity of the point process, and percolation in slabs, in analogy with the Grimmett-Marstrand theorem. We then present several applications to transport and diffusion phenomena. In particular, we prove the non-degeneracy of the effective homogenized matrix arising in the large-scale limit of random walks, exclusion processes, and resistor networks on the RCM, and the non-degeneracy of the effective diffusion constant for one-dimensional diffusion operators on the Euclidean graph associated with the RCM. As examples, we apply our results to Poisson-Boolean models and Mott variable range hopping random resistor network, providing a fundamental ingredient used in the derivation of Mott's law.

papers.title: Online Learning in Stabilized Linear Dynamical Games with Adversarial Disturbances
papers.abstract: We study online learning in linear dynamical games where multiple strategic agents act on a shared state evolving according to a linear dynamical system subject to adversarial disturbances. This setting lies beyond both single-agent nonstochastic online control and classical linear-quadratic games, which typically focus on quadratic objectives and noiseless or stochastic dynamics. Each agent seeks to minimize its own sequence of convex losses under full-state observability. Following the stabilizing-baseline paradigm in nonstochastic online control, we assume access to linear controllers that stabilize the noiseless system and focus on online adaptation by learning disturbance-action corrections. This extends adversarial online control to strategic multi-agent shared-state systems, where each agent's actions shape the state trajectory and hence the realized losses of all learners. Under state-only and aggregate-input feedback models, we analyze agents running online gradient descent with memory to update their own disturbance-action policies. We prove per-agent regret bounds that are sublinear and near-optimal in the time horizon, with population dependence that varies under the specified feedback, opponent policy, and stability assumptions. In the common-interest case, where all agents have identical cost functions, we show that the induced online problem forms a time-varying potential game and derive equilibrium tracking guarantees. Together, our results provide a theoretical framework for adversarial online learning in stabilized linear dynamical games, connecting online control with learning in games.

papers.title: fastGMRES: Robust randomized GMRES via flexible GMRES
papers.abstract: We propose a practical randomized algorithm for solving large sparse systems of linear equations. The algorithm, termed fastGMRES, uses flexible GMRES as an outer wrapper for sketched GMRES together with a practical residual bound to terminate the inner iteration. We demonstrate that fastGMRES requires very little parameter tuning, while still being efficient and robust in the sense of generating non-increasing residual norms. We observe that the inner sketched GMRES method can be run without any inner product computations and vector--vector updates on high-dimensional vectors, yielding significant speedup for many problems.

papers.title: Quasi-canonical lifting of projective varieties in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: The main aim of this article is to give new classes of smooth projective varieties over characteristic $p>0$ that admit flat liftings over the Witt vectors together with additional data (logarithmic structure and the Frobenius morphism) by showing a descending property of such Frobenius liftability. We establish a refined form of the classical result due to Mehta-Srinivas on the existence of canonical liftings. For this purpose, we also establish a result on the algebraization of certain $p$-adic formal schemes.

papers.title: On $z^\circ$-ideals and annihilator ideals
papers.abstract: For $a\in R$, let $P_a$ denote the intersection of all minimal prime ideals of $R$ containing $a$. An ideal $I$ of a ring $R$ is called a $z^{\circ}$-ideal if $P_a\subseteq I$ for all $a\in I$. In this paper, we first investigate the class of $z^{\circ}$-ideals in non-commutative rings. We provide characterizations of $z^{\circ}$-ideals in 2-by-2 generalized triangular matrix rings, full and upper triangular matrix rings, and semiprime rings. Next, we explore new properties of the lattice $rAnn(id(R))$, the set of right annihilator ideals of $R$. We prove that $rAnn(id(R))$ forms an algebraic frame when $R$ is semiprime and a coherent frame when $R$ is a reduced ring. Furthermore, we characterize the smallest (resp., largest) right annihilator ideal containing (resp., contained in) an ideal $I$ of an $SA$-ring $R$.

papers.title: On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations
papers.abstract: The cutoff phenomenon, conceptualized at the origin for finite Markov chains, states that for a parametric family of evolution equations, started from a point, the distance towards a long time equilibrium may become more and more abrupt for certain choices of initial conditions, when the parameter tends to infinity. This threshold phenomenon can be seen as a critical competition between trend to equilibrium and worst initial condition. In this note, we investigate this phenomenon beyond stochastic processes, in the context of the analysis of nonlinear partial differential equations, by proving cutoff for the fast diffusion and porous medium Fokker-Planck equations on the Euclidean space, when the dimension tends to infinity. We formulate the phenomenon using quadratic Wasserstein distance, as well as using specific relative entropy and Fisher information. Our high dimensional asymptotic analysis uses the exact solvability of the model involving Barenblatt profiles. It includes the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics as a special linear case.

papers.title: Optimal regret for dynamic matching with static priorities
papers.abstract: We study centralized two-way dynamic matching markets in which agents arrive stochastically over time and wait in queues associated with their types. We focus on static priority policies that assign each agent type a fixed ranking over its neighbors and make online matching decisions using only queue availability. We propose the General Priority ($\mathbf{GP}$) policy, which builds on the Tree Priority ($\mathbf{TP}$) policy introduced in [KAG25]. Under the general position gap condition, $\mathbf{GP}$ selects matches using a nondegenerate optimal basic solution of the fluid relaxation. It prioritizes children over parents within trees and consistently gives clockwise neighbors priority over counterclockwise neighbors on each cycle. We establish the optimal all-time regret scaling $O(ε^{-1})$ for $\mathbf{GP}$ on general two-way matching networks, where the general position gap $ε$ measures the fluid relaxation's distance from degeneracy. In particular, this resolves the conjecture by [KAG25] on the optimal $ε$-dependence for $\mathbf{TP}$.

papers.title: Asymptotic coefficients of Weil-Petersson volumes in the large genus
papers.abstract: Mirzakhani-Zograf proved the large genus asymptotic expansions of Weil-Petersson volumes and showed that the asymptotic coefficients are polynomials in $\mathbb Q[π^{-2},π^2]$. They also conjectured that these are actually polynomials in $\mathbb Q[π^{-2}]$. In this paper, we prove Mirzakhani-Zograf's conjecture.

papers.title: Simultaneous analysis of approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and mean-field inference
papers.abstract: Approximate Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (ALO-CV) is a method that has been proposed to estimate the generalization error of a regularized estimator in the high-dimensional regime where dimension and sample size are of the same order, the so-called ``proportional regime''. A new analysis is developed to derive the consistency of ALO-CV for non-differentiable regularizers under Gaussian covariates and strong convexity. Using a conditioning argument, the difference between the ALO-CV weights and their counterparts in mean-field inference is shown to be small. Combined with upper bounds between the mean-field inference estimate and the leave-one-out quantity, this provides a proof that ALO-CV approximates the leave-one-out quantity up to negligible error terms. Linear models with square loss, robust linear regression and single-index models are explicitly treated.

papers.title: On cutoff via rigidity for high dimensional curved diffusions
papers.abstract: We consider overdamped Langevin diffusions in Euclidean space, with curvature equal to the spectral gap. This includes the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process as well as non-Gaussian and non-product extensions with convex interaction, such as the Dyson process from random matrix theory. We show that a cutoff phenomenon or abrupt convergence to equilibrium occurs in high dimension, at a critical time equal to the logarithm of the dimension divided by twice the spectral gap. This cutoff holds for Wasserstein distance, total variation, relative entropy, and Fisher information. A key observation is a relation to a spectral rigidity, linked to the presence of a Gaussian factor. A novelty is the extensive usage of functional inequalities, even for short-time regularization, and the reduction to Wasserstein. The proofs are short and conceptual. Since the product condition is satisfied, an Lp cutoff holds for all finite p. We moreover discuss a natural extension to Riemannian manifolds, a link with logarithmic gradient estimates in short-time for the heat kernel, and ask about stability by perturbation. Finally, beyond rigidity but still for diffusions, a discussion around the recent progress on the product condition for non-negatively curved diffusions leads us to introduce a new curvature product condition.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Local and Global Solutions for a Partial Differential-Algebraic Equation of Index One
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use the theory of nonlinear semigroups to establish the existence and uniqueness of both local and global solutions for a partial differential-algebraic equation (PDAE) of index one. This method is applied to a reaction-diffusion system coupled with an elliptic equation in one dimension by transforming the PDAE into a system of linear evolution equations with a Lipschitz-continuous perturbation

papers.title: On the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity of holomorphic foliations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address one of the most basic and fundamental problems in the theory of foliations and ODEs, the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity of a holomorphic foliation. For instance, we prove an adapted version of A'Campo-Lê's Theorem for foliations, i.e., the algebraic multiplicity equal to one is a topological invariant in dimension two. This result is further generalized to higher dimensions under mild conditions; as a consequence, we prove that saddle-nodes are topologically invariant. We prove that the algebraic multiplicity is a topological invariant in several classes of foliations that contain, for instance, the generalized curves and the foliations of second type. Additionally, we address a fundamental result by Rosas-Bazan, which states that the existence of a homeomorphism extending through a neighborhood of the exceptional divisor of the first blow-up implies the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity. We show that the result holds if the homeomorphism extends locally near a singularity, even if it does not extend over the entire divisor.

papers.title: From Cherednik algebras to knot homology via cuspidal D-modules
papers.abstract: We prove a rational generalization of Haiman's master formula, conjectured by Gorsky and Neguţ: the bigraded Frobenius character of the associated graded of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the rational Cherednik algebra at slope $m/n$ can be expressed using the generator of the same slope in the elliptic Hall algebra acting on its polynomial representation. The filtration on $L_{m/n}$ is induced by the Hodge filtration on the cuspidal character $D$-module. As a corollary, we relate the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the torus knot to the sum of hook multiplicity spaces of $L_{m/n}$, proving a conjecture of Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. We further provide a realization of the torus knot homology in terms of explicit coherent sheaves on Hilbert schemes of points in the plane.

papers.title: A systematic approach to Diophantine equations: two thousand solved examples
papers.abstract: Monograph "B. Grechuk, Polynomial Diophantine equations. A systematic approach" suggests solving Diophantine equations systematically in certain order. Many hundreds of the equations are left to the reader. Here, we provide complete solutions to all these equations. The difficulties of solved equations range from elementary to research level. In the last section, we present a summary table of all solved equations ordered by their size, which makes them easy to find. As a result, this document may be used as a database of solved Diophantine equations of small size, to which more difficult equations can be reduced.

papers.title: Rational Cherednik algebras and torus knot Invariants
papers.abstract: The HOMFLY polynomial of the $(m,n)$ torus knot $T_{m,n}$ can be extracted from the doubly graded character of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the type $A_{n-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra as observed by Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. It is furthermore conjectured that one can obtain the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of $T_{m,n}$ by considering a certain filtration on $L_{m/n}$. In this paper, we show that two of the proposed candidates, the algebraic filtration and the inductive filtration, are equal.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean analogue of the space of valuations on convex sets
papers.abstract: In the last two decades a number of structures on the classical space of translation invariant valuations on convex bodies were discovered, e.g. product, convolution, a Fourier type transform. In this paper a non-Archimedean analogue of the space of such (even) valuations with similar structures is constructed. It is shown that, like in the classical case, the new space equipped with either product or convolution satisfies Poincaré duality and hard Lefschetz theorem.

papers.title: The fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra for formal Puiseux series
papers.abstract: The fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra has been established for formal power series solutions of systems of algebraic differential equations. It has been shown that the direct extension to formal Puiseux series solutions fails. In this paper, we overcome this issue by transforming the given differential system and such a generalization is presented. Moreover, we explain why such transformations do not work for generalizing the fundamental theorem to transseries solutions, and show that one inclusion still holds for this case even without using any transformation.

papers.title: Hodge conjecture for projective hypersurface
papers.abstract: We show that a Hodge class of a complex smooth projective hypersurface is an analytic logarithmic De Rham class. On the other hand we show that for a complex smooth projective variety an analytic logarithmic De Rham class of of type $(d,d)$ is the class of codimension $d$ algebraic cycle. We deduce the Hodge conjecture for smooth projective hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Bushnell-Reiner zeta functions over two-dimensional semilocal rings
papers.abstract: Lustig gave an infinite product formula for the zeta function of a commutative two-dimensional regular local ring with finite residue field. We extend this to the noncommutative setting with a method based on filtration by an invertible ideal. One application gives an abstract two-dimensional analogue of Hey's formula. Another application provides effective formulae for zeta functions over Rump's two-dimensional regular semiperfect rings. In the appendices, we supplement these two-dimensional applications with requisite one-dimensional calculations.

papers.title: Globally Optimal Solutions to a Class of Fractional Optimization Problems Based on Proximal Gradient Algorithm
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a category of constrained fractional optimization problems that emerge in various practical applications. The objective function for this category is characterized by the ratio of a numerator and denominator, both being convex, semi-algebraic and differentiable with Lipschitz continuous gradients over the constraint sets. The constrained sets associated with these problems are closed, convex, and semi-algebraic. We propose an efficient algorithm that is inspired by the proximal gradient method, and we provide a thorough convergence analysis. Our algorithm is shown to converge to a critical point without the typical need for a nonnegative numerator, and this critical point becomes a globally optimal solution whenever the numerator is nonpositive at the initial point. Our approach is adaptable to unbounded constraint sets as well. Therefore, our approach is viable for many more practical models. Numerical experiments show that our method not only reliably reaches ground-truth solutions in some model problems but also outperforms several existing methods in maximizing the Sharpe ratio with real-world financial data.

papers.title: Convergence of Quantum Lindstedt Series and Semiclassical Renormalization
papers.abstract: In this work we consider the KAM renormalizability problem for small pseudodifferential perturbations of the semiclassical isochronous transport operator with Diophantine frequencies on the torus. Assuming that the symbol of the perturbation is real analytic and globally bounded, we prove convergence of the quantum Lindstedt series and describe completely the set of semiclassical measures and quantum limits of the renormalized system. Each of these measures is given by symplectic deformation of the Haar measure on an invariant torus for the unperturbed classical system.

papers.title: On the mean square gap between primes
papers.abstract: We prove that the average size of the squares of differences between consecutive primes less than $x$ is $O(x^{0.23+\varepsilon})$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$. This improves on a result of Peck, who gave bound $O(x^{0.25+\varepsilon})$ in the place of $O(x^{0.23+\varepsilon})$. Key ingredients are Harman's sieve, Heath-Brown's mean value theorem for sparse Dirichlet polynomials and Heath-Brown's $R^*$ bound.

papers.title: American Options with Last Exit Times: A Free-Boundary Approach
papers.abstract: We study an optimal stopping problem with a random horizon that is not a stopping time: the last exit time of a geometric Brownian motion from a fixed level $L$. The defaultable American put option serves as the motivating example. Using the theory of enlargements of filtration and the associated Azéma supermartingale, we reduce the problem to a classical optimal stopping problem in a finite time horizon for a Markov process, whose gain function is only upper semi-continuous and has a concave kink at $L$ and a spatial derivative that blows up. These features break the standard free-boundary arguments, including the smooth-fit condition. We describe the continuation and stopping sets according to the position of $L$ relative to $B$, the optimal stopping boundary of the standard American put option. When $B$ lies completely above $L$, the random-horizon problem coincides with the standard American put option pricing problem on the continuation set. When $B$ lies below $L$ for some time interval, the optimal stopping boundary of the random-horizon problem lies below or stays at $L$ until $B$ reaches $L$ and agrees with $B$ when $B$ exceeds $L$. The smooth-fit condition fails at $L$, and we obtain upper and lower bounds for the one-sided derivative of the value function. Under numerically verifiable parameter conditions, we show that the boundary is monotone and continuous, and we derive a nonlinear integral equation and an early-exercise-premium representation with local time terms.

papers.title: Optimal control problems governed by time-fractional diffusion equations with control constraint
papers.abstract: A class of optimal control problems governed by linear fractional diffusion equation with control constraint is considered. We first establish some results on the existence of strong solution to the state equation and the existence of optimal solutions for the optimal control problem. Then we derive first-and second-order optimality conditions for locally optimal solutions to the problem.

papers.title: Arbitrarily Many Primitive Prime Divisors in an Iterate of $x^d+c$
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $R$, let $f_{d,c}(x)=x^d+c\in K[x]$ be a unicritical polynomial of degree $d\ge2$, and let $\varrho_d(n,c)$ denote the number of primitive prime divisors of $f_{d,c}^n(0)$, the $n$-th term of the critical orbit of $f_{d,c}$. We show that $\varrho_d(n,c)$ admits no uniform bound, that is, no bound depending only on $d$ and $n$. More precisely, for all $n\ge1$ and $t\ge1$ there is $c\in R$ for which $f_{d,c}^n(0)$ has at least $t$ primitive prime divisors, and these primes may be prescribed to occur with any given multiplicities. This can be done simultaneously for any finite set of iterates. The construction rests on a density computation. Namely, the set of primes occurring as a primitive prime divisor of $f_{d,c}^n(0)$ for some $c$ has positive density. We compute that density explicitly for $d=2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, under a hypothesis on the Galois group of the associated Gleason polynomial, verified for $n\le16$. As an application, we produce, for every $m\ge1$, a parameter $c\in R$ (in fact, a whole residue class of them), for which the splitting field of $f_{d,c}^m(x)$ has the maximal possible degree over $K$.

papers.title: Kodaira-type Vanishings via Non-abelian Hodge Theory
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use nonabelian Hodge theory to study Kodaira-type vanishings. In particular, we generalize Saito vanishing using mixed twistor $\sD$-modules. We also generalize it to a Kawamata-Viehweg type vanishing using $\Q$-divisors, and prove an effective global generation theorem, as an application. We also prove a relative vanishing for a projective morphism in the mixed twistor $\sD$-module setting.

papers.title: On the Bounds of Stopping and Cycle Numbers in the Collatz Process
papers.abstract: We study the stopping time and cycle structure of the normalized Collatz iteration using a binary sequence formalism. By introducing a recursive rooted sequence tree by Winkler (2017), we establish a bijection between admissible binary sequences and integers $m \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$, showing that every such integer arises uniquely in this construction. Within this framework, we derive sharp lower and upper bounds for the weighted digit-sum $\sum_{i=1}^{r} 3^{r-i} 2^{\mathbf{1}(i)-1}$, namely \[ 3^r - 2^r \;\leq\; \sum_{i=1}^{r} 3^{r-i}\, 2^{\mathbf{1}(i)-1} \;\leq\; r \cdot 3^{r-1}, \] the upper bound being strictly tighter than the bound $s \cdot 3^r$ previously established by Luca (2005). These bounds yield corresponding sharp bounds on any hypothetical cycle number $m_c$, and imply that the ratio $F_q(m)/m$ satisfies \[ 1 - \varepsilon_1 \;<\; \frac{F_q(m)}{m} \;<\; 1 + \varepsilon_2, \] with $F_q(m)/m \to 1$ as $r \to \infty$, while the ratio $3^r/2^s$ approaches but never reaches $1$ for any finite admissible sequence. We further show that the ratio of the maximum to minimum summation satisfies $α(r) \sim r/3$ as $r \to \infty$, providing a theoretical basis for the empirically observed scaling $α\approx \max(r)/3$. Together, these results imply that any nontrivial cycle number, if one exists, must grow without bound and satisfy increasingly stringent arithmetic constraints, consistent with all known computational and theoretical bounds on the Collatz conjecture.

papers.title: On the number of epi-, mono-, and homomorphisms of groups
papers.abstract: It is known that the number of homomorphisms from a group $F$ to a group $G$ is divisible by the greatest common divisor of the order of $G$ and the exponent of $F/[F,F]$. We investigate the number of homomorphisms satisfying some natural conditions such as injectivity or surjectivity. The simplest nontrivial corollary of our results is the following fact: {\it in any finite group, the number of generating pairs $(x,y)$ such that $x^3=1=y^5$, is a multiple of the greatest common divisor of 15 and the order of the group $[G,G]\cdot\{g^{15}\;|\;g\in G\}$.

papers.title: Dimension in Polynomial Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: We study the dimension of the solution set of a variational inequality whose operator is polynomial and whose constraint set is defined by finitely many convex polynomial inequalities and affine equations. Under the Abadie constraint qualification, we bound this dimension from above in terms of the ranks of the Jacobian matrices of the associated Karush--Kuhn--Tucker maps; the bound is attained in nontrivial examples and yields a sufficient condition for finiteness of the solution set. For polynomial complementarity problems, the bound is expressed through principal submatrices of the Jacobian matrix of the operator, and the resulting finiteness criterion extends the classical nondegeneracy condition for linear complementarity problems.

papers.title: Isogenous components of Jacobian surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a genus 2 curve defined over a field $K$, $\mathrm{char}\, K = p \geq 0$, and $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X}, ι)$ its Jacobian, where $ι$ is the principal polarization of $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X})$ attached to $\mathcal{X}$. Assume that $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X})$ is geometrically $(n,n)$-reducible with $E_1$ and $E_2$ its elliptic components. When $K$ is a number field, we count such curves up to geometric isomorphism, among those admitting a model over $K$. For $n=2$ and $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{X}) \cong V_4$ we prove that, for each $N=2,3,5,7$, there are infinitely many curves $\mathcal{X}$ for which $E_1$ and $E_2$ are $N$-isogenous. For $n=2$ and $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{X}) \cong D_4$ the elliptic quotients from the two classes of nonhyperelliptic involutions are always $2$-isogenous, and for each $N=3,5,7$ only finitely many curves have them $N$-isogenous. For $n=3$ there are infinitely many curves with $N$-isogenous elliptic components for each $N=2,3,5$, while for $N=7$ there are only finitely many such curves with a model over $\mathbb{Q}$. Furthermore, we determine the Kummer and the Shioda-Inose surfaces for the above $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X})$ and show how such results in positive characteristic $p>2$ suggest nice applications in cryptography.

papers.title: Twisted Yangians for symmetric pairs of types B, C, D
papers.abstract: We study a class of quantized enveloping algebras, called twisted Yangians, associated with the symmetric pairs of types B, C, D in Cartan's classification. These algebras can be regarded as coideal subalgebras of the extended Yangian for orthogonal or symplectic Lie algebras. They can also be presented as quotients of a reflection algebra by additional symmetry relations. We prove an analogue of the Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt Theorem, determine their centres and also study extended reflection algebras.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of transonic steady nozzle flows
papers.abstract: In the present article, we prove the nonlinear asymptotic stability of stationary solutions to the quasi-one-dimensional barotropic Euler equations in a finite-length nozzle with variable cross-sectional area $A(x)$. We consider all stationary flow configurations arising from subsonic inflow: flows that remain subsonic throughout the nozzle, flows that pass continuously through a sonic state and remain supersonic up to the exit, and flows that subsequently return to the subsonic regime through a stationary shock. We prove that all these stationary solutions are asymptotically stable with respect to sufficiently small perturbations. No smallness restrictions are imposed on the mass flux, the magnitude of $A_x$, or the prescribed exit pressure, provided that the corresponding stationary solution exists. The only geometrical assumptions are that $A_{xx}>0$ at a smooth subsonic--supersonic transition, and $A_x>0$ at a stationary supersonic--subsonic shock. To the best of our knowledge, this gives the first nonlinear asymptotic stability result for a stationary flow passing smoothly from the subsonic to the supersonic regime in a finite-length nozzle. The principal analytical difficulty is the degeneracy of the characteristic structure at the sonic point. We overcome this difficulty by coupling energy structures adapted respectively to the subsonic and supersonic regimes. This coupling provides the dissipation needed to control the smooth sonic transition, and when combined with the dynamics of the shock, yields a unified nonlinear stability framework for smooth and discontinuous transonic nozzle flows.

papers.title: Delta Characters and Ranks of Minimal Subisocrystals of Abelian Schemes
papers.abstract: Using the framework of delta characters on arithmetic jet spaces, we construct a canonical sequence of filtered isocrystals associated to an abelian scheme $A$ of relative dimension $g$ over a $p$-adically complete discrete valuation ring. These isocrystals map injectively via a canonical morphism into the first (rational) crystalline cohomology group $\mathbf{H}^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A)$ of the abelian scheme $A$, directly generalizing a prior construction due to Borger and Saha. Pandit showed that the canonical morphism is a map of isocrystals. This then implies that the image of this canonical embedding coincides with the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ containing the space of invariant differential forms $H^0(A,Ω_A)$. Berthelot and Ogus showed that the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ is $g$ if and only if $A$ has an endomorphism that lifts the absolute Frobenius on the special fiber of $A$. As a primary application, for a general abelian scheme $A$, we show that the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ can be viewed as a module obtained from primitive delta characters of $A$ via appropriate twists by the canonical Frobenius morphism $φ$ induced from the theory of arithmetic jet spaces. As a consequence, we show that the rank of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ depends on numerical invariants arising from the theory of delta characters of $A$. More precisely, the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ is given by the sum of the exact orders of the primitive delta characters associated to the abelian scheme $A$.

papers.title: Extrinsic Curvature Estimation by Closest Point Projection of Rays
papers.abstract: We propose a parametrization-free framework for estimating the second fundamental form and the principal curvatures of a submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The method uses the closest point projections of a few short random rays and recovers the curvature from the curves that these projections induce on the submanifold, without coordinate charts or local fitting. We analyze the geometry of the induced curves and characterize when they are geodesics. For hypersurfaces, these results give two algorithms with error bounds: a least squares reconstruction of the second fundamental form from the curvatures of the induced curves, and a direct estimate of all principal curvatures from the eigenvalues of a $d\times d$ matrix built from $d$ rays, which needs no normal information and costs $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ besides the projections. In higher codimension, we can also recover the second fundamental form one normal direction at a time. On point clouds, where the projection becomes a nearest neighbor query, we bound the additional error. Experiments confirm the predicted rates for hypersurfaces in up to $128$ dimensions, for surfaces of codimension up to $98$, and on point clouds, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework in practice.

papers.title: An optimization-based property-preserving limiter for two-phase flow in porous media on non-matching meshes
papers.abstract: Two-phase flow in porous media arises in a wide range of applications in engineering and science. A fundamental challenge in its numerical simulation is that the approximation of the saturation transport equation can violate the maximum principle, and spurious oscillations can appear even when the solution remains within physical bounds. In this work, we propose a bound-preserving anti-oscillation postprocessing limiter for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of the two-phase flow system on non-matching meshes. An optimization-based cell average limiter enforces the prescribed bounds on the cell averages while preserving global mass by minimizing the $L^2$ distance to the original cell averages. To suppress the remaining oscillations, the cell average limiter is combined with a minmod limiter, which is activated only in the cells identified by a troubled-cell detector to avoid unnecessary loss of accuracy, and a Zhang-Shu scaling limiter subsequently enforces the bounds on point values. In addition, we prove that the cell average limiter preserves the accuracy of the numerical solution at a fixed time on non-matching meshes. Numerical experiments on homogeneous, non-homogeneous, and fractured porous media demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Berezin Transform Commutators
papers.abstract: We study commutators of Berezin transforms $\mathcal B_α$ associated with radial weighted Fock spaces with exponential weights $e^{-α|z|^{m}}$ on the complex plane. We prove that when $m>2$, the commutator $[\mathcal B_α,\mathcal B_β]$ is compact on the space $L^{2}(\mathbb C, dA)$ whenever $α,β>0$. We further show that if $m>2$ and $α\neqβ$, then the commutator is never of finite rank.

papers.title: EnerGNN: Learning Optimization-Compatible Energy Functions for Exact Constrained Combinatorial Inference
papers.abstract: Learning-based approaches to combinatorial optimization often predict solutions directly or use predictions to restrict search, while expressive energy-based models typically rely on approximate inference. We introduce EnerGNN, a framework that learns energy functions over complete binary configurations and minimizes them under explicit hard constraints through mixed integer programming (MIP). EnerGNN combines a graph neural network encoder with an optimization-compatible readout and a nonlinear energy head, enabling exact constrained inference over the learned energy. An optimality-aware contrastive loss trains the energy to reflect solution quality and constraint violations. Across Quadratic Knapsack, Combinatorial Auctions, and a personalized cell therapy supply chain problem, EnerGNN achieves near-optimal solutions with 100% feasibility. On the supply chain problem, it achieves a 0.05% mean primal gap and a 17.4$\times$ speedup over the monolithic MIP. The learned energy also generalizes to larger instances and supports zero-shot constraint injection, adapting to changing constraints without retraining while preserving feasibility.

papers.title: Gravitational Radiation Coupled to a real massive scalar Field
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of small-data global solutions to the Einstein--Klein--Gordon system with a positive-mass real scalar field in wave gauge. We show that the linearized trace component of the metric perturbation admits a $\hat t^{-1}\simeq t^{-1}$ optimal decreasing rate. Moreover, a quantitative one-point observability estimate is established: the initial Klein-Gordon energy is controlled by this leading order coefficient.

papers.title: Optimal Experimental Design for the Polynomial Maximization Method: a Higher-Order Reserve Beyond Second-Order Design Theory
papers.abstract: Optimal designs for regression with asymmetric errors build on the second-order least squares estimator (SLSE) of Wang and Leblanc (2008), whose gain over ordinary least squares (OLS) comes from the error skewness. With i.i.d. errors the optimally weighted SLSE solves the same estimating equation as the degree-two Polynomial Maximization Method (PMM), a family whose degree-$S$ location estimator has asymptotic variance $g_S\le1$ times that of the sample mean. We derive optimal designs for this family when the errors are independent with constant variance but have standardised cumulants of order three and higher that vary with the regressor (cumulant heteroscedasticity). For a known reduction field $g_S(x)$, the $g_S$-weighted information matrix $M_{g_S}$ obeys the Kiefer-Wolfowitz equivalence theorem. A constant field leaves the OLS-optimal design unchanged; a non-constant field can change it but need not. For symmetric errors with varying kurtosis, the PMM$_2$ and conditional-SLSE designs cannot depart from the OLS-optimal one, whereas a degree-three design can. A stratify-and-pool PMM$_S$ estimator attains $N\mathrm{Cov}(\hatθ)\toσ^2M_{g_S}^{-1}$ at every degree as all strata grow; its per-stratum reduction is below one only for symmetric errors with the symmetry imposed. For a quadratic model on $[0,1]$ with symmetric Beta errors of unit variance and dose-varying shape, the third-order design for the known field has $A$-efficiency $1.047$ relative to the OLS-optimal design, and $1.001$ under the $D$-criterion. A two-stage procedure that estimates the field from a one-third pilot builds designs of $A$-efficiency $1.014$-$1.020$ at $N=600$-$2400$; its realised mean-squared-error ratio against the OLS-optimal design ranges from $0.89$ (a loss) to $1.08$.

papers.title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. For the converse, an endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one gives rise to a family of holonomic $A_2$-modules over finite fields. One needs to lift this family to an $A_2$-module in characteristic zero with the prescribed arithmetic support. The existence of such a lift is a special case of Kontsevich's conjecture on holonomic $\mathcal D$-modules with prescribed arithmetic support. We prove that in this special situation such a lift is unique whenever it exists. If these lifts exists for every endomorphism with Jacobian one, then $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ implies $\mathrm{JC}_2$. For every $n\ge 3$, we construct a Lagrangian subvariety of $T^*\mathbb{A}^n$ that provides a counterexample to Kontsevich's conjecture. The counterexamples arise from the graph of a noninvertible symplectic endomorphism of $\mathbb A^4$ constructed by Long. We also present a different strategy for lifting $\mathcal D$-modules associated with a Jacobian-one endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ to characteristic zero via ultraproducts and show that the existence of a characteristic-zero lift in this setting is equivalent to the uniform boundedness of the Berest--Wilson invariants of these $A_2$-modules, regarded as left $A_1$-modules. Finally, we study two other conjectures of Kontsevich on arithmetic support, giving a counterexample to one and partial results on the other.

papers.title: Improved Bounds on Proportional Choice Numbers
papers.abstract: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $χ_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. We consider two previously posed questions regarding proportional choice numbers: (1) Is there a constant $C$ such that $χ_{pc}(P_n) \leq C$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$? and (2) Is it the case that for any graph $G$, $χ_{pc}(G) \leq Δ(G)+1$ where $Δ(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$? In this paper we answer both questions: the first in the affirmative and the second in the negative. Specifically, we prove that $χ_{pc}(G) \leq 2^{χ'(G)}$ for every graph $G$ where $χ'(G)$ is the chromatic index of $G$. Consequently, $χ_{pc}(P_n) \leq 4$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. We also prove that when $G$ is the disjoint union of $(a+b-1)$ copies of $K_{a,b}$, $χ_{pc}(G)=a+b$. In particular, for each $m \in \mathbb{N}$, there is a graph $G$ with $Δ(G)=m$ and $χ_{pc}(G)=2Δ(G)$.

papers.title: Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
papers.abstract: We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$. We then use these matrix representations to construct examples of long-range quantum spin chains from $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for the classical Calogero--Inozemtsev system associated with the ${\rm BC}_n$ root system. We also construct $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero--Moser models in an external field, leading to Haldane--Shastry and Polychronakos--Frahm chains with modified spin positions.

papers.title: Near-boundary asymptotics for profile score statistics
papers.abstract: We establish asymptotic results for profile score statistics under sequences of parameters that may tend to the boundary of the parameter set. When the likelihood is profiled over a set with boundary points, the distribution of the statistic can depend, even asymptotically, on a distance to the boundary that cannot be estimated consistently. We address this in three ways. First, we give conditions under which the nuisance score has a root on an extended parameter set, and the profile score statistic formed with that root converges to a chi-squared distribution. Second, we show that the efficient score statistic converges to a chi-squared distribution under a separate condition that can hold even for estimators constrained to the original set. Both lead to confidence regions with asymptotically correct coverage probability, uniformly on sets that may contain boundary points, and the conditions allow the scores for the interest and nuisance parameters to grow at different rates or become asymptotically collinear. Third, we quantify the coverage error of applying the profile score statistic without an extended set. We approximate the distribution of the statistic and bound the error by a quantity that decays like a normal tail in the standardized distance to the boundary. The approximation also gives one-sided tests with least favorable critical values whose asymptotic size is at most the nominal level. We illustrate the results in a zero-inflated Poisson model and a one-way random effects model.

papers.title: Dynamic Interpolation and Higher-Order Turbulence Scales in 3D Navier-Stokes Flows
papers.abstract: We investigate the three-dimensional unforced Navier-Stokes equations through the interaction between spatial analyticity and the geometric sparseness of regions of intense fluid activity (i.e., regions where the fluid's motion varies sharply). Interpreting higher-order derivative ratios as turbulence scales, we introduce time-weighted bridge inequalities that quantify the relationship between lower- and higher-order derivative norms. The time weights give the derivative ratios greater flexibility while ensuring that the resulting lower bound on the radius of analyticity dominates the sparseness scale of the super-level sets, indicating that the flow has entered the dissipation regime. Combining this scale comparison with a harmonic-measure maximum principle on one-dimensional sparse sets yields a contraction in the relevant derivative norm, thereby excluding a class of strongly turbulent blow-up scenarios. Consequently, the strong solution extends analytically beyond the candidate blow-up time.

papers.title: Minimum-coordinate elimination on a simplex: polynomial first-step safety and coNP-complete correctness
papers.abstract: We study a deletion rule for strictly convex quadratic minimization on a simplex: compute the affine minimizer on the current face, permanently remove a most-negative coordinate, and repeat. Correctness is required for every linear term and every resolution of ties. We characterize first-step safety by a finite maximum principle for the constrained inverse, and correctness from every initial face by principal-inverse row inequalities. Correctness from the full simplex is a different property. The two properties coincide with at most four coordinates, but an explicit rational five-coordinate example separates them. An exact reachability condition explains the separation: boundary equalities in the constrained inverse restrict the tasks that can be entered on a facet. Away from these equalities, full-start and hereditary correctness coincide. We also determine the recognition complexity. First-step safety is decidable in polynomial bit time, by combining classical strict $n$-step-vector recognition with diagonal regularization. In contrast, full-start and hereditary correctness are coNP-complete, even on a reduction family with strict column diagonal maxima on every face. The proofs include the non-strict boundary and all affine anchors; explicit rational certificates for the finite examples are given in the text.

papers.title: On Reed-Muller-Type Codes Associated to Proto-Exact Categories
