papers.title: Fixed-point-free automorphisms of solvable Lie algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of fixed-point-free automorphisms for finite-dimensional Lie algebras. By a result of Jacobson, a Lie algebra admitting a fixed-point-free automorphism is solvable. We prove that such a Lie algebra must be even strongly unimodular. We find a necessary and sufficient criterion such that a complex almost abelian Lie algebra admits a fixed-point-free automorphism. For complex filiform Lie algebras we show that the existence of a fixed-point-free automorphism is equivalent to not being characteristically nilpotent.

papers.title: Thermodynamic formalism for singular flows
papers.abstract: We prove that $C^\infty$ smooth three-dimensional flows with positive topological entropy admit only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy, even in the presence of singularities (zero-velocity points). Furthermore, for flows in a $C^\infty$-open and dense subset of the space of such three-dimensional flows, every ergodic measure of maximal entropy is rapidly mixing. To prove this result, we construct a novel symbolic coding framework for singular flows, which serves as the fundamental technical tool. We then introduce the property of strong positive recurrence (SPR) for singular flows, and prove that SPR flows can be coded by suspension flows over SPR countable discrete symbolic systems. Under appropriate conditions, we further establish that such suspension flows are rapidly mixing. These frameworks can be further generalized to a broad class of flows, including star flows, and the results naturally extend to general equilibrium states.

papers.title: Semi-discrete approximation of Mañé, Aubry and Mather sets
papers.abstract: We study a variational discretization in time of Aubry--Mather theory for Tonelli Lagrangians on the flat torus. We define discrete Mañé, Aubry and Mather sets, establish their compactness and inclusion properties, and investigate their convergence as the time step tends to zero. We prove upper-limit results for the Mañé sets and, when the continuous Aubry set has finitely many static classes, for the Aubry sets. We obtain full Kuratowski and Hausdorff convergence of the Aubry sets when this set is a single equilibrium or periodic orbit, and, under additional assumptions, a finite union of equilibria. Every weak limit of discrete Mather measures is a continuous Mather measure. For equilibrium Aubry sets, we give sufficient conditions for exact preservation of Mather sets and measure families at small time steps. A mechanical example illustrates these results and exhibits exact preservation of the Aubry set as well.

papers.title: On nonnegative solutions of the differential inequality $Δ_pu+ Δ_q u+V(x)u^s\leq 0$ on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with differential inequalities with $(p,q)$-Laplacian operator on Riemannian manifolds. Using a test function argument, we establish Liouville-type theorems under the manifold's geometry and the potential's behavior at infinity. Finally, we give an example showing the sharpness when $V(x)$ is a positive constant.

papers.title: Signless Laplacian spectral radius of simplicial complexes without $r$-dimensional wheels
papers.abstract: An $r$-dimensional wheel is defined as the join of an $(r-2)$-simplex and a cycle. In this paper, we study the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of $n$-vertex $r$-dimensional pure simplicial complexes that contain no $r$-dimensional wheels. For sufficiently large $n$, we determine the extremal complexes that attain this maximum. Our result generalizes the corresponding extremal results of signless Laplacian on graphs and provides a spectral anlogue of a theorem of Brown, Erdős and Sós on the maximum number of facets of simplicial complexes in the case $r=2$.

papers.title: Approximation of structures:local and global
papers.abstract: We provide a mathematically rigorous definition of local approximation and demonstrate its applicability to some interesting classes of structures. In particular, we prove that any compact simple Lie group is locally approximated by finite groups. The definition and main examples are motivated by physics but the techniques are of model theory. Namely, we introduce the ultraproduct of emerging metric structures, which generalises the ultraproduct in metric model theory.

papers.title: Prime Density, Kolmogorov Quotients and Homeomorphisms between Macías Spaces of Integral Domains
papers.abstract: For an integral domain $R$ that is not a field, the Macías space $M(R)$ is the set $R^0=R\setminus\{0\}$ endowed with the topology generated by the subsets $σ_k^0=\{x\in R^0:\langle x\rangle+\langle k\rangle=R\}$ for $k\in R^0$. We show that the unit group is open in $M(R)$ precisely when $R$ is not semiprimitive, and characterize semiprimitive Dedekind domains and unique factorization domains (UFDs) by means of the density of their irreducible and prime elements, respectively. We describe the Kolmogorov quotient of $M(R)$ in terms of the maximal ideals of $R$, and reduce the homeomorphism problem to these quotients and the cardinalities of the fibers of the quotient maps. Consequently, two local domains have homeomorphic Macías spaces if and only if they have the same cardinality. We characterize the pairs of Dedekind domains with homeomorphic Macías spaces in terms of the cardinalities of their unit groups and the relations among the ideal classes of their maximal ideals; in particular, two Dedekind domains with torsion class groups, such as principal ideal domains (PIDs), have homeomorphic Macías spaces if and only if their unit groups have the same cardinality and so do their sets of maximal ideals. This characterization addresses, for countably infinite semiprimitive PIDs, the homeomorphism problem raised by Macías in 2024. Under an additional hypothesis, UFDs admit an analogous characterization in terms of comaximality with prime elements. Finally, for a class of domains of characteristic zero, we characterize additive homeomorphisms between Macías spaces in terms of isomorphisms of the underlying rings, partially answering a problem raised by Macías and Ortiz in 2024.

papers.title: Capillary John ellipsoid theorem with applications to capillary curvature problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply a capillary John ellipsoid theorem for capillary convex bodies in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}}$. This theorem yields a non-collapsing estimate for capillary hypersurfaces, which provides a new approach to obtaining $C^{0}$ estimates for solutions to some capillary curvature problems (including the capillary $L_{p}$ Christoffel-Minkowski problem and the capillary $L_{p}$ curvature problem), based on the corresponding gradient estimates. As an application, we study the capillary $L_{p}$ dual Minkowski problem. A gradient estimate, together with the non-collapsing estimate and a $C^2$ estimate, yields existence for every $1<p<q<\infty$ with positive smooth even data and an acute contact angle. The same estimates also yield the eigenvalue problem for $p=q>1$, with uniqueness up to dilation. We further obtain existence and uniqueness for $p>q$ without an upper restriction on $q$.

papers.title: On Stanley-Reisner Rings with Minimal Betti Numbers
papers.abstract: We study simplicial complexes with a given number of vertices whose Stanley-Reisner ring has the minimal sum of Betti numbers. We prove that every full subcomplex of them is homotopy equivalent either to a point or to a sphere. Moreover, we prove that such kind of simplicial complexes coincide with those having minimal Taylor resolutions.

papers.title: Poly-Bernoulli numbers from shifted log-sine integrals
papers.abstract: In 1999, Arakawa and Kaneko introduced a zeta function connecting multiple zeta values with poly-Bernoulli numbers through its special values. Log-sine integrals are also known to be related to zeta values at positive integers. In this article, we study the values of a shifted log-sine integral at negative integers and establish a connection with anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers. This gives a refinement of Stephan's observation on the central binomial series.

papers.title: On generalized covering radii of binary primitive double-error-correcting BCH codes
papers.abstract: The generalized covering radii (GCR) of linear codes are a fundamental higher-dimensional extension of the classical covering radius. While the second and third GCR of binary primitive double-error-correcting BCH codes, $\text{BCH}(2,m)$, were recently determined, their proofs relied on highly complex combinatorial arguments, and the behavior of the GCR hierarchy for larger orders $k$ has remained largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Generalized Supercode Lemma, which lower-bounds the GCR of a code using the generalized Hamming weights of an appropriate supercode. Applying this lemma, we significantly streamline and simplify the proofs for the known lower bounds of $ρ_2(\text{BCH}(2,m))$ and $ρ_3(\text{BCH}(2,m))$, and we establish a new lower bound for $ρ_4(\text{BCH}(2,m))$. Furthermore, by combining combinatorial arguments with Weil-type exponential sum estimates, we investigate the GCR hierarchy for general $k$, proving that $2k \le ρ_k(\text{BCH}(2,m)) \le 2k+1$ whenever $m$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$.

papers.title: Classification of Smooth Alignable Voss Surfaces
papers.abstract: Alignable nets are grid structures that can collapse to a planar strip. This property simplifies on-site assembly and enables compact transport and storage. These structures are then deployed by a scissor motion at vertices in a desired location. In this article, we classify all non-developable surfaces supporting an alignable net that additionally have the geodesic-conjugate net property, namely, the alignable Voss surfaces. Using the surface elements and adapted frames, we show that these surfaces arise as rotation fields of either helicoidal pseudospherical surfaces or Amsler surfaces, resulting in two distinct classes. The first class consists of helicoidal Voss surfaces. Exploiting this helicoidal structure, we combine a kinematic interpretation with the Bour family to derive explicit immersion formulas depending on the isometric deformation and alignability parameters. Furthermore, we examine several subclasses and an extension of this result in detail. In particular, we study the notable case of infinitely many geodesic-conjugate nets on a helicoid and provide a kinematic explanation for why this phenomenon appears in computations. For the second class, we obtain the classification at the level of the fundamental forms and show that they correspond to certain $3$-parameter families of non-helicoidal intrinsic surfaces of revolution. These families are governed by general Painleve III solutions including both regular and nonregular solutions. Finally, a surprising feature of this class is that its members support geodesic isothermal-conjugate nets absent from Eisenhart's classification of the aforementioned nets, thereby identifying a missing case in that classification.

papers.title: A Recognizable Substitution for the Anti-Penrose Tiling
papers.abstract: We present a substitution on six marked rhombs, called Seabed, with inflation factor $\varphi^3$. We prove that its tiling space is mutually locally derivable with the unmarked Anti-Penrose pentagrid hull. Eleven vertex patches of depth at most four recognize the parent vertices: their acceptance domains coincide with the five internally contracted windows. Matching the fine tiles around each parent rhomb to a replacement patch recovers their markings uniquely. The inverse local maps have a uniform finite radius and extend to all singular limit tilings in the hull. The construction also gives a recognizable parent hierarchy.

papers.title: Mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and their applications to boundedness of operators
papers.abstract: We introduce the mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and obtain their preduals. The boundedness of Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, iterated maximal operator, fractional integral operator, singular integral operator on these spaces is proved. In addition, we give a description of the dual of mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and conclude the reflexivity of these spaces.

papers.title: K-Means as the Zero-Temperature Limit of Normalized RBF Assignments: Rates, Trajectories, and Exact Recovery with Entmax
papers.abstract: K-Means is usually treated as a discrete procedure outside gradient-based learning, whereas normalized radial basis function (RBF) layers are smooth. We make precise the sense in which K-Means is the zero-temperature limit of such a layer. Relaxing the K-Means assignments to the simplex with a Shannon entropy penalty yields the normalized Gaussian RBF responsibilities and a reduced objective $F_σ$ with $0\le J-F_σ\le 2nσ^2\log k$, so $F_σ$ $Γ$-converges to the K-Means distortion $J$. We keep four levels of statement apart. For the objective, minimal values and minimizers converge, and above the critical temperature $σ^2=λ_{\max}$ all centroids at the mean form a strict local minimizer. For optimization, alternating minimization is a preconditioned gradient method on $F_σ$ whose hard limit is Lloyd's algorithm. For one update, under a margin $Δ_{\min}>0$, the soft centroid map approaches Lloyd's at rate $O(e^{-Δ_{\min}/2σ^2})$. For fixed points and trajectories, every nondegenerate Lloyd fixed point has a nearby soft local minimizer, and soft iterates keep Lloyd's partitions while Lloyd's path keeps a margin. With the Tsallis entropy of order 3/2, Entmax-1.5 recovers the hard assignments, the Lloyd update and, along a path with margin, Lloyd's trajectory exactly for $σ\le\sqrt{Δ_{\min}}/2$, a sharp threshold. Experiments on sixteen datasets confirm every bound, rate and threshold, and the trajectory statements at the edge of their hypotheses. As a differentiable K-Means term, $F_σ$ shows the predicted effects: its gradients do not vanish at low temperature, its closed-form centroid update needs no learning rate, a fixed temperature crosses the critical one as representations contract, and soft responsibilities keep a vector-quantized codebook in use.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Regret for KL-Regularized Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.abstract: Recent studies have shown that reinforcement learning with KL-regularized objectives can enjoy faster rates of convergence or logarithmic regret, in contrast to the classical $\sqrt{T}$-type regret in the unregularized setting. However, the statistical efficiency of online learning with respect to KL-regularized objectives remains far from completely characterized, even when specialized to multi-armed bandits (MABs). We address this problem for MABs via a sharp analysis of KL-UCB using a novel peeling argument, which yields a $\tilde{O}(ηK\log^2T)$ upper bound: the first high-probability regret bound with linear dependence on $K$. Here, $T$ is the time horizon, $K$ is the number of arms, $η^{-1}$ is the regularization intensity, and $\tilde{O}$ hides all logarithmic factors except those involving $\log T$. The near-tightness of our analysis is certified by the first non-constant lower bound $Ω(ηK \log T)$, which follows from subtle hard-instance constructions and a tailored decomposition of the Bayes prior. Moreover, in the low-regularization regime (i.e., large $η$), we show that the KL-regularized regret for MABs is $η$-independent and scales as $\tildeΘ(\sqrt{KT})$. Overall, our results provide a thorough understanding of KL-regularized MABs across all regimes of $η$ and yield nearly optimal bounds in terms of $K$, $η$, and $T$.

papers.title: Regulator Constants and Cohomology
papers.abstract: We show how regulator constants of a finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module can be related to $G$-cohomology, where $G$ is a finite group. We then derive consequences of such relation for modules naturally arising in number theory, such as ring of integers and units of number fields, $K$-theory groups of ring of integers and Mordell-Weil groups of elliptic curves.

papers.title: Endpoint variation and jump inequalities for rough singular integrals
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for the variation and jump operators corresponding to the family of truncations of singular integrals with rough kernels. This resolves an open question raised by Jones, Seeger and Wright (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (2008)). Moreover, as an immediate consequence of the variational estimate, we recover the weak type $(1,1)$ boundedness of the maximal truncation operator corresponding to singular integrals with rough kernels.

papers.title: Capillary minimal slicing and scalar curvature rigidity
papers.abstract: We develop minimal slicing via capillary hypersurfaces to understand scalar curvature metric on manifolds bounded below with boundary. In particular, in dimension $4$, we prove following comparison and rigidity statement: given a compact Riemannian $4$-manifold $(M^4,g)$ with a mean convex boundary whose boundary is diffeomorphic to boundary of a connected convex domain in $\mathbb R^4$, if the scalar curvature is non-negative and the scaled mean curvature comparison holds along the boundary, then $M$ is isometric to the Euclidean domain. Moreover, we prove a comparison and rigidity result of manifolds with Listing type scaling invariant scalar and mean curvature comparison : $R g \ge -12 g_{\mathbb{H}^{4}}$ and $\hat{H}^{2} g \ge \hat{H}_{0} g_{\mathbb{H}^{4}}$, where $\hat{H}$ is a shifted mean curvature depending on the scale of manifold. This proves the traced version of Gromov's conjecture on comparison and rigidity of hyperbolic convex domains

papers.title: Integer Cantor Sets: Arithmetic Combinatorial Properties
papers.abstract: Cantor sets of integers have a rich set of arithmetic combinatorial properties. We consider classical Cantor sets, with a base and a fixed set of allowed digits. For such sets, we (a) give examples of such sets that satisfy the intersective property with power savings (b) characterize uniform distribution, (c) establish polynomial mean ergodic theorems and (d) study metric pair correlation of Cantor sets.

papers.title: The Game-Theoretic Katětov Order and Idealised Effective Subtoposes
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the longstanding problem of determining the structure of the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order in the Effective Topos, known to effectively embed the Turing degrees. In a surprising discovery, we show that the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order is in fact tightly controlled by the combinatorics of filters on $ω$, raising deep questions about how combinatorial and computable complexity interact, both within this order and beyond it. To make the connection precise, we introduce a game-theoretic (''gamified'') variant of the Katětov order on filters over $ω$, which turns out to exhibit a striking mix of coarseness and subtlety. For one, it is strictly coarser than the classical Rudin-Keisler order and, when viewed dually on ideals, collapses all MAD families to a single equivalence class. On the other hand, the order also supports a rich internal structure, including an infinite strictly ascending chain of ideal classes, which we identify by way of a new separation technique. From the computability-theoretic perspective, we show that a computable (and extended) variant of the gamified Katětov order is isomorphic to the original $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order. Moreover, our work brings into focus a new degree-spectrum invariant for filters $\mathcal{F}$, $$\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F}):=\{\,[f\colonω\toω] \mid f\leq_{\mathrm{LT}} \mathcal{F} \},$$ which is shown to always determine a proper initial segment of the Turing degrees. Extending this, given any non-principal $Δ^1_1$ filter $\mathcal{F}$, we show that $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F})$ is precisely the class of hyperarithmetic degrees. This significantly generalises previous results obtained by van Oosten \cite{vO14} and Kihara \cite{Kih23}. The proofs draw on ideas from general topology, descriptive set theory, and computability theory.

papers.title: Sinkhorn Distributionally Robust State Estimation via System Level Synthesis
papers.abstract: In state estimation tasks, the usual assumption of an exactly known disturbance distribution is often unrealistic and renders the estimator fragile in practice. The recently emerging Wasserstein distributionally robust state estimation (DRSE) design can partially mitigate this fragility; however, its worst-case distribution is provably discrete, which deviates from the inherent continuity of real-world distributions and results in over-pessimism. In this work, we develop a new Sinkhorn DRSE design within the system level synthesis scheme with the aim of shaping the closed-loop errors under the unknown continuous disturbance distribution. For uncertainty description, we adopt the Sinkhorn ambiguity set that includes an entropic regularizer to penalize non-smooth and discrete distributions within a Wasserstein ball. We present the first result of finite-sample probabilistic guarantee of the Sinkhorn ambiguity set. Then we analyze the limiting properties of our Sinkhorn DRSE design, thereby highlighting its close connection with the generic $\mathcal{H}_2$ design and Wasserstein DRSE. To tackle the min-max optimization problem, we reformulate it as a finite-dimensional convex program through duality theory. By identifying a compact subset of the feasible set guaranteed to enclose the global optimum, we develop a tailored Frank-Wolfe solution algorithm and formally establish its convergence rate. The advantage of Sinkhorn DRSE over existing design schemes is verified through numerical case studies.

papers.title: New upper bounds for the period of a negative orientable sequence
papers.abstract: Negative orientable sequences, i.e. periodic sequences with elements from a finite alphabet of size at least three in which an n-tuple or the negative of its reverse appears at most once in a period of the sequence, were introduced by Alhakim et al. in 2024. The main goal in defining them was as a means of generating orientable sequences, which have automatic position location applications, although they are potentially of interest in their own right. In this paper we develop new upper bounds on the period of negative orientable sequences which, for n>2, are significantly sharper than the previous known bound. The approach used to develop the new bounds involves examining the nodes in the subgraph of the de Bruijn graph corresponding to a negative orientable sequence, and to consider the implications of the fact that the in-degree of every vertex in this subgraph must equal the out-degree. However, despite improving the bounds, a gap remains between the largest known period for a negative orientable sequence and the corresponding bounds for every n>2.

papers.title: Strong existence for SDEs with singular drifts driven by fractional Brownian motion
papers.abstract: Let $B^H$ be a $d$-dimensional fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1/2)$. We prove the existence of a strong solution to $$d X_t=b(t,X_t)d t+d B_t^H, X_0=x_0\in R^d,$$when $b\in L^q([0,T];L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)),2\le p,q<\infty$ and the subcritical Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin condition $\frac1q+\frac{Hd}{p}<1-H$ is satisfied. Thus, within the finite-exponent range $p,q\ge2$, the strong-existence result covers the full subcritical region, including the regime $p<2Hd$, where a uniform strong Novikov condition may fail. The proof is based on a compactness criterion for Wiener functionals. Its main ingredients are an exponentially quantitative derivative estimate for the finite-dimensional densities of fractional Brownian motion, a conditional moment estimate obtained through a martingale representation of fractional Brownian motion, and a frequency-localized truncation of the Cameron--Martin shift. These estimates yield uniform Malliavin--Sobolev bounds for smooth approximations of the equation.

papers.title: The Cofinality of Generating Familes
papers.abstract: The topology of a separable metrizable space $M$ is \emph{generated} by a family $\mathcal{C}$ of its subsets provided that a set $A\subseteq M$ is closed in $M$ if and only if $A\cap C$ is closed in $C$ for each $C\in \mathcal{C}$. The \emph{sequentiality number}, $\mathop{seq}(M)$, and \emph{$k$-ness number}, $\mathop{k}(M)$, of $M$, are the minimum size of a generating family of convergent sequences, respectively compact subsets. Let $\mathfrak{b}$ be the minimum size of an unbounded set in $ω^ω$ with the mod finite order. For a cardinal $κ$, the \emph{covering number}, $\mathop{cov}(κ)$, is the minimum size of a family of countable subsets of $κ$ so that every countable subset of $κ$ is contained in an element of the family. It is shown using the Tukey order on relations that (1) $\mathop{seq}(M)=\mathop{cov}(|M|)\cdot \mathfrak{b}$, unless $M$ is locally small (every point of $M$ has a neighborhood of size strictly less than $|M|$) in which case $\mathop{seq}(M)=\lim_{μ<|M|} \mathop{cov}(μ)\cdot \mathfrak{b}$ and (2) $k(M)$ is in the interval $[kc(M)\cdot\mathfrak{b},\mathop{cov}(kc(M))\cdot \mathfrak{b}]$, where $kc(M)$ is the minimum number of compact sets that cover $M$. Solutions to problems of van Douwen's on the $k$-ness number of analytic and of co-analytic spaces are deduced.

papers.title: Linear systems on blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: Motivated by various equivalent versions of the SHGH conjecture for $\mathbb P^2$ blown up at very general points, we propose a similar conjecture for Hirzebruch surfaces. We prove that this conjecture is true for the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$ blown up at $r\leqslant e+5$ very general points.

papers.title: On isoperimetric local-Bollobás-Thomason inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove the following isoperimetric-type inequality: for every convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and some $σ\subset[n]:=\{1,\dots,n\}$ there exists a suitable Hanner polytope $B_K$ with the same volume as $K$ and such that the volume of each of its orthogonal projections onto every subspace whose basis is formed by the canonical vectors $\{e_i:i\inτ\cup([n]\setminusσ)\}$, for every $τ\subseteqσ$, bounds from below the volume of the corresponding projections of $K$.

papers.title: Translation invariant curvature measures of convex bodies
papers.abstract: In a series of papers, Weil initiated the investigation of translation invariant curvature measures of convex bodies, which include as prime examples Federer's curvature measures. In this paper, we continue this line of research by introducing new tools to study curvature measures. Our main results suggest that the space of curvature measures, which is graded by degree and parity, is highly structured: We conjecture that each graded component has length at most $2$ as a representation of the general linear group, and we prove this in degrees $0$ and $n-2$. Beyond this conjectural picture, our methods yield a characterization of Federer's curvature measures under weaker assumptions.

papers.title: An efficient mixed-integer linear programming formulation for solving influence diagrams
papers.abstract: Influence diagrams represent decision-making problems with interdependencies between random events, decisions, and consequences. Traditionally, they have been solved using tailored algorithms that determine the expected utility-maximizing decision strategy. Towards this end, most recent state-of-the-art solution approaches convert them into mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models that can be solved using off-the-shelf MILP solvers. Computationally, these approaches are most efficient for influence diagrams that represent periodic (or sequential) decision processes, which can be cast as partially observable Markov Decision Processes. However, they are inefficient for problems that lack this periodic structure or whose influence diagrams have large state spaces. The efficient MILP formulation presented in this paper is specifically designed for influence diagrams that are challenging for earlier MILP formulations. Additionally, this formulation can be adapted to optimize conditional value-at-risk and to incorporate chance and logical constraints, thereby retaining the modeling flexibility of MILP-based methods. Finally, computational experiments on a range of problems from the literature are reported to show that the proposed formulation is much more efficient than earlier MILP formulations, particularly in problems which cannot be modeled as partially observable Markov decision processes and which lead to influence diagrams whose decision or chance nodes may have large state spaces.

papers.title: Dynamics of Interfaces in the Two-Dimensional Wave-Pinning Model
papers.abstract: We study the mass-conserved reaction-diffusion system known as the wave-pinning model, which serves as a minimal framework for describing cell polarity. In this model, the interplay between reaction kinetics and slow diffusion forms a sharp interface that partitions the domain into high- and low-concentration regions. We perform a detailed asymptotic analysis and derive higher-order approximation equations governing the motion of this interface. Our results show that on a fast timescale, the interface evolves via propagating front dynamics, whereas on a slow timescale, it evolves as an area-preserving mean curvature flow. Furthermore, using the derived free boundary problem, we demonstrate that on a significantly slower timescale, an interface whose endpoints lie on the domain boundary drifts along the boundary toward regions of higher curvature. In summary, our analysis reveals that the interface dynamics in the wave-pinning model exhibit a hierarchy of three distinct timescales: wave propagation on a fast timescale, curvature-driven area-preserving evolution on a slow timescale, and motion along the boundary on a significantly slower timescale.

papers.title: A modern perspective on Tutte's homotopy theorem
papers.abstract: We begin with a review of Tutte's homotopy theory, which concerns the structure of a certain graph associated to a matroid (together with some extra data). Concretely, Tutte's path theorem asserts that this graph is connected, and his homotopy theorem asserts that every cycle in the graph is a composition of ``elementary cycles'', which come in four different flavors. We present an extended version of the homotopy theorem, in which we give a more refined classification of the different types of elementary cycles. We explain in detail how the path theorem allows one to prove that the foundation of a matroid (in the sense of Baker--Lorscheid) is generated by universal cross-ratios, and how the extended homotopy theorem allows one to classify all algebraic relations between universal cross-ratios. The resulting ``fundamental presentation'' of the foundation was previously established in [Baker--Lorscheid], but the argument here is more self-contained. We then recall a few applications of the fundamental presentation to the representation theory of matroids. Finally, in the most novel but also the most speculative part of the paper, we discuss what a ``higher Tutte homotopy theorem'' might look like, and we present some preliminary computations along these lines. The appendices include modern language translations of Tutte's proofs of the path theorem and the homotopy theorem (the latter is a contribution by Juš Kocutar).

papers.title: High-dimensional normal approximations for sums of Langevin Markov chains
papers.abstract: Consider the well-known Langevin diffusion on $\mathbb{R}^d$ $$\mathrm{d} X_t = -\nabla U(X_t)\,\mathrm{d} t + \sqrt{2}\mathrm{d} B_t, $$ and its Euler-Maruyama discretization given by $$X_{k+1}=X_k-η\nabla U(X_k)+\sqrt{2η}ξ_{k+1},$$ where $η$ is the step size. Under mild conditions, the Langevin diffusion admits $π(\mathrm{d} x)\propto \exp(-U(x))\mathrm{d} x$ as its unique stationary distribution. In this paper, we mainly study the normal approximation of the normalized partial sum $$ W_n = η^{1/2} n^{-1/2} \left( \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} X_i- \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} x\,π(\mathrm{d} x) \right).$$ To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first dimension-explicit convergence rates in high-dimensional settings. Our main tool is a novel upper bound for the 1-Wasserstein distance $W_1(W,γ)$ via the exchange pair approach, where $W$ is any random vector of interest and $γ$ is a $d$-dimensional standard normal random vector.

papers.title: OFF Newton-type Methods for Unconstrained Optimization with Inexact Derivatives
papers.abstract: We study objective-function-free (OFF) Newton-type methods for smooth unconstrained optimization with inexact gradients and Hessians. We propose two methods for first- and second-order stationarity, coupling explicit step-size rules with derivative-accuracy and linear-solver residual conditions to guarantee sufficient decrease without evaluating the objective function. The OFF regularized Newton method finds an $\varepsilon$-first-order stationary point in $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations. Under strong convexity, a local Newton variant converges with \(Q\)-order at least $1+θ$, where \(θ\in (0, 1]\). For second-order stationarity, we combine regularized Newton steps with approximate eigenvectors associated with the minimum eigenvalue. With high probability, the resulting method finds an $(\varepsilon, \sqrt{L_h\varepsilon})$-second-order stationary point in $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ iterations, using a total of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ approximate gradient evaluations and Hessian-vector products. For finite-sum problems, we develop subsampling schemes that yield best-iterate convergence in expectation in the nonconvex first-order setting and local \(R\)-linear convergence with high probability in the strongly convex setting, followed by \(Q\)-order at least \(1+θ\) once full sampling is reached. The subsampled second-order method achieves a high-probability $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-7/2})$ total sample-operation bound, counting component gradient evaluations and component Hessian-vector products.

papers.title: Hilbert's Basis Theorem for generalized nonassociative Ore extensions
papers.abstract: We introduce a broader class of nonassociative Ore extensions that unifies and generalizes several earlier constructions, taking subadditivity of polynomial degree under multiplication as a guiding principle. We prove generalizations of Hilbert's Basis Theorem for this class, showing that left and right Noetherianity follow from corresponding degree-reduction properties. Applications include flipped nonassociative Ore extensions, mutations, cochain twists, and depolarizations of Poisson Ore extensions.

papers.title: On The Motivic Leray-Hirsch Theorem For Pure Tate Fibre Bundles
papers.abstract: We prove a Leray-Hirsch theorem for a smooth proper morphism over a smooth integral base whose generic fibre has a pure Tate motive. We further explore and highlight some key applications of this theorem.

papers.title: Weinstein Handlebodies for the Painlevé Betti Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the generic fibre of the Betti moduli space associated to any of the ten Painlevé equations coincides with the result of attaching Weinstein handles along the Stokes Legendrian, and provide Weinstein handlebody diagrams for each of them in the process. We moreover extend the procedure for obtaining presentations in Gompf normal form of Weinstein manifolds obtained by attaching handles to Legendrian lifts of cooriented curves in surfaces to their unit cotangent bundle to the case where the surface may have nonempty boundary.

papers.title: Star operation, microscopic sets and porous sets
papers.abstract: This paper explores the interplay between star operations, microscopic sets, and porous sets. The study focuses on the Galvin-Mycielski-Solovay theorem, which characterizes strongly measure zero sets and their interactions with meager sets. Results include the investigation of the star operation $\mathcal{F}^*$ and its properties. The paper also examines the relationship between porous sets and microscopic sets. Additionally, the work presents constructions of families $\mathcal{F}$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Z}), \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Z}^ω),$ and $\mathcal{P}(2^ω)$ that satisfy $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}^*$. Theorems and lemmas are provided to establish conditions under which $\mathcal{F}^{**} = \mathcal{F}$ and to analyze the implications of the Borel Conjecture and its dual. The paper concludes with a discussion of microscopic sets and their properties, including their interactions with porous sets and the non-equivalence of certain classes of sets.

papers.title: Eventually periodic resolutions with applications to integral group rings
papers.abstract: We present a general construction of eventually periodic projective resolutions for modules over the quotient of a ring by a regular central element. Our approach combines the iterated mapping cone technique with the higher homotopies of Shamash. The periodic part of each resolution comes from a matrix factorization of the central element. The construction is applied to the integral group rings of quotients of groups of finite cohomological dimension by infinite cyclic central subgroups. We give explicit calculations for several families of groups, including hyperbolic triangle groups and the mapping class group of the plane with four punctures.

papers.title: Cut elimination for the alternation-free modal mu-calculus
papers.abstract: We present a syntactic cut-elimination procedure for the alternation-free fragment of the modal mu-calculus. Cut reduction is carried out within a cyclic proof system, where proofs are finitely branching but may be non-wellfounded. The structure of such proofs is exploited to directly transform a cyclic proof with cuts into a cut-free one, without detouring through other logics or relying on intermediate machinery for regularisation. Novel ingredients include the use of multicuts and results from the theory of well-quasi-orders, the later used in the termination argument.

papers.title: Gamma Convergence and Smooth Exact-segregation Approximation for Partially Segregated Systems
papers.abstract: We study three-component Dirichlet energies subject to the partial segregation constraint \(u_1u_2u_3=0\). Our main result is a smooth approximation theorem on bounded Lipschitz domains in arbitrary dimension. For compatible nonnegative Lipschitz boundary data, every admissible \(H^1\) configuration can be approximated strongly in \(H^1\) by globally Lipschitz maps that are smooth in the interior and preserve both the prescribed boundary trace and the segregation constraint exactly. The construction combines a Lipschitz retraction, variable-radius mollification, and smooth truncation preserving existing zeros, without assumptions on interfaces or junctions. Under the weaker assumption of compatible nonnegative \(H^{1/2}\) boundary data, we establish existence of minimizers and \(Γ\)-convergence in \(L^2\) for the energies with product penalization \(\varepsilon^{-1}\int_Ω(u_1u_2u_3)^2\,dx\). We also identify the exact \(L^2\) distance to the constrained class and construct segregated corrections with controlled Dirichlet energy. The resulting correction estimate has order \(\varepsilon^{1/6}\) for bounded-energy configurations; this exponent is sharp in general and improves to \(o(\varepsilon^{1/6})\) for almost-minimizers.

papers.title: Robust Tangent Space Estimation via Laplacian Eigenvector Gradient Orthogonalization
papers.abstract: Estimating the tangent spaces of a data manifold is a fundamental problem in geometric data analysis. The standard approach, Local Principal Component Analysis (LPCA), struggles in high-noise settings due to a critical trade-off in choosing the neighborhood size. Selecting an optimal size requires prior knowledge of the geometric and noise characteristics of the data that are often unavailable. In this paper, we propose a spectral method, Laplacian Eigenvector Gradient Orthogonalization (LEGO), that utilizes the global structure of the data to guide local tangent space estimation. Instead of relying solely on local neighborhoods, LEGO estimates the tangent space at each data point by orthogonalizing the gradients of low-frequency eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian. We provide two theoretical justifications of our method. First, a differential geometric analysis on the tubular neighborhood of a manifold shows that gradients of the low-frequency Neumann eigenfunctions of the tube align closely with the manifold's tangent bundle, while an eigenfunction with high gradient in directions orthogonal to the manifold lies deeper in the spectrum. Second, a random matrix theoretic analysis also demonstrates that low-frequency eigenvectors are robust to sub-Gaussian noise. These results allow us to derive the asymptotic scaling and stability of the estimated eigenvector gradients. Numerical experiments demonstrate that LEGO yields tangent space estimates that are significantly more robust to noise than those from LPCA, resulting in marked improvements in downstream tasks such as manifold learning, boundary detection, and local intrinsic dimension estimation.

papers.title: Inverse Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of matroids under deletion
papers.abstract: We provide a deletion formula for the inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial and the inverse $Z$-polynomial of a matroid. Our formulas provide analogues to the deletion formulas of Braden--Vysogorets for Kazhdan--Lusztig and $Z$-polynomials. We discuss several consequences, which include closed formulas and recursions for these invariants on uniform matroids, projective geometries, glued cycles, and arbitrary matroids of corank $2$. As a relevant application of our deletion formula, we show the existence of a matroid of rank $19$ which disproves a conjecture of Xie and Zhang concerning a real-rootedness property of inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials.

papers.title: Diffusive Stochastic Master Equation (SME) with dispersive qubit/cavity coupling
papers.abstract: We provide a detailed analysis of the quantum diffusive Stochastic Master Equation~(SME) for qubit/cavity systems with dispersive coupling, incorporating classical input signals and output signals (measurement outcomes via homodyne/heterodyne detection). We show that the dynamics of the qubit/cavity density operator converges exponentially towards a slow invariant manifold. This manifold is parameterized by the density operator of a \emph{fictitious} qubit governed by a quantum SME that incorporates the classical input/output signals while preserving complete positivity and trace. The reduced cavity (resp.\ qubit) operator, obtained by partial trace over the qubit (resp.\ cavity), is then expressed as a time-varying deterministic quantum channel acting on the fictitious-qubit density operator. This formulation avoids the non-Markovian descriptions---with temporarily negative dephasing rates or detection efficiencies exceeding one---that appear in several publications. Extensions are considered in which the qubit is replaced by a qudit dispersively coupled to an arbitrary set of cavity modes driven by collective classical input/output signals.

papers.title: Polynomial Transformations of Jacobi Matrices, Matrix valued Orthogonal polynomials and Random Walks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study matrix valued orthogonal polynomials whose block Jacobi matrix is $Θ(J)$, viewed in blocks of size $m=\degΘ$, where $J$ is a tridiagonal Jacobi matrix and $Θ$ is a scalar polynomial. We identify their matrix measure of orthogonality intrinsically as the push-forward, under $Θ$, of a matrix measure constructed from the original scalar orthogonal polynomials. We formulate reducibility in the push-forward variable and prove that the $2\times2$ Hermite family associated with $Θ(x)=x^2+α_1x$ is irreducible for $α_1\neq0$ and reducible for $α_1=0$. This problem is motivated by random walks with transition matrix $Θ(J)$. For these models, we derive scalar and block Karlin--McGregor representations for the powers of $Θ(J)$. We apply the construction to the mixed one- and two-ball Ehrenfest chain, obtaining explicit spectral measures, spectral multiplicities, and transition formulas, and we conclude with the corresponding $k$-ball and multi-ball extensions.

papers.title: Multiply Robust Conformal Risk Control with Coarsened Data
papers.abstract: Conformal Prediction (CP) provides prediction sets with formal coverage guarantees, but most existing methods assume fully observed training and calibration data. In many applications, however, outcomes, covariates, or both may be missing or coarsened. We develop a general framework for predictive inference with coarsened data by combining semiparametric theory with conformal methods. We introduce two complementary procedures. $(i)$ Robust Split Prediction (RSP) generalizes the doubly robust estimating-equation approach of Yang et al. [2024] beyond the classical missing outcome problem by constructing an efficient influence function based estimating equation and solving its empirical analogue. This yields multiply robust prediction sets under general coarsening patterns. $(ii)$ Robust Split Conformal Prediction (RSCP) instead combines semiparametric theory with conformal risk control. Because efficient influence functions are generally non-monotone in the threshold, we first estimate the target threshold on an independent sample and freeze the threshold-dependent nuisance functions at this preliminary estimate. This restores monotonicity and allows standard conformal risk control arguments to be applied. The resulting coverage guarantees inherit the higher-order mixed-bias structure of the influence function. We develop the theory for classical, multi-stage monotone, and non-monotone missingness and illustrate the performance of the methods through simulations and a longitudinal rheumatoid-arthritis application.

papers.title: The Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $p<1$
papers.abstract: We introduce the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $0<p<1$, thereby extending earlier constructions for $1\leq p\leq \infty$. We then establish various properties of these spaces, including their behavior under complex interpolation and duality, and their invariance under Fourier integral operators. We also obtain Sobolev embeddings, equivalent characterizations, and a molecular decomposition. These spaces are used in the companion article arXiv:2502.02511 to determine the sharp $\mathcal{H}^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ and $\mathrm{bmo}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ regularity of wave equations with rough coefficients.

papers.title: Remarks on Derivations on Maximal Triangular Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: This note concerns bounded derivations on maximal triangular operator algebras on a Hilbert space. Given any bounded derivation $δ$ on a maximal triangular algebra whose invariant lattice is continuous at 1, an operator which is shown to implement $δ$ is constructed explicitly. For a general reducible maximal triangular algebra the same construction yields an operator which is shown to implement any $δ$, if and only if $δ$ obeys an additional triple product rule. This work is based on unpublished parts of the author's dissertation [19] and describes a variant of the proof of a more general result in [21] and is thus in effect a footnote to that work. To the best of the author's knowledge the constructive proof and triple product rule have not appeared elsewhere. The work here is not set in the context of the large body of subsequent research, and no claims are made regarding its relationship to later developments.

papers.title: NP-Completeness and ETH-Based Additive Inapproximability of Deterministic Communication Complexity via Relaxed Interlacing
papers.abstract: How difficult is it to find an efficient communication protocol when the entire truth table of the function is given? We give a unified interlacing proof of NP-completeness for exact optimisation and of hardness of approximation. Assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis, there is a computable, nondecreasing additive error allowance tending to infinity for which approximation is impossible in polynomial time. The proof uses interlacing, which asks the players to solve one problem selected by Alice from a collection of inputs held by Bob. For suitable matrices, a short protocol must reveal enough of Alice's selection to encode a solution to a combinatorial problem. This produces a one-bit communication gap in a polynomial-size matrix and proves exact hardness. Repeating the construction is harder: earlier messages can remove the inputs on which a later lower bound depends. Restriction bounds that survive the construction make the one-bit gain repeatable. A smaller, balanced family of interlaced columns controls the truth-table size. For every fixed number of applications, the construction takes subexponential time in the source length. This rules out every fixed additive error under ETH. A general computability argument then yields the stated unbounded allowance.

papers.title: Semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf II: the Ran space version
papers.abstract: This paper is a sequel to arXiv:2310.0638. Let G be a split reductive group. We define the parabolic semi-infinite category on the Ran version of the affine Grassmanian Gr_{G,Ran}. We study the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf in this category. We provide several descriptions of this object, one as certain colimit, another as an intermediate extension in certain category. We relate the global and local semi-infinite categories of sheaves. We also relate the intersection cohomology sheaf of the Drinfeld compactification of Bun_P with the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf.

papers.title: Comparing the face rings of a boolean complex and its barycentric subdivision
papers.abstract: We consider the relationship between the Stanley--Reisner ring (a.k.a. face ring) of a simplicial or boolean complex $Δ$ and that of its barycentric subdivision. These rings share a distinguished parameter subring. S. Murai asked if they are isomorphic, equivariantly with respect to the automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(Δ)$, as modules over this parameter subring. We show that, in general, the answer is no, but for Cohen--Macaulay complexes in characteristic coprime to $|\operatorname{Aut}(Δ)|$, it is yes, and we give an explicit construction of an isomorphism. To give this construction, we adapt a pair of tools introduced by A. Garsia in 1980. The first one transfers bases from a Stanley--Reisner ring to closely related rings of which it is a Gröbner degeneration, and the second identifies bases to transfer.

papers.title: Extremal Lyapunov exponents in random and simultaneous dynamics
papers.abstract: In this manuscript, we consider finitely many maps, all of which are defined on a compact probability space, with at least one map in the collection having degree strictly bigger than 1. Working with two different, however related, dynamics generated by this setting, we obtain an expression for the extremal Lyapunov exponents, that characterise the instability of typical orbits, as the limit of the averages of the logarithm of the operator norm of linear cocycles of generic orbits. We obtain this as a consequence to the Kingman's ergodic theorem for a subadditive sequence of measurable functions, which naturally generalises the Birkhoff's ergodic theorem, in each of the cases.

papers.title: Hausdorff dimension of the graph of the unweighted error-sum function of continued fractions
papers.abstract: We study the unweighted error-sum function $\mathcal{E}(x) \coloneqq \sum_{n \geq 0} (x - p_n(x)/q_n(x))$, where $p_n(x)/q_n(x)$ denotes the $n$th convergent of the continued fraction expansion of $x \in \mathbb{R}$, and we prove that the graph of $\mathcal{E}$ has Hausdorff dimension $1$. The key ingredient is an exact formula for the oscillation of $\mathcal{E}$ on fundamental intervals, which we obtain in a symbolic space of continued fraction sequences containing non-realizable sequences. Using the same framework, we also give a new derivation of the upper bound $3/2$ of Ridley and Petruska (2000) for the Hausdorff dimension of the graph of the relative error-sum function $P(x) \coloneqq \sum_{n \geq 0} (q_n(x)x - p_n(x))$. Moreover, we present an alternative argument based on Möbius inversion and summation over coprime convergent denominators, and we explain why the square coverings used for $P$ cannot yield an upper bound smaller than $3/2$.

papers.title: Convergence of the Birkhoff spectrum for nonintegrable observables
papers.abstract: We consider interval maps with countably many full branches and observables with polynomial tails. We show that the Birkhoff spectrum is real analytic and that its convergence to the Hausdorff dimension of the repeller is governed by the polynomial tail exponent. This result extends previous work by Arima on more regular observables and demonstrates how the tail behaviour influences the structure of the Birkhoff spectrum. Our proof relies on techniques from thermodynamic formalism and tail estimates for the observable and our applications are to natural observations on Gauss maps, Lüroth transformations as well as to a the first return time for a class of induced Manneville-Pomeau maps.

papers.title: Diophantine Equations over $\mathbb Z$: Universal Bounds and Parallel Formalization
papers.abstract: This paper explores multiple closely related themes: bounding the complexity of Diophantine equations over the integers and developing mathematical proofs in parallel with formal theorem provers. Hilbert's Tenth Problem (H10) asks about the decidability of Diophantine equations and has been answered negatively by Davis, Putnam, Robinson and Matiyasevich. It is natural to ask for which subclasses of Diophantine equations H10 remains undecidable. Such subclasses can be defined in terms of universal pairs: bounds on the number of variables $ν$ and degree $δ$ such that all Diophantine equations can be rewritten in at most this complexity. Our work develops explicit universal pairs $(ν, δ)$ for integer unknowns, focused on reducing the number of unknowns to $ν= 11$. This achieves new bounds that cannot be obtained by naive translations from known results over $\mathbb{N}$. In parallel, we have conducted a formal verification of our results using the proof assistant Isabelle. While formal proof verification has traditionally been applied a posteriori to known results, this project integrates formalization into the discovery and development process. In a final section, we describe key insights gained from this approach and its implications for mathematical practice. Our work contributes both to the study of Diophantine equations and to the broader question of how mathematics is conducted in the 21st century.

papers.title: Uniform ergodicity and spectral gap of importance-tempered MCMC with heavy-tailed targets
papers.abstract: We study the importance-tempered random-walk Metropolis (RWM) algorithm on $\mathbb{R}^d$, which targets the tempered density $π_β(x) \propto π(x)^β$ with $β\in (0,1)$ and corrects for the resulting bias by importance weighting. The dynamics of this sampler can be described by a continuous-time Markov chain whose embedded chain is the tempered RWM. We prove that when the tails of $π$ decay at rate $\|x\|^{-γ}$, this continuous-time chain is uniformly ergodic if and only if $d/γ< β< (γ- 2)/γ$. Further, the global spectral gap of this chain can be controlled via the spectral gap of the chain restricted to a ball with radius growing polynomially in $d$. Our theory and simulation studies show that, with a suitable choice of $β$, importance tempering can substantially reduce sensitivity to initialization and significantly improve efficiency over the standard RWM.

papers.title: Conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states on uniformly hyperbolic sets
papers.abstract: We establish the conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states for Hölder potentials on uniformly hyperbolic sets. While standard stochastic stability characterises measures on attractors, we analyse the statistics of transient dynamics on non-attracting sets by conditioning small random perturbations of the dynamics to not escape from our regions of interest. We prove that as the noise intensity vanishes, the quasi-ergodic measure of the $e^φ$-weighted process generated by $\e$-small random perturbations of the deterministic dynamics converges to the unique equilibrium state associated with the potential $φ- \log \left|\det \left. D T\right|_{E^u}\right|$. The results are obtained via perturbative spectral analysis of transfer operators acting on anisotropic Banach spaces and topological hyperbolic dynamics arguments. Furthermore, we extend this framework globally to Axiom A diffeomorphisms with multiple basic sets using dynamical filtrations. This work provides a rigorous characterisation of natural measures on uniformly hyperbolic repellers, which are fundamental in the context of transient chaos. Our results have been formalised in Lean~4.

papers.title: Singularity of the spectrum of typical minimal smooth area-preserving flows in any genus
papers.abstract: We consider smooth flows preserving a smooth invariant measure, or, equivalently, locally Hamiltonian flows on compact orientable surfaces, and show that almost every such locally Hamiltonian flow with only simple saddles has singular spectrum. Furthermore, we prove that for almost every pair of such flows, the elements of the pair are spectrally disjoint. More generally, the results from which these statements are deduced are singularity of the spectrum and pairwise spectral disjointness for special flows over full measure sets of interval exchange transformations under a roof with symmetric logarithmic singularities. Spectral singularity is proved using a criterion based on tightness of Birkhoff sums with exponential tail decay. The assumptions of the criterion are verified exploiting the cancellations proved by the last author to prove the absence of mixing in this class of flows, by showing that the latter can be combined with rigidity by exploiting the local product structure of Rauzy-Veech induction. Pairwise spectral disjointness then follows by producing mixing times (for the second flow), using a new mechanism for shearing based on what we call resonant rigidity times.

papers.title: A partial result towards the Chowla--Milnor conjecture
papers.abstract: The Chowla--Milnor conjecture predicts the linear independence of certain Hurwitz zeta values. In this paper, we prove that for any fixed integer $k \geqslant 2$, the dimension of the $\mathbb{Q}$-linear span of $ζ(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}ζ(k,1-a/q)$ ($1 \leqslant a < q/2$, $\gcd(a,q)=1$) is at least $(c -o(1)) \cdot \log q$ as the positive integer $q \to +\infty$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. It is well known that $ζ(k,a/q)+(-1)^{k}ζ(k,1-a/q) \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}π^k$, but much less is known previously for $ζ(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}ζ(k,1-a/q)$. Our proof is similar to those of Ball--Rivoal (2001) and Zudilin (2002) concerning the linear independence of Riemann zeta values. However, we use a new type of rational functions to construct linear forms.

papers.title: Ultraproducts of crossed product C*algebras
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between the ultraproduct of a crossed product C*algebra $(A\rtimes_{r}G)^ω$ and the crossed product of an ultraproduct C*algebra $A^ω\rtimes _{r}G$ for a fixed free ultrafilter $ω$ on $\mathbb{N}$.

papers.title: The Schützenberger involution and colored lattice models
papers.abstract: Colored lattice models can be used to describe many different types of special functions of interest in both algebraic combinatorics and representation theory, for example Schur polynomials, nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials, and characters and Whittaker functions for representations of p-adic groups. A notable example is the metaplectic ice model of which there are actually two different variants: a Gamma and a Delta variant. These variants differ in key aspects but surprisingly produce equal partition functions, which are weighted sums over admissible configurations, and this equality is called the Gamma-Delta duality. The duality was used to prove the analytic continuation of certain multiple Dirichlet series and is highly non-trivial, especially since the number of configurations on each side of the equality can differ. In this paper we generalize the Gamma-Delta duality by constructing a new family of solvable, colored lattice models and prove that they are dual to existing lattice models in the literature. Besides the above metaplectic case we also get a new lattice model and Gamma-Delta type duality for (non-metaplectic) Iwahori Whittaker functions together with a crystal limit for Demazure atoms for Cartan type A. The equality of partition functions is shown using Yang-Baxter equations involving both variants of lattice models simultaneously. For the crystal lattice model we show that the duality refines to a weight-respecting bijection of states given by the Schützenberger involution on the associated Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns or semistandard Young tableaux. We also show how the individual steps exchanging two rows in the proof of the duality for the partition functions refines to Berenstein-Kirillov or, equivalently, Bender-Knuth involutions.

papers.title: An Intersection Product for the Polytope Algebra
papers.abstract: We introduce a new multiplication for the polytope algebra, defined via the intersection of polytopes. After establishing the foundational properties of this intersection product, we investigate finite-dimensional subalgebras that arise naturally from this construction. These subalgebras can be regarded as volumetric analogues of the graded Möbius algebra, which appears in the context of the Dowling--Wilson conjecture. We conjecture that they also satisfy the injective hard Lefschetz property and the Hodge--Riemann relations, and we prove these in degree one.

papers.title: How Much Weak Overlap Can Doubly Robust T-Statistics Handle?
papers.abstract: Propensity scores near zero or one can make standard confidence intervals undercover. Econometric theory has targeted the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) under such weak overlap using nonstandard estimators or intervals. Practice has instead favored fixed thresholding rules that restore asymptotic normality by discarding extreme-propensity units for whom treatment may matter most. I show that standard t-tests for the ATE remain valid even when overlap is so weak that every regular estimator has infinite asymptotic variance. The key is to threshold the usual doubly robust estimator aggressively enough to control bias among unthresholded observations, but mildly enough to control bias from thresholding. I provide sufficient conditions for such thresholds to exist, and propose an adaptive rule of thumb to achieve coverage without knowing the weak overlap degree. In a canonical application, fixed trimming excludes 18% of the sample; the adaptive procedure estimates the resulting bias at five percent of the effect.

papers.title: Analysis of On-policy Policy Gradient Methods under the Distribution Mismatch
papers.abstract: Policy gradient methods are among the most successful approaches for solving challenging reinforcement learning problems. Despite their empirical success, many state-of-the-art policy gradient algorithms for discounted problems estimate update directions using a sampling distribution that differs from the discounted state distribution required by the policy gradient theorem. In this work, we analyze the impact of this distribution mismatch on policy gradient methods. Specifically, {for tabular direct and softmax parameterizations, we establish global convergence of objective values under biased updates}. {For tabular softmax policies, we further derive the exact leading-order coefficients of the asymptotic objective errors under biased and normalized exact updates. Their ratio provides an explicit criterion for determining when distribution mismatch accelerates or slows asymptotic convergence.} We then extend the analysis to more general policy parameterizations by deriving explicit bounds on both the state distribution mismatch and the induced normalized policy-gradient mismatch in episodic and continuing MDPs. These mismatches vanish at least linearly as the discount factor approaches one. Under an additional smoothness assumption, we further show that the limit inferior of the squared norm of the normalized exact policy-gradient direction along the biased iterates is bounded by $O((1-γ)^2)$ in both settings. Our results provide theoretical insights into the robustness of policy gradient methods to distribution mismatch and shed light on the gap between their theoretical formulations and practical implementations.

papers.title: Geometrical Proof of Generalized Mirror Transformation for Multi-Point Virtual Strucutre Constants of Projective Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a geometric proof of the generalized mirror transformation for multi-point virtual structure constants of degree k hypersurfaces in CP^{N-1}.

papers.title: On conservative algebras of 2-dimensional Algebras
papers.abstract: In 1990 Kantor introduced the conservative algebra $\mathcal{W}(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. In case $n >1$ the algebra $\mathcal{W}(n)$ does not belong to well known classes of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, Leibniz algebras). We describe $\frac{1}{2}$derivations, local (resp. $2$-local) $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and biderivations of $\mathcal{W}(2)$. We also study similar problems for the algebra $\mathcal{W}_2$ of all commutative algebras on the two-dimensional vector space and the algebra $\mathcal{S}_2$ of all commutative algebras with trace zero multiplication on the two-dimensional space.

papers.title: Approximating Kemeny's constant via spectral sparsification
papers.abstract: Kemeny's constant of a network quantifies the expected time for a random walk to reach a target vertex chosen according to the stationary distribution, independently of the starting vertex. The purpose of this work is twofold. First, we introduce the class of slightly regular networks, whose orthogonal degree vector is an eigenvector of the Laplacian, and derive an exact expression for Kemeny's constant for this class, extending previous results beyond regular networks. Second, we address the efficient approximation of Kemeny's constant using spectral sparsification. We establish multiplicative bounds relating Kemeny's constant of a network to that of any of its spectral sparsifiers, and use these bounds to design an approximation algorithm. While standard exact approaches based on a full spectral decomposition or on the computation of a pseudoinverse have $O(n^3)$ complexity, our method has complexity $O(n^2\log^{1+o(1)}n)$ for fixed approximation parameters, and is therefore nearly quadratic in the number of vertices even for dense networks.

papers.title: The Mathematical Theory of Double Descent as Shrinkage, not Overfitting: Matching Bounds for Path-Regularized Multilayer Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We give a nonasymptotic generalization theory for multilayer fully connected neural networks trained with path regularization, for general Lipschitz losses and without assuming the loss bounded, the architecture sparse, or any width or depth limit. Approximation error is modelled explicitly, and along the way we settle an open problem of E et al. on approximation rates in generalized Barron spaces. We treat the underparameterized and overparameterized regimes separately, which is what allows the resulting curve to be non-monotone in the width. We then prove lower bounds on the error itself, valid at every target and at every local minimizer, and combine them with the upper bounds into a theorem asserting that the error - not merely our bound on it - descends, rises and descends again as the width grows, with a peak exceeding the final plateau by a factor diverging in the sample size. Having both sides of the bound also identifies what drives the ascent, and it is not overfitting: once the regularization exceeds the dual norm of the noise, which the prescribed schedule does at every width, a slow-rate oracle inequality controls the error with no variance term at all. The rise is instead the shrinkage demanded by the regularization that the underparameterized regime requires, and we show it cannot be removed by any width-independent regularization under which the theory's guarantees hold. This mechanism is a property of the estimator analyzed here; we do not claim it accounts for the double descent reported for unregularized training.

papers.title: Strategic timing of arrivals to a queueing system with scheduled customers
papers.abstract: This paper examines a single-server queueing system that serves both scheduled and strategic walk-in customers. The service discipline follows a first-come, first-served policy, with scheduled customers granted non-preemptive priority. Each walk-in customer strategically chooses their arrival time to minimise their expected waiting time, taking into account the reservation schedule and the decisions of other walk-in customers. We derive the Nash equilibrium arrival distribution for walk-in customers. We also study the case where early arrivals are allowed and analyse its impact on equilibrium arrival patterns. By analysing various appointment schedules, we assess their effects on equilibrium arrival behaviour, waiting times, and server idle time. Finally, we compare different scheduling policies and evaluate their impact on overall system performance.

papers.title: Fragility-aware Classification for Risk Characterization and Robust Learning
papers.abstract: Classification models play a central role in data-driven decision-making applications such as medical diagnosis, recommendation systems, and risk assessment. Traditional performance metrics, such as accuracy and AUC, quantify classification errors and pairwise ranking performance but do not account for the magnitude of errors, i.e., the risk of confident misjudgments. This limitation is particularly consequential in safety-critical and cost-sensitive settings, where overconfident errors can lead to severe outcomes. To address this issue, we propose the Fragility Index (FI), a novel performance metric that evaluates classifiers from a risk-averse perspective by capturing the tail risk of confident misjudgments. We formulate FI within a robust satisficing (RS) framework to quantify classifier sensitivity under distributional uncertainty. Building on this, we develop a tractable surrogate-based training framework and establish provable bounds connecting training fragility to ranking-error FI. We further derive tractable reformulations for a broad class of loss functions, including cross-entropy, hinge-type, and Lipschitz losses, and identify specific conditions under which these reformulations are exact. We also introduce an FI-induced regularizer for deep neural networks. Empirical results on real-world medical diagnosis tasks demonstrate that FI complements existing metrics by revealing error tail risk not reflected in accuracy or AUC. FI-based models achieve competitive predictive performance while generally attaining lower FI. In the simulated human--AI diagnostic workflow, they also achieve lower average operational costs than empirical risk minimization.

papers.title: A declarative approach to specifying Paxos using three-valued modal fixpoint logic
papers.abstract: We present Three-valued Fixpoint Quorum Logic, or 3muQL for short; a three-valued modal fixed-point logic designed for declaratively specifying and reasoning about distributed algorithms, such as the Paxos consensus algorithm. Our methodology represents a distributed algorithm as a logical theory, enabling correctness properties to be derived directly within the framework -- or revealing logical errors in the algorithm's design when they exist. 3muQL adopts a declarative approach, specifying the overall logic of computation without prescribing control flow. Notably, message-passing and state-transitions are not explicitly modelled, and notions of 'quorum' are abstracted from concrete thresholds to abstract modal operators. This distinguishes our framework from approaches like TLA+. The logical abstraction emphasises the essence of distributed algorithms, offering a novel perspective on their specification and reasoning. We define the syntax and semantics of 3muQL, explore its theoretical properties, and demonstrate its applicability through a detailed treatment of the Paxos consensus algorithm. By presenting Paxos as a logical theory and deriving its standard correctness properties, we showcase the framework's capacity to handle non-trivial distributed systems. We envision 3muQL as a versatile tool for specifying and reasoning about distributed algorithms. The Paxos example highlights the framework's ability to capture intricate details, offering a new lens through which distributed algorithms can be specified, studied, and checked. The ideas we present are easily implemented, and to demonstrate this we have implemented a freely-available proof-of- concept 3muQL model-checker, as an effective prototyping tool.

papers.title: On the pro-Kummer étale cohomology of $\mathbb B_{\operatorname{dR}}$
papers.abstract: We investigate $p$-adic cohomologies of log rigid analytic varieties over a $p$-adic field. For a log rigid analytic variety $X$ defined over a discretely valued field, we compute the Kummer pro-étale cohomology of $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$ and $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}$. When $X$ is defined over $\mathbb{C}_p$, we introduce a logarithmic ${B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-cohomology theory, serving as a deformation of log de Rham cohomology. Additionally, we establish the log de Rham-étale comparison in this setting and prove the degeneration of both the Hodge-Tate and Hodge-log de Rham spectral sequences when $X$ is proper and log smooth.

papers.title: ItsDEAL: Inexact two-level smoothing descent algorithms for weakly convex optimization
papers.abstract: This paper addresses nonconvex optimization problems via a two-level smoothing framework, where the high-order Moreau envelope (HOME) provides a smooth approximation of weakly convex cost functions. We study the differentiability and weak smoothness of HOME. Building on the inexact two-level smoothing optimization framework (ItsOPT), we propose an inexact two-level smoothing descent algorithm (ItsDEAL) by: (i) approximately solving the proximal subproblem to obtain an inexact first-order oracle for HOME at the lower level; and (ii) applying an inexact first-order method at the upper level. We derive computable sufficient conditions for lower-level inexactness, enabling approximate high-order proximal-points to be certified without access to the exact proximal-point or HOME value. In particular, we study a parameter-free Hölderian inexact gradient method and an inexact descent method with Armijo line search, both exploiting the weak smoothness of HOME. We establish subsequential convergence under mild inexactness assumptions, and global and linear convergence under the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz (KL) property. Preliminary experiments on ridge-regularized hinge-loss classification, a high-dimensional MCP-regularized classification model, and robust matrix completion illustrate the numerical behavior of the proposed methods and the role of the HOME order.

papers.title: The smallest singular value for rectangular random matrices with Lévy entries
papers.abstract: Let $X=(x_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ be a rectangular random matrix with i.i.d. entries (we assume $N/n\to\mathbf{a}>1$), and denote by $σ_{min}(X)$ its smallest singular value. When entries have mean zero and unit second moment, the celebrated work of Bai-Yin and Tikhomirov show that $n^{-\frac{1}{2}}σ_{min}(X)$ converges almost surely to $\sqrt{\mathbf{a}}-1.$ However, little is known when the second moment is infinite. In this work we consider symmetric entry distributions satisfying $\mathbb{P}(|x_{ij}|>t)\asymp t^{-α}$ for some $α\in(0,2)$, and prove that $σ_{min}(X)$ can be determined up to a log factor with high probability: for any $D>0$, with probability at least $1-n^{-D}$ we have $$C_1n^{\frac{1}α}(\log n)^\frac{2(α-2)}α\leq σ_{min}(X)\leq C_2n^{\frac{1}α}(\log n)^\frac{α-2}{2α}$$ for some constants $C_1,C_2>0$. The upper bound was derived in a recent work of Bao, Lee and Xu \cite{bao2024phase2} but the lower bound is new and answers a problem posed in that paper in a weaker form. This appears to be the first determination of $σ_{min}(X)$ in the $α$-stable case with a correct leading order of $n$, as previous anti-concentration arguments only yield lower bound $n^\frac{1}{2}$. The same lower bound holds for $σ_{min}(X+B)$ for any fixed rectangular matrix $B$ with no assumption on its operator norm. The case of diverging aspect ratio is also computed.

papers.title: Relative Trace Formula And Simultaneous Nonvanishing for GL_3 x GL_2 and GL_3 x GL_1 L-functions
papers.abstract: Fix a Dirichlet character $χ$ and a cuspidal GL$(2)$ eigenform $φ$ with relatively prime conductors. Then we show that there are infinitely many cusp forms $π$ on GL$(3)$ such that $L(1/2, π\times χ)$ and $L(1/2, π\times φ)$ are simultaneously non-zero. We achieve this by use of Jacquet's Relative Trace Formula. We derive an expression of the average over the GL$(3)$ cuspidal spectrum as a sum of a non-zero main term and two subsidiary terms which are forced to be zero for large enough level by use of a suitable test function. This modest article is dedicated to the memory of Harish Chandra, on the occasion of his hundredth birthday.

papers.title: Spherical growth of reciprocal classes in the Hecke Groups
papers.abstract: Let $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, $r>2$, and let $Γ_{2r} \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}) \ast (\mathbb{Z}/2r\mathbb{Z})$ be the Hecke group. Let $\mathcal{N}_\ell$ denote the set of conjugacy classes of reciprocal elements with cyclically reduced word length exactly $\ell$ in the standard generating set of $Γ_{2r}$. Let $P(x)$ be the polynomial \[ P(x) = x^{r+1} - 2\sum_{i=1}^{r-1} x^{i} - 1. \] Let $ρ$ be the unique positive root of $P$ and $C$ be a constant depending on $r.$ We prove that, as $\ell \to \infty$, \[|\mathcal{N}_\ell| \sim Cρ^{\left\lfloor \tfrac{\ell+1}{2} \right\rfloor}. \] Our approach exploits the free product structure of $Γ_{2r}$, together with a combinatorial counting function and recurrence relations arising from cyclically reduced representatives. We further show that the asymptotic growth rate of primitive reciprocal conjugacy classes of word length $\ell$ coincides with that of $\mathcal{N}_\ell$. This result extends previous work for odd values of $p$ and provides a uniform asymptotic bound for all Hecke groups.
